Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 CRM.
Experience with NICE telephony and contact centre technology.
Experience in insurance, health benefits, financial services or another regulated service environment.
Experience in a unionized environment.
Experience advancing automation, self-service and AI-enabled operating models.

THE CULTURE

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. We believe that your workplace should empower you to be the best version of yourself. That’s why we provide a place where you can be inspired, challenged, and rewarded.

Where your growth means our growth.
Where your voice is heard and valued.
Where your work has purpose. And purpose matters.

We believe our people are critical to our overall success. Inclusivity makes us a stronger, smarter and more informed organization. Being intentionally inclusive of diverse backgrounds, perspectives and experiences will enhance our company culture to positively impact how we support our communities. A career at GreenShield isn’t just about personal achievements, it's about making a difference together.

Here’s to Better Health for All!

ABOUT US

At Planitar, we build technology that helps people see and understand the world’s spaces more clearly.

We are the creators of iGUIDE, a powerful property technology solution that combines immersive 3D tours, accurate floor plans and reliable spatial data into a single, easy-to-use system. Our cameras and software platform are used by professionals in real estate, insurance, construction and property management to simplify their work and deliver better results.

Planitar recently joined REA Group, one of the world’s leading digital property companies. REA operates Australia’s largest residential and commercial property platforms, including realestate.com.au and has a growing global footprint across Asia and North America. Together, we are shaping the future of property technology, combining Planitar’s deep spatial data expertise with REA’s global scale and innovation engine.

OUR VISION

A connected future where reliable spatial data enables informed decisions across the property lifecycle.

OUR VALUES

Integrity:
We do the right thing even when it’s hard.
Teamwork:
We are one team, on a big mission.
Innovation:
We value creative solutions for emerging opportunities.
Accountability:
We honour our commitments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Planitar is looking for a VP, Finance to lead our finance function through a period of continued growth. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who has operated inside a company with $100M+ in revenue, but who thrives in the scaling-company environment ($50M–$100M).

The ideal candidate is someone comfortable building process and infrastructure rather than simply administering what's already in place. You'll lead a team of 5-8, including a Sr. Manager, Finance and 4-5 Financial Analysts/Billing Specialists, and will be a key partner to the CEO and executive team on financial strategy, M&A, and IFRS based accounting.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Own the finance function end-to-end: financial planning & analysis, accounting operations, billing, treasury, and financial reporting.
Lead and develop a team of 5-8, including direct management of a Sr. Manager, Finance and oversight of 4-5 Financial Analysts/Billing Specialists.
Drive M&A activity, including deal evaluation, due diligence, structuring support, and post-acquisition financial integration across international entities.
Design and implement scalable financial processes and controls appropriate for a company moving towards its next growth stage — replacing manual processes with repeatable, integrated systems.
Lead or support ERP/financial systems implementations (NetSuite experience strongly preferred), improving automation, reporting accuracy, and close efficiency.
Partner with the CEO and executive team on financial strategy, budgeting, forecasting, and both parent and board-level reporting.
Oversee cash flow management, banking relationships, and treasury operations across multiple currencies/jurisdictions as applicable.
Ensure compliance with tax, statutory, and regulatory requirements across all operating geographies.
Build out and mature FP&A capabilities to support data-driven decision-making across the business.
Act as a key advisor to the CEO on capital structure, financing strategy, and long-term financial planning.

QUALIFICATIONS

10+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including prior experience at the VP level.
Direct experience with global M&A; deal evaluation, due diligence, integration, and managing finance across multiple international entities/jurisdictions.
A track record of designing and implementing financial processes and controls, ideally having taken a finance function through a period of scaling.
Experience operating inside a company with $100M+ in revenue, combined with genuine comfort operating in a leaner, faster-moving organization in the $50M range — this is not a "run what already exists" role.
Proven people leadership experience managing teams of 5+ across finance/accounting functions.
NetSuite implementation or optimization experience strongly preferred; broader ERP design & implementation experience considered.
CPA (or equivalent) designation preferred.
Strong communication skills and comfort operating as a direct financial advisor to the CEO/executive team.
Experience in a technology, SaaS, or hardware-adjacent business is an asset given Planitar's product line.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE IN THE FIRST YEAR

Financial processes and controls are meaningfully more scalable and automated than when you started.
The finance team is well-managed, with clear roles, development plans, and reporting cadence.
Any active or upcoming M&A activity is well-supported from a financial diligence and integration standpoint.
Leadership has clearer, faster, and more reliable financial visibility into the business.
Key financial, tax and operational risks are clearly identified, and regularly reported to leadership.
The broader organization understands why a timely, accurate close matters, how their own inputs affect it, and how reliable financial information helps drive key business decisions.
IFRS transition complete with a clean audit opinion and an approved accounting policy manual which is applied across all entities.

PERKS AND BENEFITS

100% employer-paid flexible benefits plan

Comprehensive Health & Dental coverage
Health Spending Account (HSA) or Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA) options
3% DPSP match
Hybrid Work Environment
Professional Development Incentive
Opportunities to grow as we scale
The backing of a global industry leader through REA Group

ACCESSIBILITY, INCLUSION & AI DISCLOSURE

Planitar is committed to a diverse, equitable, inclusive workplace and welcomes applications from all backgrounds. This is a back fill position. We provide accommodation under AODA at any hiring stage upon request.

In line with Ontario law, we use AI only to summarize interview notes, never to screen, assess, or decide on candidates — all decisions are made by our team. Please note this is a new position.

jobs.title: Director, Client Technology Services
jobs.description:
Note:
1 vacancy available. This position is deemed a critical replacement vacancy.

Work Mode:
This is an in-person position that requires on-site work five days per week.

Why this Role is Important

Reporting to the Executive Director, Information Technology Services, the Director, Client Technology Services provides strategic leadership for three integrated, college-wide service domains: End User Support; Digital Learning Spaces and Academic Technology; and Media and Audiovisual Services.

The Director designs and advances modern, efficient, customer-focused service models across the portfolio and develops multiyear strategies and roadmaps for endpoint technologies, bring your own device services, digital learning spaces, academic technology, media and audiovisual services, and related equipment.

The position is accountable for improving the technology experience of students, faculty, employees, and College partners by understanding customer needs, defining clear services and standards, simplifying access to support, and using modern technology and service practices to deliver reliable, accessible, secure, consistent, and financially sustainable experiences across all College locations.

The Director sets direction, designs service models, sponsors modernization, and holds portfolio leaders accountable for results rather than managing routine operational activity. The position works with academic and administrative stakeholders to shape the classroom and workplace technology experience of the future, challenge legacy practices, build organizational capability, improve measurable customer outcomes, and reduce avoidable cost without compromising academic delivery, accessibility, security, or service continuity.

How You’ll Make An Impact

Strategic Service Leadership and Transformation

Sets the strategic direction for the End User Support, Digital Learning Spaces, Academic Technology, and Media and Audiovisual Services domains and leads the transformation of service delivery into integrated, efficient, customer-focused, college-wide service models.
Develops and executes multiyear service, lifecycle, capital, investment, and modernization roadmaps aligned with College strategy and academic, administrative, accessibility, cybersecurity, sustainability, and continuity requirements.
Establishes College wide standards for end user devices, learning spaces, computer labs, specialized academic environments, audiovisual systems, media equipment, and related services.
Prioritizes investments using equipment age, condition, utilization, service performance, academic impact, accessibility, security, supportability, risk, and total cost of ownership.
Reduces unnecessary technology variants and inconsistent configurations; improves remote monitoring, deployment, maintenance, support, inventory management, and asset utilization; and recommends action on obsolete, unsupported, underused, duplicative, or disproportionately expensive technology.
Pilots and evaluates emerging technologies before broader adoption and ensures new solutions can be supported sustainably throughout their lifecycle.
Coordinates technology requirements for construction, renovation, capital renewal, and learning space projects and oversees concurrent projects within approved scope, priorities, budgets, standards, and governance.
Establishes structured and continuing relationships with academic and administrative leaders and consults faculty, students, employees, and service partners to identify needs, service gaps, risks, and changing expectations.
Develops service and technology roadmaps collaboratively, translates teaching, learning, operational, and institutional needs into investment priorities, and communicates standards, constraints, risks, costs, tradeoffs, and implementation plans.
Creates effective feedback mechanisms, demonstrates how feedback influences decisions, builds trust through transparency and follow-through, and represents the portfolio on institutional committees, capital initiatives, academic planning activities, and major College projects.

Portfolio Leadership and Stewardship

Defines services, service owners, service standards, performance measures, support models, and escalation paths and maintains a coherent service catalogue across the three service domains.
Ensures consistent service quality across locations and improves intake, prioritization, triage, resolution, communication, knowledge management, problem management, automation, self-service, remote support, standardization, and proactive service practices.
Uses data to identify recurring technology issues, demand patterns, service gaps, and improvement opportunities and maintains service continuity, emergency response, and operational readiness for critical academic and administrative periods.
Assesses organizational structures, job functions, capabilities, reporting relationships, and resource allocations against college priorities and service requirements and moves historically or location-assigned work toward clearly owned College-wide service models.
Clarifies service ownership, decision rights, escalation paths, accountabilities, and expected outcomes and identifies duplication, fragmented responsibilities, capability gaps, excessive specialization, unclear career paths, and key person dependencies.
Leads and develops a large, diverse technical and service organization; establishes clear goals, accountabilities, decision rights, and performance expectations; builds shared standards across historically independent teams; and develops leadership capability among managers, coordinators, senior technical staff, technologists, and other service leads.
Supports employee development, cross-training, internal mobility, succession, and leadership development; addresses capability and performance gaps fairly and consistently; and leads change with transparency, respect, employee engagement, and regard for collective agreements and College policies.
Develops and manages operational, capital, staffing, asset, contract, and vendor budgets and delivers sustainable efficiencies through standardization, consolidation, automation, demand management, contract optimization, improved utilization, and lifecycle planning without compromising service quality or institutional priorities.
Establishes a cost-of-service delivery model by academic program, service, technology environment, or other appropriate institutional cost unit, in consultation with the Executive Director, Finance, and academic leadership. Identifies direct and indirect costs, practical allocation methods, cost drivers, demand, utilization, support intensity, lifecycle obligations, and the cost and service implications of alternative delivery models.
Uses cost information to support planning, prioritization, investment, standardization, and service design and presents it with context so specialized or strategically important programs are not treated as inefficient solely because they cost more to support. The Director provides information and recommendations and does not independently determine academic program viability, academic resource allocation, or program closure.
Establishes and reports a balanced performance framework covering service reliability, responsiveness, resolution, experience, lifecycle risk, modernization delivery, financial and cost of service performance, savings and benefits, vendor performance, workforce capability, accessibility, security, compliance, and continuity. Uses measures to improve decisions and services rather than report activity alone.

Performs Other Related Duties As Assigned

What You’ll Bring

4-year degree in information technology, business, education technology, or a related discipline
Minimum 9 years’ progressively responsible leadership experience in a large, complex, service focused organization where service quality, customer experience, reliability, responsiveness, and measurable improvement are core operating expectations
An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered
Experience leading a multiservice technology environment is required
Demonstrated experience in IT service management; service design and customer experience improvement; organizational transformation and operating model redesign; engagement with senior academic and administrative leaders; workforce planning and organizational development; financial, capital, asset, contract, and vendor management; lifecycle and modernization planning; performance measurement; and leading change in a unionized or comparably complex environment
Knowledge of service management, customer experience, organizational design, workforce planning, financial management, procurement, contract and vendor management, lifecycle planning, accessibility, cybersecurity, project and change management, and the technology requirements of teaching and learning environments
Demonstrated ability to communicate complex service, risk, cost, and investment matters clearly to senior academic and administrative leaders
In-depth knowledge of complex, multiservice technology environments, including end-user support, digital learning spaces and academic technology, media and audiovisual services, service measurement, equipment lifecycle management, and sustainable operating models
Current ITIL certification at the Foundation level or higher is preferred
An equivalent recognized IT service management certification or substantial practical experience applying ITIL based service management practices would also be considered an asset

What This Opportunity Offers

Comprehensive Pension & Benefits: Join a defined-benefit pension plan (through the CAAT Pension Plan) that delivers predictable lifetime retirement income, plus dental, disability, travel insurance and extended health coverage.
Vacation: Enjoy paid time off and benefit from a scheduled holiday closure that offers additional rest and time with family during the winter season
Tuition & Professional Development: Continue your learning journey — eligible employees and their dependents can take select Fanshawe programs or courses at a reduced cost
Inclusive, Meaningful Campus environment: Work alongside passionate colleagues in an inclusive culture that values diversity, drives student success, and connects you to the local community and campus life.

Ready to Apply?

If you're a strategic technology leader with a passion for delivering exceptional customer experiences, modernizing services, and empowering teaching, learning, and workplace technology, we encourage you to apply. Join us in shaping the future of technology services and making a lasting impact across the College community.

Fanshawe College uses Workday to manage recruitment and hiring processes.

Educational Credentials

While transcripts are not required for the interview, they are mandatory as a condition of employment.

Equity, Diversity and Inclusion

Fanshawe College is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equity, value diversity, and welcome applicants from diverse backgrounds.

Accommodation

Fanshawe College provides accommodations to job applicants with disabilities throughout the hiring process. If a job applicant requires an accommodation during the application process or through the selection process, the hiring manager and the recruiter leading the recruitment will work with the applicant to meet the job applicant’s accommodation needs. Accommodation requests per the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act can be emailed to: askhr@fanshawec.ca

Land Acknowledgement

Fanshawe College would like to acknowledge and honour the Anishinaabe, Lotinuhsyuní and Lenape people of southwestern Ontario as the traditional owners and custodians of the lands and waterways where Fanshawe College is located.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those chosen for an interview will be contacted.

jobs.title: Head of Financial Reporting
jobs.description:
Some reporting roles ask you to maintain what already exists. This one asks you to transform it.

Reporting to the VP Finance, this opportunity is for a financial reporting leader who wants more than a steady-state mandate. The role offers meaningful autonomy to bring structure, discipline and momentum to a Finance function in transformation, while strengthening public company reporting and elevating technical accounting capability.

The successful candidate will bring experience from strong reporting environments and the confidence to apply that perspective in a setting where processes, standards and team capability can still be shaped. For a leader energized by complexity, this is an opportunity to build something better and create lasting impact.

The Opportunity

A mandate for a financial reporting leader who wants to combine public company rigor, technical accounting depth, process improvement and people leadership. This is an opportunity to shape how the function operates, develop the team and create the structure needed for a more confident, scalable and effective Finance organization.

What You'll Own

Lead quarterly and annual public company reporting: external financial statements, disclosures, and review processes under IFRS.
Act as technical accounting advisor for the Finance organization — interpreting, documenting, and applying IFRS guidance with practical judgment, including potential US GAAP considerations.
Prepare and review technical accounting memos on complex, judgmental matters (goodwill, impairment, significant estimates) for auditors and senior stakeholders.
Support accounting for M&A, integration, and divestiture activity as it arises.
Partner directly with external auditors, ensuring issues are well-prepared, well-documented, and resolved credibly.
Drive continuous improvement in reporting processes, controls, documentation, and review standards.
Lead, coach, and grow a team — including a planned Senior Manager, Technical Accounting hire.
Build trusted relationships across Finance, Tax, and senior/C-suite stakeholders.

What You Bring

CPA/CA designation, ideally grounded in public accounting.
Progressive public company financial reporting experience — you've owned a reporting process end to end.
Strong IFRS technical accounting and public company reporting experience, including confidence supporting a potential US GAAP conversion
Demonstrated technical accounting depth: writing/reviewing memos on complex, non-routine matters.
M&A-related accounting exposure is a strong asset.
A track record of process improvement in environments still being built or refined.
Proven people leadership — coaching, performance management, development.
Comfort with ambiguity, fast pace, and change.

How You Lead

You own the details without losing the bigger picture.
You bring strong reporting discipline and technical judgment, while staying pragmatic and business-minded.
You hold an uncompromising standard for quality — and get there without friction.
You're proactive and resourceful, comfortable engaging unfamiliar stakeholders to move work forward.
You communicate clearly and build trust without an aggressive style.
You develop people deliberately and address performance directly, constructively, and fairly.
You bring credibility and maturity to conversations with senior leaders, auditors, and the C-suite.

If you are a public company financial reporting leader who wants more than a steady-state mandate, this is an opportunity to build, improve and shape a function with meaningful autonomy, visibility and impact.

Don't wait and apply in confidence.

EFESO Management Consultants is a global leader in operations strategy and performance improvement. We work closely with clients across a broad range of industries to deliver measurable results tailored to their unique needs. Our end-to-end services integrate industrial AI, digital solutions, sustainability, people development, transactions and turnaround, R&D and product profitability, cost and value engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and supply chain transformation.
We drive transformation through 1,500 projects annually in over 75 countries. Powered by deep industry expertise and a commitment to lasting impact, EFESO partners with global enterprises, middle-market companies, and private equity firms to build resilient, high-performing organizations.
EFESO Americas operates across the United States, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil, combining global expertise with local execution to help clients achieve sustainable operational and financial results.
EFESO. Real Results, Together.

Experience Aviva

Together, we are Aviva.

Our values of Care, Commitment, Community, and Confidence guide how we show up for each other and our customers. At Aviva Canada, we put people first through a culture built on inclusion, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

The Opportunity

The SVP, Enterprise Risk Management is a key member of the Aviva Canada Senior Risk Leadership Team, responsible for providing enterprise-wide leadership across risk business partnering, quantitative risk, insurance and financial risk, capital, model risk, and risk analytics. The role supports the effective performance of Aviva Canada by overseeing the implementation of the Risk Management Framework, providing independent oversight and challenge to the first line, and ensuring the organization operates within its Board-approved risk appetite.

Working closely with the Chief Risk Officer, Executive Committee, and business leaders, the SVP delivers commercially focused risk insight and independent challenge on strategic and business decisions. The role acts as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders, ensuring robust governance, effective risk management, and a strong risk culture that support Aviva Canada's strategic objectives, regulatory obligations, and long-term resilience.

What You'll Do

In this role, you will be accountable for the following key areas:

Enterprise Risk Leadership and Strategy

Partner with the ACAN CRO to shape and execute Aviva Canada's risk strategy and ensure the effective operation of the Risk Management Framework.
Provide independent, commercially focused risk insight and challenge to support strategic decision-making, growth objectives, and long-term value creation.
Ensure the organization operates within Board-approved risk appetite and maintains effective risk governance, oversight, and risk culture.
Support Executive Committee, Board Risk Committee, and ACAN Board reporting on key risk exposures, emerging risks, and risk management effectiveness.

Risk Oversight and Independent Challenge

Lead independent oversight of Aviva Canada's aggregate risk profile, including insurance, financial, capital, model, technology, data, change, and operational risks.
Provide effective review and challenge of business plans, capital deployment decisions, reinsurance strategies, material transactions, product development, pricing, and other significant business initiatives.
Monitor emerging risks and material changes in risk exposure, ensuring appropriate mitigation strategies are identified and executed.
Escalate significant risk issues and risk appetite breaches, providing clear recommendations for remediation and management action.

Quantitative, Capital and Model Risk Management

Provide enterprise leadership for insurance risk, financial risk, capital risk, risk modelling and risk analytics.
Accountable for overseeing Internal Model Independent Validation (IMIV) and material model governance across Aviva Canada.
Oversee independent validation activities and provide challenge on capital adequacy, economic capital, liquidity, financial resilience, and risk-return optimization.
Drive the evolution of quantitative risk capabilities and risk analytics to enhance business decision making and risk insights.

Business Partnering and Stakeholder Management

Lead the Risk Business Partnering team, ensuring Risk is a trusted advisor and constructive challenger to business leaders across Aviva Canada.
Build strong relationships with EC, regulators, Board members, Group Risk teams, and external stakeholders
Represent Risk on key governance committees, industry forums, and global initiatives, promoting effective risk management practices and influencing outcomes.
Foster a culture of transparency, collaboration, and proactive risk management across the organization.

People Leadership and Functional Excellence

Lead and develop a high-performing team across Risk Business Partnering and Quantitative Risk.
Establish clear priorities, performance expectations, and accountability for delivery of high-quality risk outcomes.
Build organizational capability in risk management, business partnering, analytics, and technical risk disciplines.
Promote a culture of continuous improvement, talent development, and succession planning while ensuring Risk operates as a cohesive and high-performing function.

What You'll Bring

Bachelor’s degree and relevant professional designation (e.g., FCAS, FCIA, FSA, CRM) or equivalent combination of education and experience.
15+ years of progressive risk leadership experience within the insurance and/or broader financial services industry.
Deep expertise in Enterprise Risk Management, including risk governance, risk appetite, risk culture, ORSA, stress testing, capital management, and regulatory compliance.
Strong understanding of insurance risks, including underwriting, pricing, claims, reserving, reinsurance, investments, and emerging risks.
Experience engaging with Boards, Board Risk Committees, and regulators (OSFI and/or equivalent regulatory bodies).
Proven ability to develop and execute risk strategies that support business objectives, customer outcomes, and sustainable growth.
Exceptional leadership and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build high-performing teams and influence executives, regulators, and cross-functional partners.
Strong strategic, analytical, and communication capabilities, including the ability to translate complex risk, actuarial, and financial information into clear business insights and drive organizational change.

Comprehensive pension and retirement savings programs.
Flexible hybrid work model.

Professional development and executive leadership growth opportunities.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About Vitacore Industries

Vitacore was established on the conviction that Canada should have the domestic capability to produce critical healthcare products. The company became the first Canadian manufacturer of N95 respirators authorized by Health Canada, manufacturing locally in Burnaby from raw materials. Today, Vitacore generates approximately $10 million in revenue, with a product portfolio that includes surgical masks, respirators, related PPE, and Planet Impact, its program focused on recycling hard-to-recycle materials.

Vitacore is a founder-led organization characterized by speed, entrepreneurial judgment, and a disciplined appetite for growth. Mikhail Moore has built the company by identifying opportunities early and moving decisively. As the business enters its next phase, it requires a senior finance leader who can bring greater financial discipline, strategic insight, and scalable infrastructure while preserving the pace and commercial agility that have defined its success.

Download Full Job Description: Vitacore CFO - Position Profile.pdf

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is Vitacore’s first Chief Financial Officer appointment and a critical executive leadership role for the company’s next stage of scale. Reporting directly to the President, the CFO will serve as a strategic partner to ownership and leadership, establishing the financial architecture, governance discipline, capital strategy, and performance management framework required to support sustained growth. Priorities may include new markets, product expansion, strategic partnerships, government and institutional contracts, and potential external capital.

The role requires a CFO-calibre finance executive who can operate as both strategist and operator in a growing, founder-led business. The successful candidate will bring executive presence, commercial judgment, capital markets fluency, and the ability to influence enterprise decisions with confidence and credibility. Their mandate will extend beyond finance operations to include value creation, risk management, governance, capital allocation, and long-term enterprise planning.

FIRST-YEAR PRIORITIES

Required

Within the first year, the CFO will be expected to establish the financial leadership platform required for Vitacore’s next stage of growth, with measurable progress against the following priorities:

Implement a monthly close and reporting cadence that delivers accurate financial statements and executive reporting within an agreed timeline each month.
Develop a rolling 13-week cash flow forecast and 12-month financial outlook that provide clear visibility into liquidity, working capital, and capital requirements.
Establish a reliable product costing model and margin reporting framework covering key product lines, raw materials, labour, overhead, yield, and inventory movements.
Create an executive KPI dashboard that tracks revenue, gross margin, cash conversion, inventory turns, working capital, production efficiency, and capacity utilization.
Complete an assessment of accounting systems, ERP capability, internal controls, and finance team capacity, and present a prioritized roadmap for scalable infrastructure.
Prepare the company for future financing or strategic capital conversations by developing an investment narrative, integrated financial model, lender/investor materials, and data room readiness plan.
Build a practical finance team structure and development plan, including clear accountabilities, decision rights, and recruitment priorities to support the company’s growth agenda.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Partnership with the President

Serve as the President’s principal financial and strategic advisor, bringing CFO-level judgment to enterprise priorities, capital allocation, risk assessment, and growth decisions.
Lead enterprise planning and build integrated financial models that support growth initiatives, including new product launches, market expansion into the US and beyond, and investment decisions.
Evaluate strategic partnerships, joint ventures, licensing arrangements, and potential acquisitions, presenting clear, evidence-based recommendations to leadership.
Bring a commercial point of view to pricing, margin, and deal structure, especially on large institutional and government tenders.
Act as a credible financial voice with the board, shareholders, lenders, investors, and external advisors as the company matures and its stakeholder environment becomes more complex.

Capital Strategy, Banking & Investor Relations

Lead the company’s capital strategy, including banking relationships, lender negotiations, credit facilities, working capital planning, and financing structures aligned to the company’s growth ambitions.
Lead any future capital raise or strategic financing process, including the investment narrative, financial model, diligence materials, stakeholder communication, and data room readiness.
Identify and secure government funding, grants, tax credits (including SR&ED), and other non-dilutive capital available to Canadian manufacturers.
Maintain disciplined cash flow management and rolling forecasts that provide leadership with timely visibility into financial risks, opportunities, and capital requirements.

Financial Leadership, Operations & Reporting

Lead month-end and year-end close, and deliver accurate, timely financial statements.
Establish an annual planning, budgeting, forecasting, and performance management cadence that enables disciplined executive decision-making.
Establish a management reporting package with meaningful manufacturing KPIs, including gross margin by product, unit economics, inventory turns, working capital, and capacity utilization.
Oversee accounts payable, receivable, payroll, and treasury, and tighten controls as volume grows.
Coordinate the annual audit or review with external accountants.

Manufacturing Finance & Cost Management

Build a clear, reliable product costing model covering raw materials, labour, overhead, and yield.
Partner with operations on procurement, inventory planning, and capital equipment decisions, with the return on each investment clearly understood.
Identify and advance margin improvement opportunities across procurement, supply chain, production, and inventory management.
Manage foreign exchange and commodity exposure tied to raw materials and export sales.

Tax, Compliance & Risk

Oversee corporate tax, GST/HST/PST, and cross-border tax matters as the company sells into new jurisdictions.
Keep the company compliant with lender covenants, contract obligations, and financial reporting requirements.
Build out risk management, insurance, and internal controls appropriate for a company of Vitacore’s size and ambition.

Systems & Team

Assess current accounting and ERP systems and lead upgrades that give the business better, faster information.
Hire, develop, and lead a small, capable finance team, and build it thoughtfully as the company grows.
Implement practical, scalable processes that strengthen cross-functional accountability and support disciplined execution across the business.

What You Bring

15+ years of progressive finance leadership experience, including senior accountability as a CFO, VP Finance, Head of Finance, or finance executive with enterprise-wide responsibility.
CPA designation (CPA, CA, CMA, or CGA).
Experience in manufacturing, distribution, medical devices, or another product-based environment, with strong command of costing, inventory, and operational finance.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
**English below**

QUI NOUS SOMMES

Daily tous les jours est un studio d'art et de design de renommée internationale, qui dirige un nouveau champ de pratique alliant l'art interactif, la narration, la performance et le design urbain pour réinventer le vivre ensemble au 21e siècle. Avec l’espace public que l’on partage tous les jours comme terrain de jeu, le studio explore les dynamiques de coopération entre les individus, en proposant de nouveaux modèles de vivre ensemble.

L’OPPORTUNITÉ

Nous concevons la prochaine génération de nos œuvres interactives : des expériences brevetables, entièrement autonomes, sans fil et alimentées à l’énergie solaire. Nous nous appuyons sur nos 15 ans d’expérience pour imaginer à quoi ressembleront les 15 prochaines années.
Il s’agit d’un véritable défi de R&D : nœuds multimedia embarqués distribués (distributed embedded nodes), synchronisation sans fil, autonomie énergétique en extérieur et plateforme logicielle permettant de mettre à jour et surveiller les contenus à distance. Nous recherchons un·e directeur·trice des technologies (CTO) capable de porter la vision technique de cette plateforme et d’encadrer l’équipe qui la concrétisera. Une personne tout aussi à l’aise pour lire un schéma électronique, réviser une architecture de micrologiciel (firmware), spécifier une capacité solaire, collaborer avec des designers industriels et présenter une feuille de route produit.

VOTRE RÔLE

Définir et prendre en charge l’architecture technique de nouvelles plateformes : matériel embarqué (embedded hardware), micrologiciel, réseaux sans fil, gestion de l’énergie et plateforme logicielle à distance.
Monter et diriger une équipe d’ingénierie agile, en commençant par un·e développeur·se de micrologiciel embarqué et un·e directeur·trice de produit, puis en l’élargissant avec des ingénieur·e·s matériel et logiciel dédié·e·s.
Piloter le cycle complet de R&D, de la preuve de concept jusqu’à la conception pour la fabrication (DFM), en passant par les phases alpha et les pilotes sur le terrain.
Définir et protéger la propriété intellectuelle.
Agir à titre d'interlocuteur·trice technique principal·e auprès des partenaires externes, des conseiller·ère·s, des organismes subventionnaires (PARI-CNRC) et des partenaires de déploiement pilote.
Collaborer directement avec l’équipe créative pour veiller à ce que la technologie serve et rehausse l’expérience utilisateur.
Établir des pratiques d’ingénierie, des outils et des normes de documentation permettant à la plateforme de passer à une échelle de plusieurs milliers d’unités par an.
En utilisant cette plateforme comme point de départ, travailler avec l’équipe technique actuelle pour transformer nos œuvres uniques passées en une base partagée afin de développer de nouveaux produits et expériences.

VOTRE PROFIL

Plus de 10 ans d’expérience en systèmes embarqués, en développement de produits matériel-logiciel ou dans une discipline d’ingénierie connexe.
Expérience concrète dans la conduite d’un produit matériel du prototype à la production à grande échelle (conception de PCB, micrologiciels, boîtiers, bancs d’essai et chaîne d'approvisionnement).
Maîtrise approfondie des architectures embarquées sans fil : Wi-Fi, BLE, réseaux maillés (mesh), protocoles de synchronisation temporelle. Expérience avec les composants de type Espressif : un atout majeur.
Expérience pratique en gestion de l’énergie : systèmes de batteries, recharge solaire, conception faible consommation (low-power), gestion thermique en extérieur.
Capacité démontrée à diriger et faire grandir des équipes d’ingénierie dans un environnement émergent et aux ressources limitées. Vous savez quand concevoir sur mesure et quand acheter une solution existante.
Expérience de la conception pour des conditions extérieures rigoureuses, de la conformité réglementaire (CE, FCC, indices IP) et du rendement de fabrication.
Aisance à travailler au sein d’un studio créatif interdisciplinaire à taille humaine. Vous comprenez que les décisions techniques façonnent directement des expériences humaines dans l’espace public.
Bilinguisme fonctionnel (français et anglais).

ATOUTS

Expérience avec les systèmes audio : traitement numérique du signal (DSP), conception d’haut-parleurs, amplification audio en contexte embarqué.
Connaissance des plateformes infonuagiques pour la gestion de flottes IoT et les mises à jour à distance du micrologiciel (OTA).
Parcours en art interactif, en design d’expérience ou en installations publiques.
Expérience dans la rédaction de demandes de subventions ou la gestion de programmes de financement en R&D.

CE QUE NOUS OFFRONS

Un projet techniquement ambitieux doté d’une véritable portée créative. La technologie que vous développerez sera expérimentée par des milliers de personnes dans des villes du monde entier.
Un studio collaboratif à échelle humaine (environ 15 personnes) où les décisions se prennent rapidement et où votre travail a un impact direct.
Environnement de travail basé à Montréal.
Occasions de voyager pour des installations et des déploiements pilotes.
Accès à un réseau de conseiller·ère·s de calibre mondial en réseaux de capteurs sans fil et systèmes embarqués.

NOTRE ENGAGEMENT

Daily tous les jours s’engage à bâtir une équipe inclusive qui reflète la diversité des espaces publics pour lesquels nous concevons. Nous accueillons les candidatures de tous horizons, identités et parcours. Nous vous encourageons à postuler même si vous ne répondez pas à la totalité des critères.

--

WHO WE ARE

Daily tous les jours is an award-winning art and design studio working in an emergent field of practice combining interactive art, storytelling, performance, and urban design to reinvent living together for the 21st century. Using the raw material of the everyday, their work explores the dynamics of cooperation between people in proposing new models of living together.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are building the next generation of our interactive artworks: patent-pending, fully self-contained, wireless, solar-powered experiences that create collective music without a single cable or technician on site. Building on our existing 15 years of experience to imagine the next 15.
This is a genuine R&D challenge: distributed embedded nodes, wireless synchronization, outdoor power autonomy, and a software platform to update and monitor installations remotely. We need a CTO who can hold the technical vision for this platform and nurture the team that will make it real, a person who is equally at home reading a schematic, reviewing firmware architecture, specifying solar power capacity, collaborating with industrial designers and presenting a product roadmap.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Define and own the technical architecture of this new platform: embedded hardware, firmware, wireless networking, power management, and the remote software platform.
Build and lead a small, focused engineering team starting with an embedded firmware developer and a product owner, growing into dedicated hardware and software engineers.
Drive the full R&D cycle from proof-of-concept through alpha, outdoor field pilot, and design-for-manufacturing.
Define and protect intellectual property.
Act as the primary technical interlocutor for external partners, advisors, grant bodies (NRC IRAP), and pilot deployment partners.
Collaborate directly with the creative team to ensure the technology serves and elevates the experience.
Establish engineering practices, tooling, and documentation standards that allow the platform to scale to thousands of units per year.
Using this platform as a starting point, work with the existing technical team to help turn our legacy of one-off artworks into a shared foundation to develop more products and experiences.

WHAT YOU BRING

10+ years of experience in embedded systems, hardware-software product development, or a related engineering discipline.
Demonstrated experience taking a hardware product from prototype to manufacturing at scale. You have dealt with PCB design, firmware, enclosures, test fixtures, and supply chain.
Deep fluency in wireless embedded architectures: Wi-Fi, BLE, mesh networking, time-synchronization protocols. Experience with Espressif-class devices is a strong asset.
Hands-on experience with power management: battery systems, solar charging, low-power design, outdoor thermal management.
Proven ability to lead and grow engineering teams in an early-stage, resource-constrained environment. You know when to build and when to buy.
Experience designing for harsh outdoor conditions, regulatory compliance (CE, FCC, IP ratings), and manufacturing yield.
Comfort working in a small, cross-disciplinary creative studio. You understand that the technical decisions here directly shape human experiences in public space.

NICE TO HAVE

Experience with audio systems: DSP, speaker design, audio amplification in embedded contexts.
Familiarity with cloud platforms for IoT fleet management and OTA firmware updates.
Background in interactive art, experience design, or public installations.
Experience writing grant applications or managing R&D funding programs.
Functional bilingualism (French and English).

WHAT WE OFFER

A technically ambitious project with real creative purpose. The technology you build will be experienced by thousands of people in cities around the world.
A collaborative, human-scale studio (around 15 people) where decisions happen fast and your work has direct impact.
Work environment based in Montréal.
Opportunities to travel for installations and pilot deployments.
Access to a network of world-class advisors in wireless sensor networks and embedded systems.

OUR COMMITMENT

Daily tous les jours is committed to building an inclusive team that reflects the diversity of the public spaces we design for. We welcome candidates of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every single requirement.
We thank all applicants for their interest in this position; however, only those we wish to interview will be contacted.

SV Law is a leading full-service law firm proudly serving Guelph, Elora, Waterloo, and the surrounding communities since the mid-1960s. With a team of over 50 lawyers and dedicated professional staff, the Firm provides trusted, practical legal counsel across a comprehensive range of practice areas — including services to both business and personal clients.

The Firm is consistently recognized as a leader across Southwestern Ontario, is home to multiple lawyers named among The Best Lawyers in Canada and has been recognized as a Top Employer, in Guelph, and across Southwestern Ontario, and Canada. The Firm is deeply rooted in its communities — supporting local organisations through fundraising, sponsorship, and volunteerism.

The Firm has experienced continued year-on-year growth. To support the next phase of growth it is seeking an experienced financial leader to serve as its first Chief Financial Officer (‘CFO’).

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is an exciting opportunity for a senior finance professional to step into a newly created, high-impact leadership role. Reporting directly to the Managing Partner and working alongside the Executive Committee and the Chief Administrative Officer, the CFO will be an integral member of the Firm’s senior leadership team — supporting ongoing growth by maintaining and enhancing the Firm’s enviable financial foundation and overseeing the Firm’s approach to technology / artificial intelligence.

The CFO will bring the financial discipline, strategic rigour, and professional services expertise that a fast-growing firm of this scale demands. This is a superb role for a candidate who combines strategic vision with hands-on execution, and who thrives at the intersection of finance, technology, and people.

WHAT WE OFFER

Competitive Executive Compensation:

A total rewards package commensurate with the seniority and scope of the role, including a performance-based incentive component.

Comprehensive Benefits –
Health, dental, vision, life insurance, and employee wellness programs.
RRSP Matching –
A meaningful employer-matched RRSP program to support your long-term financial security.
Professional Development –
Ongoing investment in leadership growth through continuing education, professional development, and industry engagement.
Work-Life Integration –
A flexible working arrangement balancing the requirements of this senior role. The Firm highly values work / life integration.
Exceptional Culture –
A collegial, community-minded environment where your contributions will be valued, recognised, and rewarded.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The CFO will provide leadership across the following areas:

Planning & Strategy –
Work with the senior leadership team to balance financial stability with the need to transform the Firm’s systems and policies. Provide oversight and ongoing enhancement of the Firm’s finance and technology teams and systems. Build and maintain a network across the legal profession to ensure the Firm is aware of competitive trends and best practices.
Budgeting & Forecasting –
Direct the planning and execution of the Firm’s annual budget cycle, with responsibility to ensure the Firm achieves its annual Profit targets. Reporting regularly to the Executive Committee and Partnership. Provide ongoing education to all lawyers on fee strategy and profitability.
Client & Finances –
Develop and execute a plan to streamline the client intake process. Drive the ongoing improvement of financial hygiene process.
Lawyer Support –
Automate and simplify financial processes to ensure that lawyers can primarily focus on client work. Work with the Partnership on the partner compensation cycle to align with the Firm’s strategy.
People & Culture –
Serve as a senior leader across the Firm, promoting the development of a positive and proactive culture.

HOW TO APPLY

SV Law has retained Triline Consulting Inc. to conduct this executive search. Qualified candidates are invited to submit a cover letter and résumé.

Qualifications The ideal candidate will be:
CPA designation required with a minimum of five years leadership experience within a professional services firm — preferably within the legal industry.
Demonstrated ability to work both hands-on, personally delivering service, and strategically advising and guiding the partnership
Understanding of technology and the fast-changing digital environment, including experience with practice management, document management, and billing systems.
Familiarity with the Ontario legal market, Law Society of Ontario regulations, and the economics of law firm management — including partnership structures and lawyer compensation models.
Excellent people skills with a proven ability to build trust, influence and persuade partners, lead teams, and foster collaboration while driving change and adaptation across the Firm.
A superb sense of humour and a genuine willingness to work as part of a successful, collaborative, high-performing team.

Description

Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture

CTO Office - Information Technology Vice-Presidency (ITVP)

Build the Future with Us

Position Context

At a time when artificial intelligence, automation, and digital platforms are redefining the pace of change in financial services, the Information Technology Vice-Presidency is seeking to strengthen its ability to drive a comprehensive, cohesive, and forward-looking enterprise architecture vision.

Reporting to the CTO within the CTO Office, the Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture plays a critical role in evolving enterprise architecture from a function primarily focused on alignment and governance into a strategic capability that accelerates transformation, simplification, and enterprise-wide AI adoption.

Your Mission

As the leader responsible for transforming the Architecture function, the Senior Director, Enterprise Architecture is accountable for defining, championing, and evolving the enterprise architecture vision across information, application, and technology domains while supporting business sectors in their transformation initiatives. The incumbent shapes the foundations that will enable iA to evolve into an AI-augmented enterprise, where data, platforms, processes, and digital capabilities can scale rapidly, securely, and efficiently.

Working in close partnership with senior architects and domain experts, the Senior Director creates the conditions that enable architectural expertise to have greater impact, faster, on organizational decisions and transformations.

Complementing the role of the Senior Director, Business Architecture and Innovation, this position is responsible for enterprise technology directions, principles, and architectures, while the other role is responsible for business capability and value stream architecture.

What You Will Accomplish With Us

Enterprise Architecture Vision and Strategic Direction

Define and maintain an integrated enterprise architecture vision aligned with the organization’s strategic priorities and its ambition to become a more AI-augmented enterprise.
Establish and evolve target technology architectures, principles, and directions, while exercising decision-making authority over them.
Ensure alignment between business models and priorities, organizational capabilities, key processes, and application and technology architectures, while identifying opportunities for simplification and acceleration.
Define target architectures and evolution roadmaps that modernize platforms, reduce complexity, and accelerate value delivery.

IT 2030 Plan, Roadmaps, and the ITE4B Portfolio

Lead the IT 2030 plan across all business lines and domains, coordinating its execution while managing dependencies and priorities.
Ensure business sector roadmaps remain aligned with enterprise-wide directions.
Oversee the ITE4B (IT Enablers for Business) portfolio under delegated authority from the CTO, ensuring architectural and technological consistency while aligning initiatives with target architectures, the simplification strategy, and the IT 2030 plan.
Lead prioritization and investment arbitration processes for the ITE4B portfolio by making dependencies and initiative value visible and reporting to the CTO and CIO in collaboration with the Corporate Project Office and business sectors, while preserving accountability for major decisions at the sector level.

Modernization of the Enterprise Architecture Practice

Reinvent the enterprise architecture practice to support the pace of transformation required in the age of artificial intelligence while maintaining robustness, security, and compliance within a regulated environment.
Leverage generative AI, automation, and modern engineering approaches to accelerate artifact production, impact analysis, documentation, and architectural decision-making.
Evolve the architecture function toward a practice focused more on influence, reuse, platforms, and business outcomes than on documentation production.

Business and IT Alignment and Convergence

Foster long-term alignment between business needs and architectural choices by positioning architecture as a strategic accelerator rather than a control function.
Translate business challenges into coherent architectural capabilities.
Position enterprise architecture as the integration point for AI, data, cybersecurity, and technology strategies, ensuring the foundations required for their responsible scaling.
Champion iAFG’s IT strategy and ensure its alignment with business, innovation, and AI roadmaps, in close collaboration with the Senior Director, Business Architecture and Innovation.

Governance and Architectural Leadership

Design and lead governance mechanisms that accelerate key decisions, clarify trade-offs, and reduce ambiguity.
Establish architecture directions, principles, standards, and positions on major and cross-functional initiatives, emphasizing clear, actionable, and risk-proportionate guidance.
Support executive decision-making bodies through clear and structured analysis while helping resolve complex cross-functional issues.
Define enterprise architecture standards and frameworks that support strong governance and enable increasing integration with platforms, processes, and delivery tools.
In collaboration with Risk Management, define AI and agent governance principles and architectural control layers, including auditability, autonomy boundaries, and data traceability.
Accelerate architecture decisions by equipping the practice with templates, reusable components, and pre-approved decisions for priority initiatives, ensuring that the compliant path is also the simplest one.

Leadership and Team Development

Provide strong leadership to enterprise architecture directors and teams through clear direction, senior expertise, and empowerment.
Unite stakeholders around a shared vision by acting as an effective communicator and negotiator.
Build future-ready capabilities and support the growth and development of architecture talent.

What Will Help You Succeed In This Role

Education and Experience

University degree in Information Technology, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
Significant experience in enterprise architecture, IT strategy, or organizational transformation, including leadership responsibilities and transformation of professional practices.
Strong understanding of business models and complex IT environments.
Experience collaborating with executive-level stakeholders.
Knowledge of trends in artificial intelligence, data, cybersecurity, automation, and emerging architectures, as well as their implications within a regulated financial services environment (an asset).

Key Competencies

Broad organizational and systems-thinking perspective.
Ability to guide technology decisions while leveraging the expertise of senior architects and domain specialists.
Strong analytical and synthesis skills with the ability to put complex and cross-functional issues into perspective.
Excellent communication and influence skills at strategic levels.
Strong negotiation skills and the ability to unite stakeholders around a common vision.

Advanced proficiency in both French and English, as the incumbent will be required to collaborate daily, both verbally and in writing, with unilingual English-speaking partners, teams, and stakeholders across Canada and internationally.

Personal Attributes

Credible leadership and professional presence.

Collaborative approach.

Why You Will Love Working with Us

A work environment where learning and development merge with a collective pursuit of excellence;
Artificial intelligence is in everyone’s hands, helping enhance personal effectiveness and supporting organizational growth;
A healthy, safe, equitable, and inclusive environment where individuals can fully express and develop their potential;
The opportunity to work in a hybrid environment supported by flexibility and access to inspiring, innovative workspaces.

Employee share purchase program

Telemedicine services
Employee and Family Assistance Program (EFAP)
Ergonomic furniture program
Performance bonus

And much more!

Apply Today and Take Charge of Your Career

jobs.description:
Head of Operations & Strategy
Joops.ai ·

About Joops.ai
Joops.ai is an AI-powered advertising platform that helps brands create, launch, and optimize high-performing video advertising at scale. We connect directly to Meta, TikTok, Google Ads, YouTube, and other major ad networks — analyzing historical campaign performance, generating new ad concepts and video creatives, publishing campaigns automatically, and continuously learning from performance data to improve future results.
We're entering our go-to-market phase and building the founding leadership team. As one of our earliest executive hires, you'll shape how this company runs.
The Opportunity
We're looking for someone to build the operating system of the company. As Joops scales, the Head of Operations & Strategy owns the processes, systems, data infrastructure, and operating cadence that let us grow quickly without adding friction — and translates the company's strategic priorities into execution across every function.
This is a hands-on role. You will build the reporting stack yourself before you hire someone to run it. You will write the first version of the sales process, the onboarding runbook, and the board deck. You'll operate across sales, marketing, product, technology, finance, and operations — with the mandate to set priorities and hold the organization accountable to them.
What You'll Own
Operating systems and process

Design and implement the company's core operating cadence — annual and quarterly planning, goal-setting, weekly business reviews, and executive reporting.
Build the internal systems stack (CRM, data warehouse, BI/reporting, project and workflow tooling) and own how data flows between them. Define the source of truth for every number the company runs on.
Establish company-wide KPIs and operating metrics, and build the dashboards and reporting infrastructure that make performance visible in real time.
Build revenue operations end to end: pipeline definitions, sales process and stages, forecasting discipline, pricing and approval workflows, and commission structures.
Design customer onboarding and delivery operations — how a new brand gets from signed to live campaigns, with clear ownership, SLAs, and runbooks.
Own platform and partner operations: ad account provisioning, billing and ad-spend reconciliation, margin tracking, and the operational relationships with Meta, TikTok, Google, and other networks.
Build the back-office foundation: vendor management, procurement, contracts and legal workflow, finance operations, and internal policy.
Document how the company works, and automate it wherever possible — including using our own AI tooling internally. Every process you build should be one someone else can run.
Identify operational bottlenecks before they become constraints, and fix them.

Strategy and execution

Develop and help execute the company's overall strategic plan.
Partner with Sales on go-to-market strategy and the design of the commercial organization.
Develop the marketing strategy and help recruit the team to execute it.
Work with Product and Technology to prioritize the roadmap and manage inbound requests from sales, marketing, and customers through a defined intake process.
Conduct market, customer, competitor, and industry research to support strategic decision-making.
Identify new markets, partnerships, products, and revenue opportunities.
Drive cross-functional initiatives and ensure alignment and accountability across the organization.

Finance, capital, and org

Own financial modelling, budgeting, and the annual plan; track performance against it.
Support investor relations, fundraising, and financing initiatives; prepare investor presentations, financial materials, and board reporting.
Assist with executive recruiting, organizational design, and workforce planning — including the hiring, onboarding, and performance processes themselves.
Serve as a strategic partner to the CEO on other high-priority initiatives.

What We're Looking For
Experience at a top-tier management consulting firm. This is a requirement — we need the analytical rigour and structured problem-solving that comes with it.
Plus
real operating experience: time in-house at a high-growth technology company in business operations, revenue operations, strategy and operations, or a COO/chief-of-staff capacity, where you owned the systems and processes and not just the recommendation.
Demonstrated track record of building operational infrastructure from scratch — you can point to specific processes, systems, and reporting you designed and implemented, and what changed as a result.
Strong systems and tooling fluency: CRM administration, data warehouses, BI tools, workflow automation. Comfort with SQL and working directly with data is a significant advantage.
Excellent analytical, financial modelling, and problem-solving skills.
Experience developing go-to-market strategies and leading cross-functional initiatives.
Strong executive communication, presentation, and stakeholder-management skills.
Comfortable operating in ambiguity, and genuinely willing to do the unglamorous work of building processes from the ground up.
Entrepreneurial mindset and the desire to help build an early-stage company.
MBA strongly preferred.
Experience in technology, artificial intelligence, advertising, SaaS, or digital marketing is an asset.

jobs.title: Vice-President, Enterprise Onboarding & Operations
jobs.description:
*This position is available in Toronto or Windsor.

WHO WE ARE

GreenShield is a proudly Canadian, national non-profit health care and insurance organization, driven by our mission of Better Health for All. We believe health care is a right, not a privilege, and we are committed to improving health outcomes, advancing health equity, and building a future where every Canadian can reach their full health and well-being potential.

Through our unique integrated payer-provider ("payvider") model, we offer insurance, administer benefits, and pay claims as a ‘payer’ while offering health care services such as mental health, pharmacy, telemedicine, and chronic disease management as a ‘provider’. As a non-profit social enterprise without shareholders, we reinvest our excess earnings to directly support underserved communities. Through GreenShield Cares, we positively impacted the health and well-being of over one million Canadians between 2020 and 2025. What’s driving us now is the commitment to measurably impact an additional three million Canadians by 2030 – across mental health, essential medicines, and chronic disease management – through scalable initiatives that deliver meaningful change in pursuit of our mission of Better Health for All.

At GreenShield, our culture is where purpose meets passion and performance. Our teams work as one to deliver meaningful, measurable impact for the people and communities we serve.

THE ROLE IN A NUTSHELL

The Vice-President, Enterprise Onboarding & Operations Optimization is accountable for leading GreenShield’s enterprise onboarding, enrollment, and implementation functions, ensuring the seamless, accurate, and scalable implementation of clients, plans, and members across all GreenShield portfolios (Group and Individual Insurance, Claims Adjudication, Benefits Administration, Third-Party Administration (TPA), and Health services).

This role is responsible for delivering a consistent, high-quality onboarding, enrollment and implementation experience that enables operational readiness, supports growth, and protects the client and member experience from day one.

In addition to leading onboarding and enrollment, the Vice-President has accountability for key enterprise operations capabilities that strengthen service delivery across the organization, including the Enterprise Operations Business Partnership & Problem Resolution team, and Enterprise Operations reporting. Through these capabilities, the role ensures strong internal stakeholder partnership, coordinated resolution of operational issues, and clear performance visibility from frontline operations through to executive leadership.

The Vice-President will lead a broad mandate that combines operational execution with enterprise coordination—driving standardization, continuous improvement, service quality, and operational transparency across onboarding, enrollment, implementation, reporting, business partnership, and problem resolution. This role ensures GreenShield has the governance, insight, and cross-functional alignment needed to deliver consistent outcomes and support enterprise growth.

We’re looking for a strategic and execution-oriented leader with deep experience building and scaling complex operational functions, and a strong track record of improving quality, speed, transparency, and experience through process discipline, stakeholder partnership, and technology enablement.

This leader brings credibility with senior stakeholders, strong operational judgment, and the ability to balance hands-on execution with enterprise-level thinking. They are equally comfortable leading core onboarding and enrollment operations, overseeing performance reporting and service insights, and ensuring complex operational issues are resolved in a deliberate, timely, and sustainable way.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and evolve the Enterprise Onboarding, Enrollment, and Implementation function, accountable for client, plan, and member implementation and onboarding across GreenShield.
End-to-end ownership of onboarding, enrollment, and implementation processes, from intake and setup through operational readiness and handoff to steady-state operations.
Direct and own all onboarding, implementation, and enrollment support activities for new business occurring across the enterprise, including approach, timing, processes, plans, execution, client relationship management, and quality.
Drive a consistent, unified, and elevated customer and client experience both within and across GreenShield.
Ensure quality and accuracy, with a goal to be “error free”, in implementation, eligibility, plan build, enrollment, related solution configuration activities, and client-ready contract and booklet production.
Partner with GreenShield's Lines of Business (LOBs), the Quebec market, Client Segments, Technology, Product, and Enterprise Operations to enable growth, reduce friction, and improve time-to-live for new clients and plans.
Coordinate with internal stakeholders to ensure awareness of new clients and requirements, downstream impacts are understood and addressed, capacity implications are considered, and implementation schedules reflect operational realities.
Lead transformation initiatives focused on automation and technology, standardization, simplification, and continuous improvement to enable increased scalability/efficiency, create enterprise capacity for growth, and improve customer experience.
Establish and manage performance metrics related to timeliness, accuracy, quality, readiness, and client experience across onboarding and enrollment operations.
Ensure that the Enterprise Business Partner & Problem Resolution function is effectively fulfilling its mandate to be the single point of contact for all LOB EVPs, LOB SLT leaders, Quebec market lead, Client Segment leads, and Enterprise Sales leadership in relation to Enterprise Operations.
Ensure that the Change Advisory Board (CAB) is chaired and managed effectively to fulfill its mandate as the formal approval gate for non-standard requirements, implementation timing, and enterprise capacity related to implementation timing.
Ensure rapid, comprehensive, and consistent issue resolution and communication related to all operational issues, problems, questions, escalations, and strategic requests related to Enterprise Operations.
Ensure strong internal stakeholder partnership by enabling responsive, coordinated, and solutions-oriented engagement on operational priorities, issues, and service needs.
Oversee the coordination and resolution of cross-functional operational issues and escalations, ensuring timely communication, clear accountability, and a focus on sustainable root-cause resolution.
Oversee the development and use of KPIs, dashboards, and enterprise reporting, ensuring performance visibility from frontline operations through to executive leadership, and enabling data-informed decision-making, prioritization, and continuous improvement.
Ensure enterprise leaders have clear, consistent, and actionable operational insights through structured reporting and effective translation of performance data into business implications and improvement priorities.
Support effective cross-functional governance and integration across Enterprise Operations, ensuring interdependencies are managed, information flows appropriately, and leaders are equipped to act quickly and cohesively.
Support Enterprise Operations leadership in responding to internal audit, risk, compliance, and regulatory requests relevant to operational performance, readiness, and issue resolution.
Build and lead a high-performing, engaged team, embedding a culture of accountability, responsiveness, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Extensive senior leadership experience in enterprise operations, onboarding, enrollment, implementation, solution configuration, or related functions, ideally within insurance, health, benefits administration, or financial services.
Extensive senior leadership experience in enterprise operations, onboarding, enrollment, implementation, solution configuration, or related functions, ideally within insurance, health, benefits administration, or financial services.
Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional operational processes at scale with accountability for quality, service, and business outcomes.
Proven experience driving transformation, standardization, and automation in large, matrixed organizations.
Strong understanding of operational risk, data accuracy, readiness, and the downstream impacts of onboarding and enrollment quality on client, member, and business outcomes.
Strong financial, operational, and analytical acumen, including experience managing operational performance, capacity, and service effectiveness.
Exceptional communication and stakeholder leadership skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and build trusted partnerships across functions and lines of business.
Experience leading, interpreting, and using operational metrics, dashboards, and performance reporting to improve visibility, accountability, and decision-making.
Experience overseeing complex issue resolution, service recovery, or enterprise escalation processes, with a focus on root-cause resolution and sustainable improvement.
Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration or a related field; advanced degree preferred.

Leadership Behaviors

Results-focused, with the ability to balance pace, quality, and risk.
Leads with an end-to-end service mindset, understanding the impact of decisions and execution across the full client, member, and operational experience.
Drives consistency and quality, setting high standards for execution, follow-through, and operational discipline.
Creates accountable integration across teams, ensuring alignment, transparency, and coordinated action across functions and levels of the organization.
Brings strong ownership and accountability for outcomes, balancing pace, quality, risk, and sustainability.
Communicates clearly and proactively, translating operational complexity into practical direction, decisions, and action.
Builds trust and credibility through sound judgment, responsiveness, and a practical, solutions-oriented leadership style.
Leads people with clarity and care, creating an environment of inclusion, high expectations, and continuous improvement.

THE CULTURE

We believe a career should be meaningful. Not just a means to earn a living. Our culture is one where everyone's voice is heard and valued. Because that’s what it takes to create better health for all. We dare to challenge the status quo. And we’re driven by people who have challenged theirs. We believe that your workplace should empower you to be the best version of yourself. That’s why we provide a place where you can be inspired, challenged, and rewarded.

Where your growth means our growth.
Where your voice is heard and valued.
Where your work has purpose. And purpose matters.

We believe our people are critical to our overall success. Inclusivity makes us a stronger, smarter and more informed organization. Being intentionally inclusive of diverse backgrounds, perspectives and experiences will enhance our company culture to positively impact how we support our communities. A career at GreenShield isn’t just about personal achievements, it's about making a difference together.

Here’s to Better Health for All!

A FEW MORE DETAILS

Proficiency in English is required for this position. As part of this role, you will be required to communicate with colleagues or customers who use English as their primary language. By requiring English proficiency for this position, we aim to ensure that our employees can excel in their roles, collaborate, and communicate effectively, and contribute to the success of our organization.

GS supports diversity, equity and inclusion in our teams and communities, and we value the unique contributions made by all. Eve

Du développement et de la construction de projets évolutifs dans l'éolien (terrestre et maritime), le solaire, le stockage (batteries et centrales hydroélectriques à pompage-turbinage), la recharge intelligente des véhicules électriques, les microréseaux, l'hydrogène vert et les projets de transmission, jusqu'à la maximisation de la performance et de la rentabilité grâce à des opérations et une maintenance qualifiées et une optimisation innovante des actifs, nos équipes fournissent des solutions expertes tout au long de la chaîne de valeur, de l'origine à l'exploitation commerciale.

Faites partie d'une équipe collaborative et innovante qui s'engage à fournir des solutions renouvelables pour promouvoir la transition vers un avenir énergétique durable.

Avantages Et Bénéfices

Des bonis compétitifs. Ce poste est éligible à notre programme de bonis annuels.

REER/RPDP gratifiant. Nous fournissons une généreuse contribution de contrepartie.

Responsabilités

Responsabilités

Canada Create™ is a Toronto-based digital marketing agency founded in 2008, specializing in web development, branding, SEO, social media marketing, and lead generation.
