jobs.description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

Sitting within the broader Safety & Customer Care team, Lyft's Customer Care Operations organization manages over 1.7 million monthly customer interactions and serves as the company's primary direct touchpoint with riders, drivers, and businesses — spanning frontline support across multiple customer segments, a global BPO workforce, and the central functions that enable them to operate at scale.

The Director of Business Planning & Central Operations is a newly created role at the center of how Customer Care runs and grows. This leader will ensure the org is resourced and positioned for the future, and will own the functions that keep Customer Care financially disciplined and execution-ready. Reporting to the Senior Director of Customer Care Operations, they will lead five functions: Planning & Forecasting, Workforce Management, Readiness & Integration, Vendor Management, and Support Excellence.

What You'll Do

Business Planning & Strategy

Partner with the Senior Director to drive H1 and H2 planning — translating annual objectives into operational plans, investment decisions, and resource models.
Lead the investment brief process: sizing opportunities, articulating trade-offs, and building the business cases that secure resourcing for strategic priorities.
Drive capacity planning, scenario modeling, and long-range forecasting to ensure the internal and external workforce scales efficiently alongside platform growth and AI adoption.
Define and operationalize OKRs across the portfolio, then build the rhythms and infrastructure — scorecards, business reviews, and performance dashboards — that hold teams accountable and give leadership clear visibility into progress and outcomes.

Growth & Integrations

Lead operational readiness for major product launches, external partnerships, and platform expansions — ensuring Customer Care is prepared from scoping through hypercare.
Own the integration framework for new lines of business and strategic partnerships, including Lyft's expansion into autonomous vehicles and external mobility platforms.
Serve as the connective tissue between Customer Care and Product, Engineering, Legal, and Communications on initiatives with significant customer support implications.

Vendor & Financial Operations

Own financial operations across the portfolio, partnering with Finance and Workforce Management to maintain cost discipline, model the impact of product changes and AI automation, and invest strategically in quality and transformation.
Lead end-to-end management of Lyft's BPO vendor relationships — owning governance cadences, enterprise-level performance reviews, SLA enforcement, escalation management, and contract renewals, in close partnership with Procurement for new and renegotiated agreements.

People Leadership

Hire, develop, and retain high-performing teams.
Create clarity of ownership across a function that sits at the intersection of finance, operations, and technology, where the decisions made show up directly in customer experience and cost structure.

What We're Looking For

10+ years in business strategy, operations, consulting, or investment banking, with at least 5 years in a senior leadership role owning complex operational or strategic functions.
Strong financial and analytical foundation — comfortable building capacity models, stress-testing business cases, and translating the output into a crisp leadership narrative.
Experience leading or supporting large-scale growth initiatives, integrations, or partnerships, ideally in a marketplace or platform business.
AI fluency — you understand how AI is reshaping operations and can lead through that transformation with confidence.
Exceptional cross-functional partner — you build trust with Finance, Product, Tech, and Operations and can drive alignment across a matrixed organization.
Clear, direct, and decisive — you make decisions with the information available, communicate them crisply, and adapt when new data arrives.
Experience in customer support or contact center operations is a plus, not a requirement.
MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred; strong quantitative background required.

Mental health benefits
Family building benefits
Child care and pet benefits
Access to a Lyft funded Health Care Savings Account
RRSP plan to help save for your future

jobs.description:
Requisition ID: 261595

Join a purpose driven winning team, committed to results, in an inclusive and high-performing culture.

The Role

The Director, Cloud Governance & Controls Engineering is responsible for establishing, operationalizing, and continuously enhancing a fully automated control and governance framework for cloud platforms within a highly regulated global financial institution. This role provides enterprise leadership to ensure that cloud infrastructure and platform services are designed, built, and operated with appropriate risk management, regulatory compliance, and security controls embedded by default across the full technology lifecycle.

Reporting directly to the Senior Vice President & Global Head, Global Banking & Markets Engineering, the role blends governance accountability with a strong engineering mindset. The Director partners closely with independent risk, compliance, and control functions to define a comprehensive control inventory, while leading the automation and enforcement of those controls through scalable cloud engineering frameworks. This position plays a critical role in enabling safe cloud adoption at scale, supporting innovation while meeting regulatory and audit expectations.

Is this role right for you? In this role you will:

Own the design, implementation, and ongoing evolution of the cloud controls and governance framework, ensuring alignment with regulatory, risk, security, and audit requirements applicable to financial services.
Partner with independent risk, compliance, and control functions to establish and maintain a comprehensive, well‑defined control inventory for cloud infrastructure and platform services.
Lead the automation and enforcement of controls across the cloud lifecycle, embedding guardrails into engineering platforms, pipelines, and reference architectures.
Build and lead a high‑performing team of 3–4 specialists responsible for translating control requirements into scalable engineering solutions and reusable frameworks.
Collaborate with product and platform Technical Program Managers to ensure controls are captured early in design and consistently applied through build, deployment, and operations.
Define and oversee engineering‑led governance mechanisms, including dashboards, interfaces, and metrics that provide real‑time visibility into control effectiveness and compliance posture.
Influence cloud strategy and platform roadmaps to ensure risk and control considerations are addressed without compromising developer productivity or time to market.
Support internal and external audits, regulatory inquiries, and management reviews by providing clear evidence of automated control design and operation.
Establish standards, policies, and patterns that promote secure‑by‑design and compliant‑by‑default cloud engineering practices.

Skills

Do you have the skills that will enable you to succeed in this role? We’d love to work with you if you have:

Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent experience.
Extensive experience in cloud engineering, platform engineering, or cloud security within largescale, regulated environments.
Demonstrated experience designing and implementing automated controls, policy‑as‑code, and governance frameworks across IaaS and PaaS platforms.
Proven people‑leadership experience, including building and leading small, specialized technical teams.
Experience in financial services, capital markets, or other highly regulated industries.
Deep familiarity with public cloud platforms and modern control enforcement techniques (e.g., policy‑as‑code, CI/CD integration, cloud security posture management).
Experience engaging with regulators, auditors, and second‑line risk functions on technology control matters.
Strong executive communication skills with the ability to influence senior technology and risk leaders.

What's in it for you?

Diversity, Equity, Inclusion & Allyship - We strive to create an inclusive culture where every employee is empowered to reach their fullest potential, respected for who they are, and are embraced through bias-free practices and inclusive values across Scotiabank. Accessibility and Workplace Accommodations - We value the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the Bank and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Scotiabank continues to locate, remove, and prevent barriers so that we can build a diverse and inclusive environment while meeting accessibility requirements.
Upskilling through online courses, cross-functional development opportunities, and tuition assistance.
Competitive Rewards program including bonus, flexible vacation, personal, sick days, and benefits will start on day one.
Community Engagement - no matter where you choose to work from; we offer opportunities for community engagement & belonging with our various programs.

Guided by our purpose: "for every future", we help our customers, their families and their communities achieve success through a broad range of advice, products and services, including personal and commercial banking, wealth management and private banking, corporate and investment banking, and capital markets.

jobs.title: Director, Developer Platform & Experience
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit gomotive.com to learn more.

About The Role

Motive is moving to an AI-driven development lifecycle. Agents that plan, generate, test, review, and help operate our systems — with engineers directing the work rather than typing all of it — are where software engineering at Motive is going. That direction is set. What we need now is a leader to build it.

We are hiring a Director of Developer Platform & Experience to own that execution and the platform underneath it. This role owns Motive's internal developer ecosystem end to end: developer experience, developer infrastructure, build and CI/CD systems, and the testing frameworks that let hundreds of engineers move quickly without breaking things. It also owns AI-DLC in practice — the tooling, cloud agent infrastructure, evaluation practice, and governance that determine whether agentic development actually makes us faster or just makes us noisier.

Our engineering organization spans North America, Europe, and Asia, across a Rails monolith, Go services, mobile, and embedded systems. How fast and how confidently that organization ships is one of our most important business levers.

This is a builder's leadership role, not a strategy role. You will inherit real systems and real teams, and be measured on whether engineers at Motive ship faster, with higher confidence, and with less friction than they did the quarter before.

The mandates

AI-driven development — make agentic development a governed, measured, everyday part of how Motive builds software.
Cloud-based agentic development infrastructure — build the substrate that lets agents run in the cloud, in parallel, safely.
Developer experience — make the inner loop fast and the right path the easy path.
Developer infrastructure — make build, CI/CD, and release systems fast, reliable, and cost-aware at scale.

The defining challenge: agentic development in the cloud

Most AI coding adoption stops at the laptop — one engineer, one agent, one local checkout. That ceiling is low, and moving past it is the signature technical challenge of this role.

You will build the infrastructure that runs agentic development in the cloud: ephemeral, reproducible, isolated environments where many agents work concurrently on real Motive codebases, run real tests against real dependencies, and open real pull requests — without an engineer babysitting a terminal, and without compromising security or blowing up spend.

This is a hard distributed-systems and platform problem, not a tooling procurement exercise. Done right, engineers stop being throughput-bound by their own machines and start operating as reviewers and directors of parallel work. We want a leader who finds that problem exciting and has the platform depth to solve it.

What you'll own

AI-driven development lifecycle (AI-DLC)

Translate Motive's AI-driven development direction into an executable multi-year plan — how agents plan, generate, test, review, and operate under human direction, what "human in the loop" means at each stage, and where engineers spend their time as a result.
Evaluate, select, and roll out AI developer tools (coding agents, code review, test generation, incident investigation, documentation) and build the internal scaffolding — context, MCP servers, evals, guardrails — that makes them effective on Motive's actual codebases rather than on a demo repo.
Stand up a rigorous LLM and agent evaluation practice: benchmarks, offline and online evals, quality and cost regression tracking, and a defensible model and vendor selection process that survives a fast-moving landscape.
Own the governance layer with Security, Legal, and Platform: acceptable use, code provenance and licensing, secrets and data handling, and audit trails for AI-generated changes.
Define and report the adoption and impact metrics that tell us whether this is actually working — not just seat counts and enthusiasm.
Bring the organization along. Drive enablement, internal advocacy, and the cultural shift from "write code, then review" to continuous review of agent-generated work.

Cloud-based agentic development infrastructure

Build and own the platform that runs agentic development in the cloud: on-demand, reproducible, isolated workspaces provisioned per task, with the right source, dependencies, secrets, and services already in place.
Design for concurrency and safety — sandboxed execution, least-privilege credentials, network egress controls, and blast-radius limits so many agents can run against real codebases without becoming a security or reliability incident.
Make agent runs fast and cheap: warm environment pools, caching and snapshotting, incremental builds, and test selection so a cloud agent loop is measured in minutes, not tens of minutes.
Own the orchestration and control plane — queueing, scheduling, autoscaling on Kubernetes, session lifecycle, artifact and log retention, and observability into what agents did and why.
Own unit economics. Instrument per-task and per-agent cost, set budgets and quotas, and keep the platform financially sustainable as usage scales across the org.
Build the human interface layer: how engineers dispatch work to cloud agents, monitor fleets of concurrent runs, review and merge results, and intervene when a run goes sideways.
Design for multi-region (US and EU) from the start, with configuration-driven rather than hardcoded regional behavior, and honor data residency and code-egress constraints.

Developer Experience

Own the inner loop end to end: local and cloud development environments, code search and navigation, IDE and agent tooling, dependency management, and onboarding time-to-first-PR.
Treat developers as your customers. Run regular DevEx research — surveys, interviews, instrumented telemetry — and publish a prioritized backlog the whole engineering org can see.
Define and drive the internal developer platform: golden paths, service scaffolding, and self-service capabilities that make the right way the easy way.

Developer infrastructure and engineering velocity

Own build systems, CI/CD, artifact and release pipelines, and the platform's outer loop across a Rails monolith, Go services, mobile, and embedded/firmware codebases.
Drive step-function improvements in DORA and velocity metrics: PR lead time, build and CI duration, CI reliability and flake rate, change failure rate, and time to restore.
Make cost, scale, and reliability of the developer platform a first-class concern — including multi-region (US and EU) behavior and configuration flexibility rather than hardcoded assumptions.

Testing and quality engineering

Own the testing strategy and frameworks: unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, hardware-in-the-loop, and performance. Drive test reliability, isolation, and speed so engineers trust the signal.
Build the infrastructure that makes high-quality testing cheap: fixtures, factories, test data management, environment provisioning, parallelization, and flake detection and quarantine.
Partner with quality and release engineering to shift quality left without slowing teams down.

Leadership

Lead a multi-team organization as a manager of managers, hiring and developing engineering managers and senior/staff-plus ICs.
Run an org distributed across North American and Asian time zones with genuine care for handoffs, overlap hours, on-call fairness, and inclusion — not just calendar math.
Operate as a peer to product and infrastructure leaders, influence a large engineering org without direct authority, and communicate strategy and results credibly to executives.

What we're looking for

Required

12+ years in software engineering with 6+ years leading engineering teams, including 2+ years as a manager of managers (Director, Senior Manager of Managers, or equivalent scope).
A real developer background — you have shipped and operated production systems, and engineers respect your technical judgment.
Deep DevOps and infrastructure depth: CI/CD, build systems, containers and Kubernetes, infrastructure as code (Terraform), cloud platforms (AWS preferred), and observability.
Demonstrated ownership of developer productivity, developer platform, or developer infrastructure at meaningful scale (hundreds of engineers or a large multi-language codebase), with measurable velocity outcomes you can describe.
Hands-on experience with modern AI developer tooling and a clear, opinionated point of view on where agentic development genuinely helps and where it does not.
Experience building or operating cloud-based development or execution environments — remote dev environments, ephemeral CI/build workers, container sandboxing, or multi-tenant compute platforms — including the security and cost controls that make them viable at scale.
Practical understanding of LLM evaluation — how to benchmark models and agents for coding tasks, how to measure quality and cost, and how to avoid being sold a demo.
Strong empathy for developers: you instrument the pain, listen to it, and prioritize accordingly rather than shipping platforms nobody adopts.
Experience leading distributed teams across multiple time zones.

Preferred

Experience with a large monolith undergoing modernization, and with polyglot environments (Ruby on Rails, Go, mobile, embedded).
Background in test infrastructure at scale — flake reduction, test selection, parallelization, hermetic environments.
Experience running platform work as a product: roadmaps, adoption funnels, internal customers, feature-flagged rollouts.
Familiarity with multi-region deployment and data residency constraints (US/EU).
Open source contribution, developer community involvement, or public writing on developer productivity or AI-assisted engineering.

Pay Transparency

Your compensation may be based on several factors, including education, work experience, and certifications. For certain roles, total compensation may include restricted stock units. Motive offers benefits including health, pharmacy, optical and dental care benefits, paid time off, sick time off, short term and long term disability coverage, life insurance as well as 401k contribution (all benefits are subject to eligibility requirements). Learn more about our benefits by visiting Motive Perks & Benefits .

The compensation range for this position will depend on where you reside. For this role, the compensation range is:

$238,000—$300,000 CAD

Job Description

Senior Director, AI Business Enablement

What's the opportunity?

We're looking for a transformational leader who can serve as a strategic peer to senior business executives and drive AI-powered business transformation across an entire Line of Business or Function. As a Senior Director on the AI Business Enablement team, you will own the full AI transformation ambition for your domain — setting the vision, building the opportunity pipeline, and ensuring executive alignment from ideation through to program framing and handoff.

You will be expected to challenge, provoke, and co-develop transformation roadmaps with senior business leaders — bringing a combination of strategic rigour, AI fluency, and the credibility that comes from having built and shipped solutions, not just recommended them.

Your responsibilities will include:

Executive partnership: Holding sustained, peer-level strategic relationships with senior business leaders (SVP+); co-developing and communicating the AI-enabled transformation vision for your domain
Pipeline origination: Identifying, sizing, and prioritising a rigorous pipeline of AI transformation opportunities — including new ideas not yet on the business’ horizon — with quantified value hypotheses ready for delivery intake
AI solution concept development: Generating innovative AI solution concepts for large business problems and validating them through rapid POC cycles (weeks, not quarters)
Business model & process re-engineering: Helping leaders fundamentally rethink business processes and operating models through an AI-enabled lens
Program framing: Partnering with business leaders beyond ideation — through business case development, go-to-market strategy, and program framing — to ensure ambition translates into execution
Delivery partnership: Working closely with our world-class AI Solutions and Research teams to ensure business context and outcomes expectations are carried through into delivery — maintaining alignment between the transformation ambition and the technical execution path
Cross-enterprise pattern recognition: Surfacing reuse opportunities, multi-LOB programs, and horizontal themes that no single vertical would initiate alone
Team leadership: Leading and developing a small team of high-performing leaders aligned to sub-segments within your domain

You're our ideal candidate if you:

Have 15+ years of progressive experience in management consulting, technology, AI/ML product development, or a combination thereof
Have a track record of building AI or technology-driven solutions that created material business impact — strategy and advisory experience is valued, but must be complemented by accountability for delivery outcomes
Possess the executive gravitas and communication skills to challenge and influence senior business leaders (SVP+) as a peer
Have demonstrated experience in process re-engineering or business model redesign, ideally enabled by technology or data
Have experience partnering with technical or engineering teams to translate business requirements into solution design and ensure delivery stays aligned to intended business outcomes
Bring a consultative problem-solving approach — able to structure ambiguous problems, develop hypotheses, and drive to action quickly
Have a working knowledge of AI/ML technologies, LLMs, and data platforms — sufficient to credibly assess feasibility, shape solution concepts, and engage technical teams
Banking or financial services experience is welcome but not required; what matters is the ability to rapidly develop domain depth and business-model understanding in complex industries

What's in it for you:

Lead AI transformation at one of Canada's largest and most respected financial institutions, with direct visibility to Group Head and Operating Committee level leadership at RBC
Shape the mandate and culture of a newly formed, high-impact function within RBC's AI Group
A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock options where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Ability to make a difference and lasting impact from a local-to-global scale

About the AI Group:

RBC's AI Group is the AI accelerator for RBC, with a focus on driving the shift from early-stage AI projects to scaled, client outcomes that amplify the impact of RBC's people. In addition to helping scale the biggest AI opportunities at RBC, the AI Group is responsible for advancing research into emerging use cases across generative and agentic AI, while maintaining expertise in security, responsible AI and regulatory expectations. The Business Enablement function within the AI Group partners with LOBs and Functions to set AI ambition, originate transformation opportunities, and frame programs for delivery — ensuring RBC remains at the frontier of AI-enabled value creation.

Head of Finance & Accounting

Weir Minerals

Mississauga, Ontario or Salt Lake City, UT

Hybrid

What We Do At Weir

We are a global leader in mining technology for a sustainable future. We help our customers extract the resources the world needs more efficiently and more sustainably. Our planet’s future depends on the transition to renewable energy, and that transition can only happen with the metals and minerals our customers deliver. So, we work side by side with mines across the globe to move less rock, use less energy, use water wisely, and create less waste. Together, we drive the shift to smart, efficient, and more sustainable mining.

Make your Impact

The Head of Finance and Accounting is a highly visible leadership position responsible for managing the organization’s financial control environment and ensuring compliance with IFRS, Group Financial Guidelines and local Statutory Accounting and regulatory requirements across the region.

This role oversees end-to-end accounting operations, including monthly, quarterly, and annual closings, and holds accountability for working capital and balance sheet forecasting, Balance Sheet and treasury management, and intercompany processes to maintain financial integrity.

In addition, the Head of F&A drives the harmonization and standardization of finance processes in line with divisional standards, ensuring robust governance and audit readiness across the business. Acting as a subject matter expert and key liaison for internal and external stakeholders, this individual combines exceptional technical expertise with strong leadership capabilities to build and develop a high-performing accounting organization, lead transformational initiatives, and foster a culture of compliance, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.

What you'll do:

Financial Governance & Compliance: Lead the management of the financial control environment across NAM, ensuring compliance with IFRS, Group Financial Guidelines, and local statutory requirements. Oversee month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes, maintain audit readiness, and manage treasury operations including cash flow and FX risk mitigation. Success means maintaining financial integrity and robust governance with zero compliance issues. Travel will be occasional across the region to support audit and stakeholder engagement.
Process Improvement & Standardization: Drive harmonization and standardization of finance processes (R2R, P2P, OTC) to transition from fragmented regional operations to a consistent, efficient model. What is the opportunity?

Global Functions Technology (GFT) is part of RBC’s Technology and Operations division. GFT’s impact is far-reaching as we collaborate with partners from across the company to deliver innovative and transformative IT solutions. Our clients represent Risk, Finance, HR, CAO, Audit, Legal, Compliance, Financial Crime, Capital Markets, Personal and Commercial Banking and Wealth Management. In your role, You’ll architect and create systems that directly influence billions in lending decisions, shaping RBC’s competitive edge in financial innovation.

We’re seeking a Director & Principal Engineer, AI/ML & MLOps Platform, who brings a unique blend of deep technical expertise and strategic leadership. This is a hands-on engineering leadership role focused on building and scaling data-driven systems and platform capabilities that enable advanced analytics, machine learning, and impactful business decisions. You will play a key role in shaping our next-generation credit decisioning and risk management platform, and lead by example in applying sound architectural thinking, engineering rigor, and technical mentorship. You will manage a team of seasoned engineers to deliver the visions to scale your impacts and pace of development.

What will you do?

Lead by Doing: Design, build, and review scalable data pipelines, analytics platforms, and ML systems. This is a hands-on role with end-to-end ownership, balancing hands-on coding (20-30%) with solution architectural & engineering leadership.
Set Technical Direction: Define and promote best practices in data and ML engineering. Evaluate emerging technologies and guide adoption to drive innovation.
Partner Cross-Functionally: Work closely with data scientists, business leaders, and IT teams to understand needs and translate them into technical solutions. Your first set of prominent goals are to transform the bank’s retail credit decisioning by bringing together a set of platform capabilities to enable our risk experts to scale vertically and horizontally to provide the depth and the breadth for competitive and personalize lending products.
Mentor and Inspire: Coach engineers and foster a high-performing, collaborative culture. Champion engineering excellence and team growth. You are not an old fashioned manager that just command, but a role model that cultivates a culture of innovation and high performance, who skillfully inspires the next generation of leaders without micro managing.
Deliver at Scale: Ensure projects are executed with high quality, on time, and aligned with business goals. Proactively identify risks and enforce compliance standards, especially around data governance and security.

8+ years of experience in designing and building data-intensive applications, with 3+ years in a senior technical leadership role.
Deep expertise in modern distributed data processing and ML engineering tools and languages (e.g., Python, Java/Scala, PySpark/Spark, Kafka, SQL, orchestration frameworks).

Excellent communication skills - able to clearly explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Demonstrated success in leading engineering teams and delivering high-impact platforms or products.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; Master's or PhD preferred.

Hands-on experience with AWS SageMaker and related services (Glue, EMR, Lambda, Step Functions, Airflow, CloudWatch).
Track record of building high-performing teams (e.g., hiring/retaining top talent, improving team NPS)

Shared Health leads the planning and coordinates the integration of patient-centered clinical and preventive health services across Manitoba. The organization also delivers some province-wide health services and supports centralized administrative and business functions for Manitoba health organizations.

Position Overview

Digital Health focuses on supporting clinical and business systems as the foundation for leveraging electronic data in the delivery of health-care services.

We have an opportunity for an executive director clinical digital services, who will lead a consultative clinical digital solution practice in support of Manitoba’s Clinical Preventive Services Plan and the outcomes defined in the approved clinical digital strategic services plan and annual operating plan. Focused on providing effective clinical digital solutions, processes, systems and technologies for public health system clients in Manitoba including Shared Health and six provincial service delivery organizations, the executive director clinical digital solutions will establish health informatics processes, systems and provide technology advice that enables the achievement of innovative and sustainable health services. The executive director will provide service-focused leadership to the clinical digital solutions staff across the province, ensure the delivery on service commitments by staff and vendors, lead the service delivery, performance measurement, continuous improvement and efficiency of a provincially-focused interdisciplinary team with a culture of client service in Shared Health, and encourage provincial clients to engage the team as their primary resource for clinical informatics and digital health processes, systems and technology advice. The successful candidate will develop and recommend provincial standards for clinical informatics and digital health processes, systems and technologies, collaborate with senior leaders across the health system to ensure the effective delivery, implementation, ongoing support and adoption of effective clinical informatics and digital health processes, systems and technologies, and act as a primary contact for the engagement of external vendors.

Reporting to the provincial lead and chief information officer of Digital Health, this executive director will engage leaders and critical stakeholders to collaboratively realign and standardize the use of provincial clinical informatics and digital health systems. The successful candidate will lead organizational change, ensure ongoing adoption, optimization, deployment and maintenance of technologies and related equipment, support and manage vendor contracts, and ensure effective services are provided to support overall organizational and health-care system requirements. The successful candidate’s leadership, professionalism, diplomacy, and continuous improvement orientation will be evident as they collaborate with clients and colleagues to provide excellent customer service, identify system solutions, and support an integrated province-wide health-care system that provides multiculturally respectful health services delivery.

As this role is provincial in nature, the work location is flexible within Manitoba and will be made in consultation with the successful candidate. We would be pleased to share a full job description with interested candidates who have submitted their application. Requests for more information may be directed via email to info@sharedhealthmb.ca, Attention: Human Resources.

15 years of progressive experience including:
10 years of senior or executive management experience in digitally enabled health service delivery, business transformation, strategic planning, participating in digital health solution planning, system implementation, and/or leading the management of digital health information systems for a large ICT services organization ensuring operational sustainment and service management according to ITIL processes, and running a 24/7 on-call support team.
5 years of experience leading a matrixed team to ensure collaboration and effective operations, working in a leadership role managing operational support for digital health systems, services and technologies.
5 years of experience applying strong program/project management in leading multiple, large, cross-functional teams on projects, delivering executive-level presentations and influencing, leading and managing negotiations with senior-level management and key internal and external stakeholders.
5 years of direct experience working in a clinical program with strong professional relationships with clinicians.

Post-secondary degree in clinical informatics, digital health or a related degree in computer science or technology from an accredited educational institution.
Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Foundation certification, or higher.
An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.

A valid Manitoba driver’s license and use of a personal motor vehicle for regular travel within the province.

Demonstrated senior-level leadership capabilities. Shared Health has adopted the LEADS in a Caring Environment framework.

Must be available for regular travel within the province, able to work safely in a typical computerized office environment, and able to lift and move items of up to approximately 25 pounds.

jobs.description:
At Saputo, we bring good to the table by making high-quality products, investing in our people, and supporting communities around the world . As a top 10 global dairy processor, we value contributions that matter and strive to foster an inclusive, growth-driven work environment. Ready to bring your best?

Overview of the role:

The Senior Director, People Strategy & Business Initiatives is a strategic leadership role reporting directly to the Chief Human Resources Officer. This role is designed to increase the strategic capacity of the CHRO and HR Leadership Team by connecting people strategy, organization design, talent strategy, people insights, HR modernization, and future-of-work capabilities into one integrated enterprise agenda.

The Senior Director will serve as a trusted advisor to the CHRO, HR Leadership Team, and other key stakeholders to advance priority business and people initiatives. The role leads a direct report and may provide indirect leadership to cross-functional project teams and external partners.

The role focuses on shaping fit-for-purpose operating models, strengthening organization design, simplifying how work gets done, enabling AI and technology-driven solutions, and translating people insights into clear recommendations for senior leaders.

How you will make contributions that matter:

Organization Design and Operating Model Strategy

Lead organization design and operating model work, including spans and layers analysis, role clarity, decision rights, governance, and ways of working.
Partner with the CHRO, HR Leadership Team, HRBPs, and business leaders to determine structures, capabilities, and accountabilities required to support business objectives.
Develop practical organization design principles, tools, and standards to support consistent, fact-based decisions across functions, geographies, and divisions.
Use internal insights, external benchmarks, and business context to challenge current models and recommend simpler, more agile, and more effective ways of operating.

HR Modernization, Future of Work and AI Enablement

Identify where process simplification, technology, automation, AI-enabled solutions, and stronger data can improve HR quality, speed, consistency, and employee experience.
Lead or support key HR and business initiatives that simplify governance, service delivery, decision-making forums, and ways of working.
Assess emerging trends in AI, skills, workforce planning, employee experience, analytics, and HR service delivery, and translate them into practical opportunities for Saputo.
Promote continuous improvement across HR by reducing complexity, eliminating duplication, clarifying accountabilities, and increasing work effectiveness.

Talent Strategy and Succession Management

Support the enterprise talent agenda by connecting talent insights, succession risks, workforce planning, internal mobility, and organization design implications to Saputo’s business strategy.
Partner with the HRBPs, division talent leaders, Talent Acquisition, Learning & Development, and Total Rewards to ensure talent discussions are informed by business priorities, workforce needs, and clear data.
Support preparation of CHRO, Executive Leadership Team, and Board-level materials related to talent pipeline, succession risks, critical roles, workforce capability, and organizational health.

People Insights, HR KPIs and Decision Support

Define and monitor the HR KPIs and people metrics that matter most to business performance, including organization health, workforce productivity, talent pipeline, internal mobility, retention, engagement, and HR process performance.
Connect data from talent, workforce planning, organization design, employee listening, HR systems, and business indicators to build stronger people insights.
Translate data, benchmarks, and trends into clear implications, options, and recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Partner with HR Systems to improve data quality, reporting discipline, dashboard usefulness, and analytics maturity.

Executive Advisory and Decision Support

Act as a thought partner to the CHRO on key people priorities, business initiatives, organization risks, and decision points.
Prepare executive-ready insights, options, recommendations, and discussion materials for CHRO, HR Leadership Team, Executive Leadership Team, and Board-related discussions.
Facilitate senior-level discussions on operating model choices, talent risks, workforce scenarios, organization design, and HR modernization priorities.
Build alignment across stakeholders and maintain momentum on priority initiatives that support the people agenda and business strategy.

You are best suited for the role if you have the following qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, Organizational Psychology, Organizational Development, Data Analytics, or a related field; Master’s degree considered an asset.
12+ years of progressive experience in HR strategy, organization design, talent management, strategic workforce planning, people analytics, HR modernization, management consulting, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading operating model reviews, organization design, spans and layers analysis, business initiatives, or enterprise change work in a complex organization.
Strong business acumen and ability to connect business strategy, organization design, talent implications, HR processes, technology, and people data into practical recommendations.
Data fluent, with the ability to interpret people metrics, identify trends, challenge assumptions, and translate insights into executive-level advice and action.
Experience identifying, implementing, or enabling technology, automation, digital, or AI-enabled HR solutions considered a strong asset.
Executive presence, consulting skills, sound judgment, discretion, and ability to influence senior stakeholders in a matrixed, multinational environment.
Excellent communication, facilitation, storytelling, and presentation skills, with the ability to make complex topics clear, concise, and actionable.
Experience in a multinational, manufacturing, CPG, food, or other operationally complex environment considered an asset.
Professional HR designation, considered an asset.
Candidates must be bilingual in French and English, as they will regularly interact with stakeholders across Canada and the United States.

The work you'll do is more than just a job.

At the State of Minnesota, employees play a critical role in developing policies, providing essential services, and working to improve the well-being and quality of life for all Minnesotans. The State of Minnesota is committed to equity and inclusion, and invests in employees by providing benefits, support resources, and training and development opportunities.

Minnesota Management and Budget (MMB) is seeking a Chief Data Officer (CDO) to serve as the State of Minnesota’s enterprise leader for statewide data strategy, governance, and ethical use. This position will set the vision for how data can strengthen program integrity and overall government performance. As the lead of the Minnesota Data Strategy Team, the CDO will build the legal, technical, and operational foundation that allows agencies to securely and responsibly use and share data, while guiding commissioners, executives, and cross-sector partners through complex policy and privacy considerations.

This role pairs strategic leadership with practical problem-solving, setting a statewide vision for data infrastructure by building collaboration across a federated data environment. The CDO will be a trusted advisor on law, ethics, and information policy, driving long-term improvements of the state’s data ecosystem and helping ensure Minnesotans benefit from well-governed, high-quality data.

Job Duties For This Position Include

Providing executive leadership for the Minnesota Data Strategy Team (MDST), directing managers, staff, and cross-agency partners to implement statewide data governance and privacy priorities
Establishing strategic, operational, and legal direction for the MDST, incorporating input from commissioners and executive leaders while making final determinations on statewide priorities
Advising senior leaders on the strategic, legal, and ethical considerations of data sharing and use, and directing implementation of governance mechanisms that balance innovation, privacy, risk mitigation, and accountability
Serving as the statewide point of escalation for complex, novel, or cross-agency legal issues affecting enterprise data sharing and governance
Establishing and implementing an enterprise data strategy that integrates national best practices in data governance, sharing, and use consistent with state and federal information policy and law
Building the enterprise legal frameworks, technical infrastructure, and agreements required for secure, privacy-protective, and responsible data sharing across agencies
Advancing the enterprise workforce’s capability to access and use data effectively to improve service delivery

All MMB Leaders are expected to demonstrate and develop the six competency themes from the Enterprise-Wide Leader Competency Model:

Leading Self
Leading Others
Leading the Organization
Leading Outside the Organization
Leading with DEAI
Getting Work Done

Telework options for this position are dependent on where the employee lives. With approval, employees that live within 50 miles from the primary work location may telework up to 50%. Employees that live 50 miles or more from the primary location and live in Minnesota
may telework more than 50% with approval.

Minimum Qualifications

To facilitate proper years of service crediting, please ensure that your resume clearly describes your experience in the areas listed and indicates the beginning and ending month and year for each job held. Candidates must clearly demonstrate all the following qualifications on their resume. Resume tips are available here. To be considered for the Chief Data Officer position, applicants must submit a cover letter.

At least six (6) years of experience developing or overseeing governance structures, data-sharing frameworks, or major policy or technology implementations involving multiple stakeholders or organizations
Juris Doctor (J.D.) from an ABA-accredited law school and actively licensed and in good standing to practice law in the State of Minnesota (or ability to obtain licensure prior to end of standard one-year probationary period).

Experience Must Include

Demonstrated senior-level experience in leading teams and large coalitions through complex organizational change, including designing and driving strategy through periods of significant structural, technological, or policy transformation.
Experience leading teams to analyze and set direction on complex issues at the intersection of policy, technology, and law, applying rigorous legal and technical analysis, negotiation, and sound judgment to forge a shared vision among parties with divergent interests.
Advanced ability to interpret statutes, regulations, and policy frameworks, including privacy law, and translate them into practical, actionable guidance for executives, legal teams, and technical stakeholders.
Writing and communication skills sufficient to represent significant projects with authority, distilling complex technical and legal information into clear, credible narratives for executives, subject matter experts, legislators, external partners, and the public.
Demonstrated respect for diversity and a deep commitment to fostering an inclusive and collaborative work environment.

jobs.title: Director, AI Product Ops
jobs.description:
Director, AI Product Ops — Direct Tax & Audit Product

Job Description

We are seeking an exceptional, transformative Director of AI Product Ops
to lead the operational and cultural evolution of Thomson Reuters' Direct Tax & Audit product
organization.

In this exciting opportunity as Director, AI Product Ops
, you will evolve our traditional program and operations function into a lean, AI-first Product Ops office. Your mission is two-fold: drive operational excellence across our entire software portfolio with "near-zero-overhead," and spearhead our AI maturity program, moving our teams from basic personal productivity to advanced, agent-driven workflows.

This is a hands-on, builder's seat designed to modernize how our teams work. You will serve as a critical catalyst for product innovation and foster faster, more effective ways of working across the team. By automating coordination and program management tasks, you will not only liberate our product teams from administrative overhead, but enable them to focus on deep customer discovery, modern product craft, and high-velocity execution—ultimately delivering superior customer experiences, higher-quality products, and stronger commercial value for Thomson Reuters. You will lead a small, senior team of product ops experts and carry a Direct Tax & Audit-wide change-management mandate.

Scope of the Estate

Your operational mandate spans the entire Direct Tax & Audit product landscape:

The Core Portfolio ("Bedrock"): Our market-leading, established suite of tax and accounting products.
The Agentic Stack ("Catalyst"): Our cutting-edge, agent-first platform powering experiences like CoCounsel and Ready to Review.

Key Responsibilities

AI-First Product Operations
Drive a Near-Zero-Overhead Model: Architect and run product operations where AI agents automate traditional coordination tasks—such as status reporting, dependency tracking, and cross-functional communications—allowing humans to focus on product judgment and execution.
Streamline the Product Estate: Own product operations across both the Core ("Bedrock") and Agentic ("Catalyst") portfolios, unifying them under a single, highly efficient, and modern operating rhythm.
Bridge Multi-Product Dependencies: Own the dependency seam where product commitments break. Build automated tooling and visibility systems to expose cross-team dependencies, GTM milestones, and timelines across Catalyst and Bedrock applications.
Support Modern SDLC Workflows: Ensure that all operational processes and visibility tools integrate seamlessly with our suite of modern agile and AI tools (e.g., Linear, Slack, GitHub, Claude) so that the operational backbone supports, rather than slows down, rapid engineering sprint cycles.
Partner on Migrations: Collaborate with Customer Success to integrate large-scale customer migrations smoothly into the product-ops framework without interrupting core product execution.
Define & Execute against Metrics that Matter: Move the organization away from vanity metrics toward metrics that drive the business forward. Execute a regular cadence that moves the metrics and the business.
AI Transformation across Direct Tax & Audit
Drive the AI-Maturity Roadmap: Lead Direct Tax & Audit's evolution from Level 1 AI usage (individual productivity tools) to Level 2 (shared team infrastructure: e.g., shared prompts, MCP integrations, shared skills) and toward Level 3 (agents acting on systems of record) and beyond.
Enable Modern PM Ways of Working: Use the AI-maturity transformation as the vehicle to elevate the PM craft. Lead enablement of PMs on using modern AI tools (e.g., Cursor, v0, Claude Code) and AI-first product development.
Build Shared Capability Playbooks: Establish and scale the internal playbooks (covering shared context, agentic workflows, model evaluations, and prompt libraries) that teams adopt as standard, reusable infrastructure.
Leadership, Change Management & Team Evolution
Build and Lead a High Impact Team: Recruit, mentor, and manage a high-performing, lean team of senior program-ops experts, establishing a strong operational cadence and a high bar for talent & execution.
Execute a Direct Tax & Audit -wide Mandate: Act as an influential change agent across Direct Tax & Audit, brokering alignment and operational commitments with product, engineering, and design teams outside your direct reporting line.
Drive the Transformation Drumbeat & Communications: In close partnership with the Head of Direct Tax & Audit Product and the Direct Tax & Audit Product Leadership Team, design and lead a comprehensive change-management communications strategy. Establish a regular, engaging organizational 'drumbeat' to share wins, spotlight successful AI-enabled behaviors, reinforce new ways of working, and maintain high transformation momentum across the division.

You’re a fit for this role, if your background includes:

AI-Native: You have successfully driven a real organization or department up the AI maturity curve (L1 to L2/L3). You think in terms of systemic capability and shipped outcomes, and you are highly fluent in modern AI tooling (agents, prompt engineering, MCP, evals, and prototyping).
Modern Product-Ops & SDLC Advocate: You value lean, automated systems and shared team infrastructure over traditional, heavy PMO ceremony. You understand modern software development lifecycles (SDLC) and how to design operational systems that help modern PMs, Engineers, and Designers build software faster.
Ambidextrous Operator: Equally credible and comfortable operating across complex, high-transaction legacy architectures (Bedrock) and fast-moving, agent-first modern stacks (Catalyst).
Transformational Change Leader: You are an inspiring evangelist who drives cultural and behavioral shifts by building excitement, capturing buy-in, and bringing teams along on the journey. Rather than relying on top-down mandates, you lead with influence, empathy, and positive reinforcement to align cross-functional partners around a shared vision.
Hands-on AI Fluency: You are a daily, active user of agentsand LLMs. You possess intuitive, practical knowledge of how generative AI tools can optimize a product team's day-to-day work.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in program management, product operations, or technical operations leadership at scale.
Deep familiarity with modern product management practices (ideally within modern tech, high-growth startups, or progressive B2B SaaS), with a clear understanding of how modern PM, Engineering, and Design squads collaborate.
Proven experience implementing modern agile SDLC structures and automating project-tracking workflows.
Experience in regulated or professional software industries (e.g., tax, legal, audit, finance, or compliance) where data security, accuracy, and AI governance are critical is a strong plus.
Demonstrated track record of leading change-management and communication initiatives, upskilling teams, and inspiring cultural transformations to adopt modern, technical capabilities.
Demonstrated track record of leading change management initiatives, upskilling teams, and transitioning legacy roles into modern, technical capabilities.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Business, Engineering, Management Information Systems, or a related field.

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Business, Engineering, Management Information Systems, or a related field.

What’s in it For You?

Hybrid Work Model: We’ve adopted a flexible hybrid working environment for our office-based roles while delivering a seamless experience that is digitally and physically connected.
Flexibility & Work-Life Balance: Flex My Way is a set of supportive workplace policies designed to help manage personal and professional responsibilities, whether caring for family, giving back to the community, or finding time to refresh and reset. This builds upon our flexible work arrangements, including work from anywhere for up to 8 weeks per year, empowering employees to achieve a better work-life balance.
Career Development and Growth: By fostering a culture of continuous learning and skill development, we prepare our talent to tackle tomorrow’s challenges and deliver real-world solutions. Our Grow My Way programming and skills-first approach ensures you have the tools and knowledge to grow, lead, and thrive in an AI-enabled future.
Industry Competitive Benefits: We offer comprehensive benefit plans to include flexible vacation, two company-wide Mental Health Days off, access to the Headspace app, retirement savings, tuition reimbursement, employee incentive programs, and resources for mental, physical, and financial wellbeing.
Culture: Globally recognized, award-winning reputation for inclusion and belonging, flexibility, work-life balance, and more. We live by our values: Obsess over our Customers, Compete to Win, Challenge (Y)our Thinking, Act Fast / Learn Fast, and Stronger Together.

Making a Real-World Impact: We are one of the few companies globally that helps its customers pursue justice, truth, and transparency. Together, with the professionals and institutions we serve, we help uphold the rule of law, turn the wheels of commerce, catch bad actors, report the facts, and provide trusted, unbiased information to people all over the world.

jobs.description:
Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

À propos de Crowe BGK

Depuis 75 ans, Crowe BGK S.E.N.C.R.L. est un chef de file de confiance en matière de services de comptabilité et de conseil au Canada. Notre équipe compte plus de 250 professionnels qui servent nos clients à partir de nos bureaux de Montréal et d’Ottawa. Nous offrons des services d’audit, de fiscalité, de conseil et de consultation, aidant les particuliers et les sociétés privées à relever des défis complexes. Nous sommes fiers d’avoir été nommés parmi les 100 meilleurs employeurs de PME au Canada et parmi les meilleurs employeurs de Montréal, car nous croyons qu’il est essentiel de créer un milieu de travail où les gens se sentent soutenus, valorisés et inspirés à progresser.

Nous sommes à la recherche d’un(e) Directeur(trice) Principal(e) de la Technologie et de l'Innovation

expérimenté(e) et pratique pour aider Crowe BGK à maintenir un environnement technologique fiable et à faire progresser l’utilisation des logiciels à l’échelle du cabinet. La personne retenue combinera une compréhension des processus d’affaires, une discipline opérationnelle et une expertise technologique afin d’améliorer le service à la clientèle, l’efficacité, l’évolutivité et l’expérience employé.

Vous Serez Responsable De

Stratégie et gouvernance des logiciels d’entreprise

Élaborer et maintenir la feuille de route pluriannuelle des applications du cabinet, l’inventaire des logiciels, le modèle de propriété et la gouvernance pour la sélection, les accès, les changements, les intégrations, les renouvellements et le retrait.
Identifier les lacunes en matière de capacités, les dédoublements, les outils sous-utilisés ou non pris en charge ainsi que les occasions émergentes; conseiller le ou la COFO, les associé(e)s et la direction sur les priorités, les investissements, les compromis, la normalisation et les coûts.

Amélioration des processus d’affaires et innovation

Analyser et repenser les processus dans les services à la clientèle et les fonctions corporatives, en mobilisant les parties prenantes afin de résoudre les irritants, les lacunes de contrôle, le travail à refaire, les problèmes de données et les besoins non satisfaits avant l’automatisation.
Utiliser les données et les commentaires pour prioriser les améliorations à forte valeur ajoutée et évaluer les flux de travail, l’automatisation, l’analytique, l’intelligence artificielle et les technologies émergentes en tenant compte de la confidentialité, de la qualité, des contrôles et de la supervision humaine appropriés.

Évaluation des logiciels et analyses de rentabilité

Traduire les besoins d’affaires en exigences mesurables sur les plans fonctionnel, technique, des données, de la sécurité, de l’intégration, des contrôles, du service et des utilisateurs; diriger les démonstrations, les projets pilotes, les vérifications de références, les grilles d’évaluation, la diligence raisonnable des fournisseurs et la comparaison objective des risques et des solutions de rechange.
Préparer et présenter des analyses de rentabilité pour les décisions d’aller de l’avant ou non, couvrant le coût total de possession, le rendement du capital investi, les échéanciers, les ressources, l’incidence du changement, la formation, l’atténuation des risques, le soutien et les coûts de sortie; soutenir les négociations commerciales et contractuelles.

Gouvernance et responsabilité de la mise en œuvre

Agir à titre de responsable imputable du volet affaires et technologie, en partenariat avec le ou la gestionnaire de projet attitré(e), afin de définir la portée, les résultats, le budget, les ressources, la gouvernance, les jalons, les droits décisionnels, les risques, les communications et les mesures de succès.
Coordonner les parties prenantes et veiller à la conception des processus, à la configuration, aux intégrations, à la conversion des données, aux essais, aux contrôles, à la formation, à la mise en production, au soutien, à la préparation, à la stabilisation, à l’adoption et à la réalisation des bénéfices; faire remonter les lacunes importantes et maintenir la visibilité auprès de la direction.

Gestion du portefeuille, des fournisseurs, des données et des risques

Gérer les budgets logiciels, les licences, l’utilisation, les renouvellements, les fournisseurs, les contrats, les niveaux de service, les indicateurs du portefeuille, la rationalisation et le retrait des solutions.
Collaborer avec les ressources en TI, cybersécurité, protection de la vie privée, affaires juridiques et gestion des risques afin d’encadrer les intégrations, les données, les contrôles d’accès, la continuité des activités, les risques liés aux tiers, l’intelligence artificielle et l’automatisation.

Leadership du changement et mobilisation des parties prenantes

Établir des relations de confiance avec les associé(e)s, les dirigeant(e)s, le personnel, les fournisseurs et les prestataires de services; diriger les employé(e)s attitré(e)s et les équipes interfonctionnelles en assurant une responsabilisation claire et une forte orientation vers le service.
Diriger les communications, la formation, l’adoption, la documentation, le soutien et la propriété des applications; développer des ambassadeurs internes, contribuer au plan d’affaires du cabinet et tenir le ou la COFO ainsi que les parties prenantes informés.

Autorité et responsabilité

Responsable du portefeuille de logiciels, de la feuille de route des applications, des normes de gouvernance et de la direction des équipes de mise en œuvre des TI et des processus dans le cadre de la stratégie et des budgets approuvés; peut exiger les examens appropriés en matière d’affaires, de sécurité, de protection de la vie privée, d’intégration, de contrôle et de mise en œuvre.
Recommande la sélection, le séquencement, le renouvellement, l’expansion, la consolidation ou le retrait des logiciels; peut suspendre ou faire remonter les préoccupations non résolues et est responsable de la qualité des recommandations, de la gouvernance de la mise en œuvre, de l’adoption, de la stabilisation et des bénéfices approuvés.

Mesures de succès

Gérer un inventaire à jour des logiciels, une propriété claire, une gouvernance rigoureuse, une feuille de route approuvée, des analyses de rentabilité crédibles et des dépenses contrôlées.

Role Summary

We are seeking a senior engineering and AI/ML leader to build and lead a distributed team of AI/ML engineers supporting manufacturing sites across the company. Based in Bangkok or the UK or Canada and reporting to the Chief AI Officer, this role will translate high-value manufacturing problems into reliable, scalable AI systems that improve productivity, quality, yield, equipment performance, and operational decision-making.

Lead, grow, and develop a distributed team of AI/ML engineers who work across manufacturing sites and solve site-specific operational problems.

Create a strong partnership model with plant leadership, manufacturing engineering, process engineering, yield, quality, operations, IT, and enterprise data teams.
Balance local site responsiveness with reusable platforms, common architectures, shared components, and responsible AI practices that scale across plants.

Key Responsibilities

Set and execute a multi-year roadmap for AI/ML applications in manufacturing, aligned to business priorities and measurable operational outcomes.
Identify and prioritize high-impact opportunities across process optimization, yield improvement, visual inspection, defect classification, predictive maintenance, anomaly detection, root-cause analysis, quality, scheduling, and engineering productivity.

Build and maintain strong relationships with senior manufacturing and technology leaders, communicating technical tradeoffs, risks, investment needs, and results with clarity.
Promote effective use of classical machine learning, deep learning, computer vision, optimization, statistical methods, LLMs, and generative AI where they are fit for purpose.

Job Title

AVP, Data Governance

Job Description

Pacific Life Re is progressing a major business, technology and data transformation across Divisional Business Services. The Divisional Data Team is delivering the governed data foundations, warehouse, data quality and reporting capabilities required to support Project Unify, regulatory and management reporting, operational resilience and future analytics.

The AVP, Head of Data Governance provides strategic and delivery leadership for data governance and data quality across Pacific Life Re. The role translates the Data Strategy and Data Governance and Management Program into practical standards, controls, operating practices and measurable outcomes, ensuring that data is trusted, understood, appropriately controlled and fit for operational, regulatory and strategic use.

Working across business functions, Technology, Architecture, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit and Pacific Life enterprise teams, the role embeds governance into transformation delivery, the Snowflake data warehouse, reporting and analytics, and the wider information lifecycle. A central expectation is to communicate progress, risks, dependencies, decisions and business outcomes clearly to executive sponsors, governance forums, delivery teams and data users.

This role is on-site 4 days per week and work from home 1 day per week.

Role Responsibilities

Strategy, Framework and Accountability

Lead the execution of the divisional Data Governance strategy, framework, operating model and roadmap, aligned with the PL Re Data Strategy and relevant enterprise standards.
Develop and maintain clear decision rights, accountability and escalation routes across Data Owners, Business Data Managers, Data Stewards, Business Process Owners and Technology Owners.
Chair the Data Governance Forum and ensure that decisions, actions, standards, exceptions and escalations are recorded, communicated and progressed.
Define and report measures for governance maturity, adoption, control effectiveness and the resolution of material data issues.

Program Delivery

Support the VP for Data, in delivering the Data Governance and Management Program, including mobilization, analysis, target-state design, investment planning, prioritized remediation and transition into sustainable implementation.
In collaboration with strategic projects and business workstreams, embed data requirements, definitions, ownership, quality thresholds, lineage, controls, acceptance criteria and governance sign-off throughout delivery.
Maintain an integrated delivery view of milestones, dependencies, risks, issues, resources, budgets, benefits and readiness, escalating decisions promptly and constructively.
Provide executive sponsors and governance bodies with concise, evidence-based updates on progress, outcomes, residual risks and decisions required.

Data Quality & Metadata

Develop and implement the divisional data quality strategy and operating model, covering critical data, quality rules, measures, controls, scorecards, root-cause analysis and remediation prioritization.
Lead the adoption of metadata, business glossary, lineage and data catalogue capabilities, ensuring that priority data assets are discoverable, consistently defined and supported by accountable business roles.
In collaboration with Business Analysts, Data Engineering, Reporting and Architecture, embed governance by design into data products, semantic models, workspaces and reporting solutions.
Direct the effective use and integration of strategic governance and data quality technologies, including Collibra and Informatica IDMC, with a focus on control outcomes and business adoption.

Risk, Lifecycle & Assurance

Lead data lifecycle governance, including retention, classification, discoverability, permitted access, defensible disposition and remediation of identified control gaps.
Act as the senior Data Governance contact for regulatory, audit and risk activity, coordinating evidence, management responses, remediation plans and reporting through the appropriate governance routes.
In collaboration with Legal, Data Protection, Information Security, Risk and Technology, translate policy and regulatory requirements into proportionate, implementable data controls.
Monitor material data risks and issues, challenge remediation plans and support accountable business and technology leaders in reaching documented decisions on residual risk. Working closely with legal and risk functions.

People, Engagement and Capability

Build and lead a high-performing Data Governance team, setting clear objectives, developing capability, delegating effectively and creating succession depth.
Develop and maintain an engagement and communication plan that translates governance priorities into clear executive narratives, adoption messages, training and role-based guidance.
Establish and support an active stewardship community that shares good practice, resolves cross-functional issues and embeds governance in day-to-day business activity.
Manage specialist partners and contractors against clear deliverables, quality expectations, knowledge-transfer requirements and value outcomes.

Skills & Experience

Extensive experience in data governance, data management, data quality and data leadership within a complex, regulated organization.
Demonstrable success in moving governance from policy and framework design into practical delivery, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.
Strong program and change delivery experience, with the ability to coordinate concurrent workstreams, dependencies, risks, resources and budgets.
Strong knowledge of data ownership and stewardship, metadata, business glossaries, lineage, data quality, controls, retention, classification and information lifecycle management.
Practical knowledge of governance and quality technologies, ideally Collibra, Informatica IDMC, Snowflake and Power BI.
Experience supporting regulatory reporting, audit, risk and control remediation in financial services, ideally insurance or reinsurance.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive updates, decision papers, roadmaps, program communications and adoption materials.
Strong people leadership, coaching and capability-building skills, including experience developing federated communities as well as direct teams.
Relevant professional qualification, such as CDMP or an equivalent data-management credential; recognized program, risk or change qualifications would be advantageous.

Competencies and Behaviours

Strategic and outcome-focused, with the delivery discipline to convert direction into measurable progress.
Creates clarity from complexity and connects governance, data quality, engineering, reporting, risk and change into a coherent agenda.
Visible and accountable, surfacing risks and dependencies early and following through on commitments.
Commercial and pragmatic, applying proportionate governance that protects the business without creating unnecessary delivery friction.
Collaborative and influential, building shared accountability across business and technology teams.
Communicates with precision and adapts messages for executives, delivery teams and business users.
Develops others, delegates effectively and builds sustainable organizational capability.
Demonstrates integrity, sound judgement and resilience when operating with ambiguity, scrutiny and competing priorities.

Salary: $165,000.00 – $175,000.00 CAD

Compensation Range

The compensation range noted represents the company’s good faith minimum and maximum range for this role at the time of posting. The actual compensation offered to a candidate will be dependent upon several factors, including but not limited to experience, qualifications and geographic location.

Working For Pacific Life Re

Every person in our global team is valued for the unique qualities they bring to our business and we seek to build their expertise and support their individual ambitions at every step. We work hard and thrive on achievement, but we also know how to have fun and relax too. We regularly host a range of team building days to strengthen our team's connection with each other and reflect on their successes.

jobs.description:
At eBay, we're more than a global ecommerce leader — we’re changing the way the world shops and sells. Our platform empowers millions of buyers and sellers in more than 190 markets around the world. We’re committed to pushing boundaries and leaving our mark as we reinvent the future of ecommerce for enthusiasts.

Our customers are our compass, authenticity thrives, bold ideas are welcome, and everyone can bring their unique selves to work — every day. We're in this together, sustaining the future of our customers, our company, and our planet.

Join a team of passionate thinkers, innovators, and dreamers — and help us connect people and build communities to create economic opportunity for all.

Looking for a company that inspires passion, courage and creativity, where you can be on the team shaping the future of global commerce? Want to shape how millions of people buy, sell, connect, and share around the world? If you’re interested in joining a purpose driven community that is dedicated to crafting an ambitious and inclusive work environment, join eBay – a company you can be proud to be with.

With more than 130 million active users across 190 countries and over 1 billion active product listings, eBay is the world’s most vibrant and dynamic online marketplace. Founded in 1995, eBay Inc. connects people around the world, enabling them to buy and sell online. eBay Inc. does this by providing the Internet platforms of choice for global commerce, payments and communications. eBay Inc. is headquartered in San Jose, California. For more information about the company and its global portfolio of online brands, visit www.ebayinc.com

About The Team

We are responsible for setting the strategic direction of eBay: our ambition, where we play, and how we win in the market. The team is responsible for deeply understanding the needs of our core buyers and sellers and crafting the strategies that will differentiate eBay relative to our competitors. We work very closely with product, technology, and regional business teams to ensure the strategy is translated into action across the end-to-end customer experience. Our work can be divided into 3 main topics: we develop eBay Inc’s strategy together with eBay’s executives, we run strategic projects to solve key strategic issues supporting select executives at eBay, we closely monitor the competitive environment & trends.

The opportunity

The Director, Corporate Strategy is a senior leader who will lead several cross-functional projects consisting of 2-6 Strategy Associates, Managers, and Senior Managers. You will bring both process and content leadership to strategy projects and act as the point person between Strategy and cross-functional business teams. Within this role, you will have the ability to influence key elements of eBay’s strategy and to help shape the strategic direction of eBay. The ideal candidate has a track record of making pragmatic, concrete recommendations with real world implementation experience.
