The Role

Cineflix Media is seeking a Senior Director, Enterprise Systems & AI Enablement to lead the practical implementation of our enterprise AI and technology transformation agenda.
This cross-functional role will work across the organisation to identify opportunities, modernise systems, redesign processes and embed effective AI-enabled ways of working. 

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, the Senior Director will partner closely with IT and leaders across Cineflix to translate business priorities into practical, measurable outcomes. Initial areas of focus may include Cineflix’s finance, rights management, production budgeting, payroll and planning systems, but the scope of the role extends across the organisation. This is a full-time role based in our Toronto, Ontario office on a hybrid, in-office schedule.

The Salary range for this role is CAD $150,000 - $200,000

Key Responsibilities 

Lead the implementation of Cineflix’s enterprise AI agenda across corporate and operational functions.
Identify and prioritise practical AI and automation opportunities that improve productivity, accuracy and decision-making.
Translate business requirements into scalable AI-enabled solutions and workflows.

·       Lead the development and deployment of Cineflix-owned LLM capability for internal processes, reducing reliance on external tools and ensuring solutions are tailored to Cineflix’s workflows, data, security and governance requirements.
·       Establish responsible AI practices in partnership with IT, Legal, Privacy and business leaders.
Collaborate with Creative AI leadership to align governance while maintaining clear areas of accountability.
Develop and deliver a roadmap for modernising, connecting and, where appropriate, consolidating Cineflix’s core business systems.
Improve the quality, accessibility and governance of enterprise data.
Reduce reliance on manual processes, disconnected systems and uncontrolled spreadsheets.
Lead systems integration, automation and modernisation initiatives in partnership with IT and functional leaders.
Evaluate technology partners and solutions based on business value, security, scalability and cost.
Lead the successful adoption of new systems, AI tools and redesigned processes.
Partner with business leaders and HR to support communications, training and skills development.
Help teams understand and adapt to changing roles, responsibilities and ways of working.
Build shared ownership across functions and address barriers to adoption and measure implementation progress, employee adoption and realised business benefits.

Senior experience in enterprise technology, AI enablement, business systems or digital transformation.
Demonstrated success implementing practical AI, automation and workflow solutions.
Experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation programmes.
Strong knowledge of enterprise systems, data governance, cybersecurity and vendor management.
The ability to connect business needs with practical technology solutions.
Strong stakeholder management, change leadership and communication skills.
A collaborative, pragmatic and execution-focused leadership style.
Experience in media, entertainment, production or another project-based organisation would be an asset.

The Alberta Public Service works to build a stronger province for current and future generations. We make a difference in the lives of Albertans through rewarding and diverse career opportunities.

The Ministry of Primary and Preventive Health Services (PPHS) is building a more resilient and sustainable health care system that can support Albertans getting care when and where they need it, while responding to system-wide health challenges, improving health outcomes and maintaining fiscal responsibility.

Role Responsibilities

The Primary Care Corridor Transformation team is seeking two experienced and strategic leaders to fill the positions of Director, Change Management and Director, System Planning. These positions play a key role in advancing Alberta’s primary care transformation agenda through strategic leadership, stakeholder collaboration, system planning, and change implementation. The successful candidates will lead complex initiatives that support a more integrated, accessible, and sustainable primary and preventative health care system for Albertans.

Director, Change Management

Key Responsibilities:

Lead stakeholder engagement and change management strategies that support the successful implementation of primary care transformation initiatives across Alberta.
Build and maintain strategic relationships with health system partners, government ministries, health care providers, and community stakeholders to foster collaboration and alignment.
Provide strategic advice and recommendations to senior leadership on stakeholder issues, implementation risks, emerging opportunities, and transformation priorities.
Develop and implement change management, communication, and stakeholder readiness plans that support sustainable system change.
Lead complex consultations and engagement activities to inform decision-making, build consensus, and advance government priorities.
Identify and mitigate risks, barriers, and interdependencies that may impact the successful delivery of transformation initiatives.
Provide leadership to a multidisciplinary team while fostering a collaborative, innovative, and high-performing work environment.

Director, System Planning

Key Responsibilities:

Lead the development and implementation of strategies, frameworks, and system plans that support the transformation of Alberta’s primary and preventative care system.
Assess current and emerging health system needs, service gaps, trends, and system pressures to inform planning priorities and strategic decision-making.
Provide strategic advice to senior leadership on complex health system issues, policy considerations, service delivery models, and system improvement opportunities.
Lead the development of recommendations and implementation approaches that support Primary Care Corridor Transformation initiatives.
Use data, evidence, and stakeholder input to inform planning, policy development, and decision-making.
Establish effective governance, accountability, and risk management processes to support planning activities and major initiatives.
Provide leadership to a multidisciplinary team while fostering a collaborative, innovative, and high-performing work environment.

Develop Networks

Data Science & Advanced Analytics

Team & Technical Leadership

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
About KLONDIKE

For over 35 years, KLONDIKE Lubricants has challenged the status quo to become one of Canada’s leading independent manufacturers and marketers of high-performance commercial, industrial, and automotive lubricants, greases, and specialty chemicals.

KLONDIKE manages a portfolio of more than 650 SKUs and sells exclusively through a distributor network of over 700 independent distributors across Canada and the United States. These distributors, in turn, serve a wide range of end markets including automotive, heavy-duty on-road and off-road, mining, forestry, agriculture, and industrial applications.

KLONDIKE does not sell directly to end users or mass merchandisers. This disciplined approach has allowed the company to build long-term, trust-based partnerships and consistently deliver profitable growth.

Building on its strong Canadian foundation, KLONDIKE is also in the early stages of expanding its presence in the United States. This growth is intentional and disciplined, following the same distributor-focused model that has driven success in Canada, and represents an important next chapter in the company’s long-term growth strategy.

KLONDIKE’s business model is built around one simple guiding principle: We Grow Independent Business.

This philosophy shapes how the company designs products, sets pricing, manages inventory, delivers service, and partners with distributors. KLONDIKE is positioned just below the global majors on price, while meeting or exceeding required industry specifications and certifications. The company competes on value, trust, availability, and technical credibility — not on being the cheapest option in the market.

Manufacturing and warehousing are fully outsourced to long-term strategic partners, while KLONDIKE invests heavily in inventory across six warehouses. Supply chain reliability and product availability are core competitive advantages and key drivers of distributor loyalty.

www.klondikelubricants.com

Investors

KLONDIKE Lubricants is backed by Snowdon Partners, a private equity firm focused on helping companies grow and reach their full potential.

Snowdon Partners brings a collaborative and supportive approach to value creation, providing strategic guidance, access to expertise, and additional resources to help scale the business. As part of this partnership, the finance function benefits from the perspective of an experienced Private Equity CFO, offering mentorship, strategic insight, and thought partnership while empowering the Director of Finance to lead the function and grow with the organization.

www.snowdonpartners.ca

The Role

KLONDIKE Lubricants is seeking a high caliber Director of Finance to lead and further strengthen the company’s finance function as the business continues to scale in size, complexity, and ambition. This role represents a significant leadership opportunity for a finance professional who is ready to operate at a senior level today, with a clear runway to take on broader responsibility over time.

The Director of Finance will play a central role in ensuring financial discipline, reliability, and insight across the organization, while remaining closely connected to the day-to-day financial operations of the business. This is a role for a finance leader who takes ownership, values precision, and understands the importance of strong fundamentals in enabling sustainable growth.

Who You Are

You are a finance leader who takes pride in owning the numbers and understands that credibility is built by staying closely connected to the business. You bring a naturally investigative mindset, seeking to understand the “why” behind the results, not just the outcomes. You operate comfortably across both strategic and operational levels, maintaining a strong focus on accuracy, control, and timely execution.

You bring strong technical accounting capability paired with sound business judgment. You believe that financial leadership starts with disciplined execution; timely closes, reliable reporting, and robust controls, but you also know that the real value of finance lies in enabling better decisions, managing risk, and supporting growth.

You are energized by complexity and change, and you operate effectively in environments where priorities evolve and judgment matters. You ask thoughtful questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and take ownership of outcomes rather than deferring responsibility.

You operate effectively in complex, evolving environments where priorities shift and judgment matters. You ask thoughtful questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and take ownership of outcomes rather than deferring responsibility.

You are comfortable partnering closely with the CEO and Leadership Team, providing clear insight and perspective without slowing the organization down. You communicate confidently with external lenders and support Board-level reporting with clarity and professionalism.

You are motivated by the opportunity to support a business expanding beyond Canada into the U.S. market. While grounded in strong Canadian financial fundamentals today, you view geographic expansion as an opportunity to help the business scale thoughtfully and to broaden your own exposure and impact over time.

You are comfortable operating in financially complex, inventory-intensive environments. You understand the nuances of multi-warehouse inventory accounting, high SKU counts, and product costing, and you bring experience managing foreign exchange exposure related to cross-border payables and inventory purchases. You are also comfortable supporting financial consolidation across multiple legal entities, navigating increased scale and cross-border complexity as the business grows.

You thrive in entrepreneurial, growth-oriented businesses and see runway ahead, an opportunity to grow your scope, influence and leadership impact as KLONDIKE continues to scale.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Reporting & Controls

Oversee the company’s full accounting and financial reporting function
Ensure timely and accurate month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close
Prepare and review monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements (Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow)
Develop, implement, and maintain appropriate financial controls and policies
Build and refine KPIs and management dashboards to support decision-making
Prepare annual budgets and rolling forecasts, track performance against plan
Serve as the internal source of truth for financial performance and insight

Hands-On Accounting & Cash Management

Review and verify work performed by the Controller and accounting team
Maintain active involvement in transactional accounting as required
Oversee weekly bank reconciliations and cash forecasting
Actively manage working capital, including receivables, payables, and inventory
Support working capital optimization in an inventory-intensive, multi-warehouse environment
Prepare audit support schedules and coordinate with external accountants

Lender, Board & Governance Support

Lead relationships with senior lending partners
Prepare monthly bank reporting packages and compliance metrics
Support Board reporting with clear, concise financial materials and analysis
Ensure compliance with credit agreements and governance requirements

Strategic & Operational Support

Partner with the CEO and Leadership Team on financial planning and analysis
Support long-term financial planning, scenario analysis, and forecasting
Analyze product lines, pricing, margins, inventory, and distribution economics
Evaluate investments, operational initiatives, and growth opportunities

Risk, Tax & Compliance

Oversee sales tax filings and ongoing compliance
Coordinate corporate tax filings with external advisors
Support government audits and regulatory inquiries
Manage insurance programs and periodically review coverage
Support foreign exchange exposure management related to suppliers
Own and manage the company’s foreign exchange risk, including monitoring exposure and executing an appropriate hedging policy

Systems & Process Improvement

Ensure effective integration between ERP (SAP), CRM, WMS, and accounting systems
Act as a finance lead on system enhancements and implementations
Identify opportunities to automate or streamline recurring finance processes

Team Leadership

Lead, coach, and develop the Controller and accounting team
Set clear standards for accuracy, accountability, and performance
Foster a culture of continuous improvement and professionalism
Support talent development and succession planning within the function

Your Profile

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA designation required
7+ years of progressive experience in accounting and finance, including leadership roles
Strong technical accounting foundation with solid knowledge of ASPE
Experience in distribution, manufacturing, industrial, or inventory-intensive environments is an asset
Prior exposure to private equity–backed or lender-driven environments is beneficial but not required
Demonstrated ability to operate hands-on while managing broader responsibilities
Strong organizational skills with exceptional attention to detail
Clear and confident communicator, able to present financial information to non-financial leaders
Comfortable leveraging systems and technology to improve processes
High integrity, sound judgment, and a practical, business-oriented mindset

What We Offer

A high-performance environment where you will grow and take your career to the next level
Brand new, open-concept space in Langley, with modern design and the latest communication technology
An intensely collaborative team and culture, where decision velocity and results are primary markers of success, but where people are at the heart of it all
A market-leading mindset where creative solutions are not only encouraged but rewarded
Competitive compensation including high-caliber bonus plan
Medical benefits, parking, laptop, smart phone

jobs.title: Director, AI Delivery & Portfolio Management – Global Payments Technology
jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the Opportunity?

RBC's Global Payments Technology organization is modernizing international payments infrastructure across real-time payments, cross-border transactions, debit cards, ACH, and emerging payment channels. We're now scaling AI capabilities to enhance fraud detection, optimize payment routing, improve transaction monitoring, and drive operational efficiency across our global payments ecosystem.

We're seeking an exceptional delivery leader to orchestrate multiple large AI programs within Global Payments Technology while establishing AI-native delivery practices that respect the security, compliance, and reliability demands of mission-critical payments systems.

As Director, AI Delivery & Portfolio Management – Global Payments Technology, you will lead a strategic portfolio of AI initiatives across research, engineering, platform, and business teams. You will drive alignment across complex programs, champion modern AI delivery methodologies, and ensure program management evolves to embrace AI's iterative nature while maintaining stringent operational and regulatory standards.

Reporting to the Senior Director, Program Delivery, you will own end-to-end delivery accountability for this strategic AI portfolio while establishing AI SDLC standards that shape how RBC delivers AI solutions for payments at scale.

What will you do?

Program & Portfolio Leadership

Lead delivery on multiple concurrent AI initiatives focused on payments innovation (fraud detection, payment routing optimization, transaction monitoring, operational efficiency) with high complexity, uncertainty, and strategic value
Manage portfolio-level roadmaps, dependencies, and resource allocation across payments-focused AI programs
Own end-to-end delivery accountability from planning through production deployment and value realization for each initiative, ensuring seamless integration with RBC's global payments infrastructure
Develop and maintain program roadmaps, milestones, dependency plans, and execution strategies aligned with business objectives and approved timelines, budgets, and scope
Coordinate activities across AI Research, AI Solutions Engineering, platform teams, payments operations, governance partners, and business stakeholders across international payments, debit cards, ACH, RTR, and payment channel teams

Payments Domain Expertise & AI SDLC Development

Maintain strong understanding of Global Payments Technology domain: international payments flows, debit card processing, ACH, Real-Time Payments (RTR/FedNow), SWIFT, cross-border settlement, and emerging payment channels
Champion the evolution and operationalization of AI-native software development lifecycle practices tailored to payments systems, where reliability, security, and regulatory compliance are non-negotiable
Establish standards and processes that reflect the unique characteristics of AI development in payments (model development, experimentation, data pipelines, validation, monitoring, fraud pattern evolution)
Influence engineering teams and stakeholders toward adoption of modern AI delivery practices including continuous training, model governance, MLOps, production monitoring, and explainability requirements critical to payments
Balance traditional delivery discipline with the iterative, experimental nature of AI development; advise teams on risk-based approaches to AI model validation and deployment in payments contexts
Drive knowledge sharing across programs on AI SDLC best practices, payments-specific lessons learned, and regulatory considerations

Cross-Functional Team Leadership

Foster a culture of ownership, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement across diverse technical teams (data scientists, ML engineers, platform engineers, payments domain experts, infrastructure teams, and business partners)
Build trusted relationships across business, engineering, platform, payments operations, compliance, and governance functions; serve as the primary delivery point of contact for senior stakeholders
Lead large cross-functional teams and influence stakeholders across business and technology organizations within Global Payments Technology
Coach delivery leads and team members on program management best practices tailored to AI initiatives in payments; share payments domain knowledge across delivery teams
Work effectively with Global Payments business partners, payment network providers (networks, central banks, regulators), and third-party payment solution providers

Delivery Execution & Governance

Establish effective governance processes including status reviews, risk management, issue resolution, and executive reporting that account for payments-specific compliance and operational requirements
Monitor initiative health through delivery metrics, OKRs, KPIs, and operational dashboards; maintain performance visibility and accountability
Identify and proactively resolve delivery bottlenecks, technical dependencies, organizational challenges, and AI-specific risks (model performance, data quality, fairness, regulatory compliance, payment accuracy, fraud evolution)
Anticipate and quantify tactical, operational, and strategic risks specific to payments (transaction volume spikes, regulatory changes, network disruptions); apply risk-based approaches to forecasting and mitigation
Manage program-level communications including status reports, executive updates, steering committee materials, and regulatory/compliance reporting as required
Ensure delivery teams maintain rigorous quality assurance and testing standards appropriate to mission-critical payments systems

Technical Leadership & Stakeholder Management

Develop strong understanding of AI solution architecture for payments, data ecosystems, platform capabilities, and operational requirements supporting payments initiatives
Partner with engineering leaders, architects, product teams, payments domain experts, data governance partners, and compliance teams to understand technical requirements, constraints, and delivery dependencies
Translate technical AI concepts into clear business language and payments-specific business requirements into actionable delivery plans
Balance business priorities, technical quality, delivery timelines, and payments-specific considerations (security, compliance, SLA requirements) when supporting implementation decisions
Manage stakeholder expectations through transparent communication and proactive management of complex, high-pressure situations inherent in payments technology
Ensure technical risks are identified, communicated, and mitigated throughout the delivery lifecycle, with particular attention to payments system stability and data security

Resource, Risk & Financial Management

Manage initiative budgets, forecasts, resource plans, and vendor engagements across the payments AI portfolio
Ensure effective utilization of resources while balancing delivery commitments and organizational priorities
Track financial performance and value realization against approved business cases; drive ROI visibility and accountability
Identify, communicate, and mitigate risks impacting timelines, scope, quality, or business outcomes, including payments-specific operational and regulatory risks
Drive timely issue resolution and escalation management; facilitate decision-making to maintain delivery momentum while protecting payment system integrity

What do you need to succeed?

Must have:

10+ years of experience managing large and complex transformation programs or technology initiatives
Strong understanding of payments domain (international payments, debit cards, ACH, RTR, cross-border settlement, or related payment channels) OR proven ability to quickly master complex domain requirements
Strong understanding of AI/ML software delivery lifecycle, Agile methodologies, modern engineering practices
Expert knowledge of program and project plan development & management, scheduling methodology, and program metrics/analysis
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving capabilities with demonstrated ability to lead and influence large cross-functional teams across business and technology organizations
Experience managing program-level budgets, delivery plans, risks, dependencies, and executive communications

Nice to have:

Demonstrated experience leading technology delivery in payments, financial services, or similarly regulated/mission-critical environments
Background as a software engineer, data engineer, ML engineer, payments engineer, or distinguished engineer who transitioned into delivery leadership
Experience driving cultural transformation and organizational change in payments or technology organizations
Proven people management skills and ability to retain top technical talent

What's in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses, flexible benefits, competitive compensation, and stock where applicable

Job Description

You will be working on a flexible hybrid schedule as part of Fidelity’s dynamic working arrangement.

The work location for this role is 483 Bay Street in Toronto until approximately late 2026, when the work location will change to the new Mississauga office at 3 Robert Speck Parkway.

Current work authorization for Canada is required for all openings.

At Fidelity, we’ve been helping Canadian investors build better financial futures for over 35 years. We offer individuals and institutions a range of trusted investment portfolios and services - and we’re constantly seeking to find new and better ways to help our clients. As a privately owned company, we boldly embrace innovation in all areas as we continue to grow our business into the future.

Working with us means you’ll be part of a diverse and dedicated group of people who make a real difference for our clients and communities every day. You’ll have a wide range of opportunities to grow and develop your career in an inclusive environment where you’ll feel valued and supported to be your best - both personally and professionally.

How You’ll Make An Impact

The Director, Product Strategy and Commercialization will lead the commercial strategy for Fidelity’s digital investing platform, ensuring the Investly product roadmap, go-to-market priorities, incentives, lifecycle programs and client value proposition are directly tied to measurable business outcomes. Working within their team and cross-functionally, they will be accountable for translating the Investly vision into a prioritized growth agenda that supports funded investor growth, AUM growth, revenue generation, margin improvement, client lifetime value and long-term P&L performance.

They will own the commercial planning discipline for Investly, including business case development, roadmap prioritization, experimentation, commercialization planning, incentive optimization, feedback collection, partner alignment and performance management against agreed business targets.

Within the team, the Director, Product Strategy and Commercialization will establish, maintain and iterate the operating cadence, goals and metric framework required to run Investly with stronger commercial discipline. They will ensure team members and cross-functional partners understand how their work contributes to growth, revenue, cost efficiency, client outcomes, enterprise value and P&L performance.

Own the commercial strategy, business planning and P&L accountability framework for Investly, including the strategic plan, business cases and performance targets that guide product and growth decisions.
Own the commercialization programme for priority growth initiatives, coordinating cross-functional execution and ensuring initiatives deliver against agreed business outcomes.
Translate customer, market and performance insights into product, commercialization and lifecycle priorities that improve user experience and drive profitable growth.
Champion a data-informed, user-centric and commercially disciplined approach to product strategy, commercialization and P&L performance.
Build and lead a high-performing team that aligns with Fidelity’s values and that collaborates well in cross-functional environments Collaborate with Digital Client Experience, Product Managers, Investly, Incentive Managers and cross-functionally with Business Development, Social Media, Data Analytics, Finance, Risk, Compliance and Marketing to deliver customer-centric, compliant and financially sound outcomes.

Degree in Business, Software or a related field/equivalent experience

3+ years of experience managing and growing a high-performing team

Experience building business cases, performance scorecards and commercialization plans tied to measurable financial and growth outcomes

Planning and Delivery

Reporting to the Managing Director, you will partner with investment teams and enterprise stakeholders to optimize external data sourcing, vendor relationships, and commercial outcomes. You will lead a team of market data professionals while driving transparency, operational excellence, and value across the firm's external data investments.

The Team

Technology & Operations enables CPP Investments to deliver on its global investment mandate by providing secure, innovative, and data-driven technology capabilities. The department partners across the organization to deliver trusted data, modern platforms, and strategic technology services that enhance investment decision-making and operational excellence.

The Data Scouting team is responsible for the strategy, sourcing, governance, and commercial management of external data across CPP Investments. Working closely with investment teams and enterprise partners, the team ensures external data is accessible, cost-effective, and aligned with business priorities while maximizing the value of the firm's data investments.

Accountabilities

Develop and execute the strategy for CPP Investments' external data portfolio, ensuring data products align with evolving business needs while improving value, transparency, and portfolio efficiency.
Provide strategic advice to investment teams and enterprise stakeholders on external data sourcing, vendor capabilities, and commercial models to support informed investment decisions.
Lead the evaluation, negotiation, and management of complex third-party data contracts, ensuring commercial value, consistency, compliance, and effective risk management.
Build and manage strategic relationships with external data providers, driving vendor performance, governance, innovation, and long-term partnership value.
Identify opportunities to optimize external data spend through portfolio rationalization, contract consolidation, product substitution, and disciplined cost management.
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing team while fostering a collaborative, inclusive culture focused on continuous improvement and professional growth.

Job Description:

Reporting to the Vice-President, HR Business Partner, Digital, Client Experience and Operations Transformation, the AVP, Program Management & Transformation is a senior leadership role responsible for translating the people and workplace transformation agenda into coordinated, measurable execution across a complex portfolio of business, technology and operations teams.

The role is the central orchestration point for priority people and workplace transformations. It establishes the plans, governance, management routines and cross-functional accountability required to move work from strategy to sustained delivery, while connecting workforce planning, organizational effectiveness, employee experience, data, talent and change.

This is a high-impact role for a pragmatic executive leader who combines transformation expertise, disciplined program management, organizational judgment and strong influence without authority.

Please note this role requires regular presence at our Toronto One York office

What will you do:

Transformation Program Leadership & Enterprise Delivery

Lead integrated execution across the portfolio's highest-priority workplace transformation programs, translating strategy into actionable plans with clear outcomes, ownership, milestones and value measures.
Act as the drumbeat behind delivery, maintaining momentum week over week and proactively identifying risks, dependencies, resource constraints and decisions before they become barriers.
Coordinate senior leaders, HRBPs, Centres of Expertise, Finance, Talent Acquisition, Data and Analytics, Technology and business workstream owners to align priorities and resolve blockers without direct authority.
Establish fit-for-purpose governance, decision forums, risk registers, integrated roadmaps and escalation paths that accelerate execution while preserving appropriate people and risk considerations.
Monitor progress against strategic commitments and provide executive-level recommendations on priorities, trade-offs and interventions required.

OKR Governance, Performance & Measurement

Design and lead a connected OKR governance approach spanning Canadian business units, functions and HR, with clear standards, cadences, ownership and escalation mechanisms.
Connect OKRs to the enterprise metrics agenda and performance culture, building the capability and tools leaders need to set high-quality objectives and use data to improve performance.
Define value measures across workstreams, integrating workforce, organizational health, employee experience and business indicators into a trusted view of delivery.
Develop executive dashboards, portfolio reviews and management routines that create transparency, surface root causes and drive timely corrective action.

Workforce Strategy & People Process Alignment

Lead cross-business workforce planning grounded in labour supply and demand, capability gaps and build-versus-buy choices, with short-, medium- and long-term talent requirements.
Partner with HRBPs, Talent Acquisition and Finance to assess hiring pipeline health, fill-rate risks and talent investment effectiveness, and sponsor targeted improvement initiatives.
Align role, level, compensation and talent evaluation approaches to external technology and AI markets while maintaining enterprise consistency.
Integrate workforce transition and capability-building plans into transformation roadmaps, connecting the work to enterprise Talent mechanisms.

Employee Experience, Change & Ways of Working

Embed employee experience and data and analytics into program design, using evidence to understand workforce needs, anticipate friction and improve adoption and outcomes.
Lead the change approach for complex transformations, including stakeholder segmentation, communications, readiness, transition support and sustained adoption.
Assess the cumulative impact of change on leaders, teams and HR, and sequence work to protect delivery capacity, employee trust and business continuity.
Advance new ways of working across the Canadian organization, simplifying how work moves across organizational boundaries and strengthening accountability, pace and collaboration.

Executive Partnership & Organizational Enablement

Serve as a trusted advisor to the VP HRBP and senior business and HR leaders, bringing structured problem solving, sound judgment and a clear enterprise perspective to ambiguous issues.
Define effective connection points with Strategy and Enablement, Employee Experience, Data and Analytics, Talent and other HR capabilities so accountability is clear and work is integrated end to end.
Prepare concise, decision-oriented materials for the VP HRBP, CHRO, senior leadership and governance forums, translating complex work into clear implications and recommendations.
Facilitate cross-functional working sessions that align leaders, accelerate decisions and convert insight into action.
Lead and develop a high-performing team and project community while promoting collaboration, inclusion and continuous improvement.

What Do You Need To Succeed

10+ years of progressive experience in transformation, enterprise program leadership, strategy execution, organizational effectiveness, consulting, HR transformation or a related field.
Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional transformation programs in a large, matrixed organization, with measurable results and sustained adoption.
Strong program and portfolio management capability, including integrated planning, governance, dependency and risk management, value realization and executive reporting.
Experience shaping workforce strategy, organizational change and people transformation across business, technology and operations environments.
Proven ability to influence VP- and SVP-level stakeholders, navigate competing priorities and drive accountability without direct authority.
Experience with OKRs, performance measurement, employee experience and data-informed decision-making, combined with an understanding of AI-enabled transformation.
Post-secondary education in a related discipline or equivalent experience.

Leadership Profile

The successful candidate will be:

A pragmatic transformation leader who turns strategy into action, pace and measurable outcomes.
A systems thinker who can connect strategy, workforce, performance, employee experience, data and change.
A disciplined operator who creates clarity, anticipates dependencies and follows through on commitments.
A trusted advisor with the judgment and executive presence to influence senior leaders and resolve difficult trade-offs.
A data-driven decision-maker who uses evidence to diagnose issues, measure progress and recommend interventions.
An exceptional communicator who simplifies complexity and creates clear, decision-oriented narratives.
A collaborative people leader who develops talent and models accountability, inclusion and continuous improvement.

You will manage the preparation and review of client quarterly, semi-annual and annual financial statements, regulatory filings and other periodic reporting by our staff and our offshore teams. You will engage with clients, auditors and other State Street teams to resolve issues and answer inquiries to ready client financial statements and filings for finalization.

Why this role is important to us

The team you will be joining is a part of State Street Global Services (SSGS). SSGS gives asset owners and managers access to the essential financial tools they need to deliver effective investment solutions. From core custody, accounting, fund administration and shareholder recordkeeping, to complete operations solutions and servicing for alternative assets like OTC derivatives, private equity and real estate, SSGS’ tools help our clients make better investment choices and act on growth opportunities.

Join us if making your mark in the financial services industry from day one is a challenge you are up for.

What You Will Be Responsible For

As Financial Reporting, Assistant Vice President you will

Manage a diverse group of personnel involved in the preparation of interim / annual financial statements for alternative investments products (e.g. hedge, private equity, real estate, fund of funds, business development companies).
Lead, direct and manage the department in collaboration with your manager and senior colleagues
Act as the primary point of escalation for clients with responsibility for implementing and supporting the service requirements of the various client relationships serviced within the group
Work internally in allocating clients and resources within the team
Collaborate with the clients and colleagues globally as appropriate to service clients and/or projects
Responsible for the effective recruitment, training, development and retention of a team of managers who are responsible for meeting their client’s financial reporting needs and effectively managing their team members
Develop and retain personal and team talent.
Act as a source of technical support and guidance to the team, other State Street internal teams and the client. This includes reviewing of files prepared by the teams.
Work with other members of the team in setting individual and team targets and priorities; maintain high standards of client service; conduct performance appraisals and give feedback on individual and team performance
Effective messaging and communication
Participate in team specific and department wide projects as required from time to time
Perform other duties as required in order to meet client and department deliverables/goals

What We Value

These skills will help you succeed in this role

Experience managing a team.
Ability to develop business relationships, both within and outside of the organization. Excellent interpersonal, organizational and communication skills.
Demonstrates an ability to be a leader on their team, as well as be a leader amongst your peers in the department.
Knowledge of Securities Exchange Commission (SEC), Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) requirements and laws as they apply to investment companies, Trusts, Partnerships and other fund structures.
Ability to effectively handle and resolve numerous ongoing communications and reporting deliverables in fast paced environment.
Ability to drive change and process improvements, while managing day-to-day activities in a reporting cycle.
Ability to communicate effectively with clients regarding their financial statements, regulatory disclosures and process improvements (standardization of disclosures and automation).
Ability to effectively manage a team of professionals, planning out work and resource allocation. Provide feedback and development.

Education & Preferred Qualifications

BS degree in Accounting, Business, or related field. CPA or MBA is preferred.
Six or more years of experience in alternative funds fund administration function (financial reporting preferred) or accounting, audit or related business activity.

About State Street

What we do.
State Street is one of the largest custodian banks, asset managers and asset intelligence companies in the world. From technology to product innovation we’re making our mark on the financial services industry. For more than two centuries, we’ve been helping our clients safeguard and steward the investments of millions of people. We provide investment servicing, data & analytics, investment research & trading and investment management to institutional clients.

Work, Live and Grow.
We make all efforts to create a great work environment. Our benefits packages are competitive and comprehensive. Details vary in locations, but you may expect generous medical care, insurance and savings plans among other perks. You’ll have access to flexible Work Program to help you match your needs. And our wealth of development programs and educational support will help you reach your full potential.

Inclusion, Diversity and Social Responsibility.
We truly believe our employees’ diverse backgrounds, experiences and perspective are a powerful contributor to creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive and reach their maximum potential while adding value to both our organization and our clients. Another fundamental value at State Street is active engagement with our communities around the world, both as a partner and a leader. jobs.description:
Choose a workplace that empowers your impact.

Join a global workplace where employees thrive. One that embraces diversity of thought, expertise and experience. A place where you can personalize your employee journey to be — and deliver — your best.

We are a purpose-driven, dynamic and sustainable pension plan. An industry leading global investor with teams in Toronto to London, New York, Singapore, Sydney and other major cities across North America and Europe. We embody the values of our 665,000 members, placing their best interests at the heart of everything we do.

Join us to accelerate your growth & development, prioritize wellness, build connections, and support the communities where we live and work.

Don’t just work anywhere — come build tomorrow together with us.

Know someone at OMERS or Oxford Properties?
Great! If you're referred, have them submit your name through Workday first. Then, watch for a unique link in your email to apply.

The Associate Director, Internal Audit provides both strategic leadership and hands-on execution across pension operations and technology-focused audit and project assurance activities. Our Pension system modernization and automation has been critical to keeping pace with the service requirements of our growing membership base and is a critical strategic objective to support our OMERS 2030 strategy. This role bridges audit delivery with advisory leadership, overseeing high-impact, risk-based audits while providing consultative guidance on governance, risk management, and control environments across both the operations and technology in Pensions. The role works closely with senior leaders across the business, technology, and second-line oversight functions, and supports the Director and IA leadership in shaping audit strategy, identifying emerging risks, and strengthening the overall risk management and control framework.

You Will Be Responsible For

Audit, Risk & Control Leadership & Execution:

Lead the planning, execution, and reporting of risk-based audit engagements across financial, operational and strategic domains, primarily in Pension Operations and Technology.
Lead project assurance engagements focused on reviewing of technology transformations and IT risk assessments, including evaluation of system development, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and application controls in multiple environments: in-house developed platforms, SaaS and “on prem” applications.
Develop engagement objectives, audit approaches, scopes, and timelines aligned with organizational strategy, risk appetite, and regulatory expectations.
Identify control gaps, assess root causes, validate remediation plans, and support residual risk acceptance where appropriate

Stakeholder Engagement & Advisory

Cultivate strong relationships with senior business partners in pensions and technology to understand processes, risks, and control environments.
Serve as a key liaison during audits and risk engagements, providing timely insights, practical recommendations, and ongoing status updates.
Translate audit and technology risk issues into clear, business-focused language for executive and senior management audiences.
Collaborate closely with Corporate Oversight functions (e.g., Compliance & Ethics, Enterprise Risk partners) to ensure consistent and effective risk management approaches.

Reporting, Insights & Follow-Up

Deliver clear, balanced, and actionable audit reports ingrained with recommendations based on root cause analysis and risk assessments for senior management and Board committees.
Partner with management to develop effective, sustainable action plans and monitor timely remediation of findings.
Develop reporting, metrics, and dashboards to highlight control effectiveness, emerging risks, and thematic issues.

Strategic Planning & Methodology

Assist IA leadership in identifying emerging risks, developing the annual audit plan, and optimizing audit methodologies, including agile, AI and data-driven audit approaches.
Contribute to the development and maintenance of the audit universe and help ensure alignment with organizational strategy and goals and regulatory requirements (where applicable).
Support the development of the annual audit plan.
Apply and promote leading practices and regulatory frameworks (e.g., COBIT, ISO, NIST, FFIEC, PCI, ITIL, agile audit methodologies).
Advance the use of data analytics, automation, artificial intelligence and technology-enabled audit techniques.

Leadership, Culture & Capability Building

Mentor, coach, and develop audit professionals, building deep technical, analytical, and stakeholder management capabilities across the IA team.
Support continuous improvement initiatives, including training, methodology enhancements, and innovation within the audit function.
Promote risk awareness and strong control discipline across the organization through formal and informal engagement.

Required Skills & Experience

University degree in accounting, finance, business, information technology, or a related field.
Professional designation preferred: CPA, CIA, and CISA, CISSP or other relevant designation considered an asset.
Significant progressive experience (typically 8+ years) in internal or external audit, technology risk or assurance.
Experience with audit and risk analytics, reporting tools, and audit management software (e.g., TeamMate, Diligent, Resolver, ACL or equivalent).
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to assess complex, interrelated processes.
Proven leadership and influencing skills, with comfort engaging senior executives and diverse stakeholder groups.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present concise, executive-ready materials.
Demonstrated ability to balance assurance, advisory, and delivery responsibilities in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
Experience with audit and risk analytics, reporting tools, and audit management software (e.g., TeamMate, Diligent, Resolver, ACL or equivalent).

Preferred Skills & Experiences

Pension Plan Administration Certificate (PPAC) is considered an asset.
Working knowledge of regulatory and control frameworks such as COBIT, ISO 27001, NIST Cybersecurity Framework, ITIL, and related standards.
Ability to interpret data queries (e.g. SQL) and leverage analytics to support data driven audit and risk insights.
Proficiency in AI prompting would be an asset.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

The expected salary range for this position is $122,000.00 - $188,000.00 per year.

You may also be eligible to receive an annual Incentive Award pursuant to our Short-term Incentive plan and our Long-Term Incentive plan (if applicable), and to participate in our group benefits and retirement plans – details on these elements of compensation are included within OMERS & Oxford offer letters.

As one of Canada’s largest defined benefit pension plans, our people-first culture is at its best when our workforce reflects the communities where we live and work — and the members we proudly serve.

From hire to retire, we are an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment and selection process that extends all the way through your employee experience. This sense of belonging and connection is cultivated up, down and across our global organization thanks to our vast network of Employee Resource Groups with executive leader sponsorship, our Purpose@Work committee and employee recognition programs.

jobs.description:
Head of Digital

This is a full-time, in-office position based at INK Entertainment's Head Office in the heart of Yorkville. We believe our best ideas come from collaboration, creativity, and being together, which is why this role works primarily from our Toronto headquarters, partnering closely with teams across our restaurants, nightlife venues, live events, and entertainment brands.

Build the Future of Hospitality, Entertainment & Live Experiences.

At INK Entertainment
, we don't just open restaurants or produce events—we create destinations, experiences, and brands that people remember.

From award-winning restaurants and nightlife venues to concerts, festivals, and cultural experiences, INK is redefining hospitality and entertainment across North America. Its restaurant portfolio includes Amal (Toronto, Miami & Fort Lauderdale), Byblos (Toronto & Miami), Daphne, Figo, Level 6 (Miami), Beso by Patria, Sofia Yorkville, Sofia Design District (Miami), Primadonna, Vinny, Honey Chinese, Melani, STORYS Building, Portland Room and its premium QSR concept Little Baba. INK also operates trendsetting nightlife destinations, including REBEL, Cabana, and DPRTMNT. The company represents Taglialatella Galleries in Toronto, New York, and Paris, and produces Canada’s largest electronic music festival, VELD, now entering its 14th consecutive year.

We're looking for a visionary Head of Digital
to lead the next evolution of our digital ecosystem and transform how millions of guests discover, engage with, and experience our brands. If you're equally passionate about technology, creativity, customer experience, data, and culture, this is an opportunity to shape one of Canada's most dynamic hospitality and entertainment companies.

As Head of Digital, you'll lead the digital strategy across INK's portfolio of restaurants, nightlife venues, concerts, festivals, hospitality brands, and corporate initiatives.
You'll own the digital roadmap—from websites and CRM to paid media, SEO, marketing technology, AI, analytics, and digital customer experiences. You'll partner with leaders across Marketing, Operations, Creative, Brand Partnerships, PR, Events, and Technology to drive measurable business growth while building exceptional digital experiences.
You'll also lead and mentor our digital team, including Social Media, ensuring every digital touchpoint reflects the creativity and innovation that defines INK.

What You'll Own:

Digital Strategy

Define and execute INK's enterprise digital strategy across hospitality, entertainment, music, and live events.
Identify emerging technologies and consumer trends that create competitive advantage.
Lead digital transformation initiatives that improve customer experience and business performance.
Build the roadmap for future digital growth.

Customer Growth

Grow reservations, ticket sales, memberships, loyalty, gift card sales, and online revenue.
Develop CRM, email, SMS, and lifecycle marketing strategies that increase customer acquisition, retention, and lifetime value.
Optimize every step of the digital customer journey.

Digital Marketing

Lead paid media strategy across Google, Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, Reddit, Spotify, and emerging platforms.
Oversee SEO, digital advertising, audience acquisition, conversion optimization, and performance marketing.
Manage agency relationships and media investments to maximize ROI.

Digital Experiences

Oversee the strategy and evolution of INK's websites, ticketing experiences, reservation platforms, and digital products.
Ensure every digital experience is intuitive, accessible, mobile-first, and conversion-focused.
Champion innovation using AI, automation, personalization, and emerging technology.

Music, Live Events & Brand Partnerships

Develop digital marketing strategies that drive awareness and ticket sales for concerts, festivals, nightlife programming, and live experiences.
Partner with artists, promoters, venues, agencies, and brand partners to amplify campaigns across digital channels.
Support sponsorship activations with measurable digital strategies that create value for partners and unforgettable experiences for guests.

Analytics & Innovation

Turn data into action through reporting, attribution, experimentation, and optimization.
Build executive dashboards and performance insights that influence business decisions.
Continuously test, learn, and improve.

Who You Are:

You're a strategic digital leader who thrives in fast-paced, creative environments. You know how to balance brand storytelling with performance marketing, and you're as comfortable discussing customer acquisition costs as you are envisioning the next big digital experience.
You bring curiosity, commercial thinking, and a passion for innovation—and you're excited to help shape what's next.

What You'll Bring:

8+ years of progressive digital marketing experience, including leadership experience.
Experience in hospitality, entertainment, live events, music, lifestyle, retail, or consumer brands.
Expertise across paid media, SEO, CRM, marketing automation, analytics, websites, and digital strategy.
Experience leading multi-brand digital ecosystems.
Strong understanding of audience growth, customer acquisition, digital commerce, and lifecycle marketing.
Experience managing agencies, budgets, and cross-functional teams.
Knowledge of ticketing platforms, event marketing, sponsorship activations, or entertainment marketing is a strong asset.
Familiarity with Google Analytics 4, Google Ads, Meta Ads Manager, TikTok Ads, CRM platforms (including Tradable Bits), CMS platforms, AI marketing tools, and marketing technology ecosystems.

Why INK?

This isn't a traditional hospitality marketing role.
You'll help shape some of Canada's most recognized restaurants, nightlife venues, music experiences, festivals, and entertainment brands while working alongside some of the industry's most creative minds.
You'll have the freedom to build, innovate, challenge convention, and make a measurable impact on a growing portfolio of iconic brands.
If you're ready to redefine what digital looks like in hospitality and entertainment, we'd love to meet you.

The salary range for this role is $100,000 to $120,000 CAD per year, plus benefits.
The final offer will be based on a variety of factors, including relevant experience, skills, education, and market considerations.

Diversity, Equity & Inclusion

At INK Entertainment
, we believe that great experiences are created by diverse teams and unique perspectives. We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where every employee feels welcomed, respected, empowered, and supported to do their best work.
We celebrate diversity in all its forms and encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds, identities, experiences, and abilities.
We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to providing an accessible and inclusive recruitment process in accordance with the Ontario Human Rights Code and the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). If you require accommodation at any stage of the hiring process, please let us know and we will work with you to meet your needs.

Business Intelligence
Location:
Toronto, ON

CA$145,000 - CA$165,000 / year

Description

The Senior Director, Business Intelligence and Analytics is a senior enterprise leader responsible for building and leading GS1 Canada’s business intelligence, analytics, and market insight capability. The role gives the organization a clear, trusted, and evidence-based view of strategic performance, subscriber growth and retention, product and service adoption, sector opportunity, and emerging market dynamics.

The role leads a team of analysts and market intelligence professionals who measure organizational performance, identify growth opportunities, assess subscriber and sector trends, and translate data into clear recommendations for senior leadership. The function will move beyond traditional reporting toward predictive, decision-oriented analytics that explain what is happening, why it matters, what is likely to happen next, and where action is required.

A central mandate is to transform the analytics function through the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence. This leader will establish the roadmap, operating model, capabilities, and governance needed to embed AI into analytical workflows; improve the speed, quality, and reach of insight; and equip the team and business leaders to use AI effectively and responsibly.

The role translates GS1 Canada’s enterprise strategy into measurable outcomes, owns the enterprise KPI and performance framework, and ensures executives and business leaders receive timely, consistent, and decision-ready insight. It partners closely with Product, Subscriber Management, Finance, Marketing, Industry Relations, Community Engagement, Technology, Operations, Data Governance, Privacy, Cybersecurity, and the AI Council.

This is a high-impact, enterprise-facing leadership role requiring analytical judgment, strategic thinking, executive communication, change leadership, people development, and

Key Responsibilities

Build and Lead the Business Intelligence and Analytics Function
Build, lead, and mature GS1 Canada’s business intelligence and analytics capability, including enterprise reporting, subscriber and sector analytics, product and service usage analytics, market intelligence, and growth insights.
Establish a trusted and consistent single version of the truth by aligning data definitions, metrics, dashboards, and reports across business units
Lead enterprise dashboards, executive scorecards, and recurring insight products covering subscriber growth, retention, churn, adoption, engagement, service usage, sector penetration, revenue performance, and strategic execution.
Advance the function from descriptive reporting to diagnostic, predictive, and prescriptive insight that identifies drivers, anticipates risks and opportunities, and recommends action.
Establish standards for analytical quality, metric definitions, dashboard governance, documentation, reproducibility, and executive communication.
Partner with Technology, Data Governance, and business teams to improve data accessibility, quality, reliability, and fitness for analytical and AI use.

Lead Subscriber, Sector and Market Intelligence
Build an integrated intelligence capability that combines subscriber and operational data, sector insight, competitive intelligence, and external market trends.
Monitor changes in subscriber expectations, digital and agentic commerce, product data management, regulation, sustainability, 2D barcode adoption, AI-enabled data management, and other developments affecting GS1 Canada’s relevance and growth.
Synthesize quantitative and qualitative signals from sector boards, working groups, subscriber interactions, support channels, research, and industry forums in partnership with relevant business teams.
Identify enterprise-wide patterns and sector-specific needs, and provide regular executive briefings on market shifts, subscriber expectations, competitors, opportunities, and strategic risks.
Recommend where insights indicate a need to adjust strategic focus, product priorities, positioning, education, or market engagement.

Own the Enterprise KPI and Measurement Framework
Define and maintain the enterprise KPI framework, aligned to strategy, subscriber value, growth, adoption, financial performance, and operational outcomes.
Set consistent definitions and ownership for core measures, including subscriber growth, retention, churn, engagement, adoption, product and service usage, sector penetration, revenue trends, and strategic progress
Partner with Finance and functional leaders to ensure measures are reliable, decision-useful, and consistently applied across executive, functional, and sector reporting.
Identify gaps or inconsistencies in measurement and recommend improvements to data, instrumentation, reporting, and accountability.
Focus leadership attention on the few measures that matter most, connecting activity to subscriber outcomes, growth impact, and strategic value.

Lead the AI-Enabled Transformation of Analytics
Develop and execute a multi-year roadmap to transform the analytics function through AI, aligned with enterprise strategy, the AI Council, and GS1 Canada’s technology and data priorities.
Prioritize high-value use cases such as automated data preparation and reporting, insight synthesis, anomaly detection, forecasting, segmentation, churn and propensity analysis, and conversational or self-service analytics.
Redesign analyst workflows and roles to combine automation with human judgment, enabling the team to spend less time producing reports and more time interpreting results, advising leaders, and driving action.
Establish a disciplined path from experimentation to production, including use-case intake, value assessment, pilots, validation, adoption planning, controls, and scaling.
Partner with Technology and Data Governance on approved tools, architecture, secure data access, semantic models, data quality, integration, and production support; retain business ownership of analytical use cases, adoption, and outcomes.
Partner with the AI Council, Privacy, Legal, Cybersecurity, and Data Governance to ensure appropriate human oversight, transparency, confidentiality, intellectual property protection, bias testing, accuracy, and responsible use
Build team capability in AI-assisted analysis, prompt and context design, model limitations, validation, documentation, and effective human review.
Measure transformation value through adoption, time-to-insight, productivity, analytical quality, decision impact, and measurable business outcomes.

Provide Executive and Board-Level Insight
Prepare executive and Board materials that clearly communicate strategic progress, performance trends, subscriber outcomes, growth opportunities, and emerging risks.
Translate complex analysis into concise narratives that connect metrics to strategy, market conditions, implications, and decisions required.
Support executive decision-making by identifying the most important insights, dependencies, risks, options, and recommended actions.
Serve as a trusted enterprise advisor by providing balanced, objective, transparent, and analytically rigorous insight.

Partner Across the Organization to Enable Insight-Driven Decisions
Act as a strategic partner to Product, Subscriber Management, Finance, Marketing, Industry Relations, Community Engagement, Technology, Operations, and Data Governance
Provide Product and Subscriber Management with insight on adoption, usage, lifecycle performance, acquisition, retention, churn, account health, sector performance, and growth potential.
Support Marketing, Product Marketing, Industry Relations, and Community Engagement with analysis of awareness, engagement, campaign effectiveness, market positioning, sector signals, and subscriber sentiment.
Align revenue and performance analytics with Finance while preserving Finance’s accountability for budgeting, forecasting, accounting, and financial controls.
·Promote a culture in which data, evidence, and insight consistently shape leadership discussions, priorities, and resource decisions.

Build and Lead a High-Performing Analytics Team
Define the team structure, roles, capabilities, workflows, service model, and operating rhythms required for a modern enterprise analytics function.
Coach analysts to progress from report production to insight generation, storytelling, analytical judgment, business partnership, and strategic advisory work.
Set clear objectives and quality standards, manage performance, allocate capacity to the highest-value work, and establish transparent intake and prioritization practices.
Create a high-performance culture grounded in curiosity, objectivity, experimentation, collaboration, accountability, and subscriber value.

Chez FTI Consulting, vous travaillerez aux côtés de leaders qui ont façonné l’histoire, en aidant à régler les plus grands défis qui font les manchettes aujourd’hui. Dès le premier jour, vous ferez partie intégrante d’une équipe focalisée où vous pourrez faire une vraie différence. Vous serez entouré d’une culture ouverte et collaborative qui souscrit à la diversité, à la reconnaissance, au perfectionnement professionnel, et de façon plus importante, à vous.

Êtes-vous prêt à faire votre différence ?

Français

À propos de FTI et du poste

Le groupe Financement corporatif et restructuration de FTI Consulting accompagne les entreprises, prêteurs, investisseurs, conseils d’administration, fonds de capital-investissement et autres parties prenantes dans la gestion de défis financiers, opérationnels et stratégiques complexes. Nos professionnels travaillent aux côtés des équipes de direction afin de répondre à des enjeux de liquidité, d’améliorer la performance, d’évaluer des solutions stratégiques et d’accompagner les organisations dans des périodes de transformation, de crise ou de changement. Le groupe Financement corporatif et restructuration de FTI offre des services couvrant le redressement et la restructuration, les transactions ainsi que les initiatives de transformation d'entreprise.

FTI Consulting est un cabinet-conseil de premier plan à l’échelle mondiale comptant plus de 8 000 professionnels et des bureaux dans les principaux marchés canadiens. Notre pratique de Montréal poursuit sa croissance et offre une occasion unique de joindre une équipe entrepreneuriale tout en bénéficiant des ressources, de l’expertise et des possibilités de carrière d’un leader mondial du secteur.

Nos équipes de mission sont volontairement de taille restreinte, permettant à chacun d’assumer rapidement des responsabilités importantes, d’interagir directement avec les clients et d’accélérer son développement professionnel dès le premier jour.

À titre de directeur(trice), vous jouerez un rôle clé auprès des entreprises et des parties prenantes confrontées à des situations financières et opérationnelles complexes, en dirigeant des mandats, en développant des relations de confiance avec les clients et en contribuant à la croissance continue de notre pratique.

Exemples de mandats récents

Gestion des liquidités et préparation de flux de trésorerie prévisionnels sur 13 semaines
Revues indépendantes des opérations de l’entreprise pour des prêteurs et investisseurs
Évaluations de la performance financière et opérationnelle
Mandats de redressement et de restructuration
Procédures en vertu de la Loi sur la faillite et l’insolvabilité (LFI) et de la Loi sur les arrangements avec les créanciers des compagnies (LACC)
Transactions de fusions et acquisitions en contexte de détresse financière et évaluations d’alternatives stratégiques
Mandats de conseil auprès des parties prenantes

Ce poste convient parfaitement aux candidats souhaitant mettre à profit leur expérience en restructuration, en finance corporative, en conseil auprès des parties prenantes et en gestion tout en jouant un rôle concret dans le développement d’une pratique en forte croissance.

Ce que vous ferez

À titre de directeur(trice), vous travaillerez directement avec des équipes de direction, des prêteurs, des investisseurs, des conseillers juridiques et des professionnels chevronnés de FTI sur des mandats auprès d’entreprises canadiennes et internationales évoluant dans divers secteurs d’activité. Vous serez impliqué dans des mandats complexes, superviserez leur exécution et contribuerez au développement continu de la pratique Financement corporatif et restructuration de FTI à Montréal.

Responsabilités principales

Superviser l’exécution quotidienne de mandats de restructuration, de redressement d’entreprise et de transactions, incluant des interactions avec les équipes de direction, les conseillers juridiques, les prêteurs, les investisseurs et les autres conseillers financiers
Mettre à profit vos compétences en affaires, en comptabilité, en finance et en analyse dans le cadre de divers mandats

Évaluer des plans d’affaires, des initiatives de restructuration, des alternatives stratégiques et d’importants volumes de données liés aux mandats
Réaliser des revues diligentes financières et d’autres analyses en appui à des mandats de restructuration, de refinancement ou de transaction

Préparer et réviser des rapports, des présentations et d’autres livrables destinés aux équipes de direction, prêteurs, investisseurs, conseils d’administration et autres parties prenantes
Collaborer étroitement avec les équipes de direction, les conseillers juridiques, les prêteurs, les investisseurs et les autres parties prenantes dans le cadre de processus de restructuration, de financement ou de transaction
Gérer les équipes de mission et offrir du mentorat, de l’encadrement et des opportunités de développement aux professionnels plus juniors
Contribuer aux initiatives de développement des affaires et à la croissance continue de la pratique de Financement corporatif et restructuration de Montréal

Titre professionnel CPA requis.
7+ années d’expérience pertinente au sein d’un cabinet de services professionnels, notamment en comptabilité publique, consultation, financement corporatif, services transactionnels ou dans un environnement similaire.

Capacité et volonté d’apprendre, de s’adapter et de réussir dans un environnement en constante évolution afin de répondre aux besoins des clients.

Bénéficier du mentorat de professionnels reconnus dans les domaines de la restructuration et de la finance corporative
Faire partie d’une culture entrepreneuriale, collaborative et stimulante soutenue par les ressources d’un cabinet mondial
Construire votre carrière au sein d’un cabinet reconnu mondialement comme un chef de file en financement corporatif, restructuration et services-conseils en redressement
