jobs.title: Vice President, Business Technology
jobs.description:
About Us
RJC Engineers is a well-established, employee-owned engineering firm with a broad geographic footprint and deep roots across Canada and the United States. We are leaders in structural engineering, building science, structural restoration, structural glass engineering, parking facility design, and building energy modelling. What sets us apart?
Our commitment to clients, cutting-edge technology, collaborative culture, and the passion of our people. We’re driven by a purpose: to positively impact our communities and invest in our team’s growth and success. At RJC, you’ll join an inclusive, fast-paced team tackling exciting and complex projects. You’ll work alongside industry-leading experts, explore emerging technologies, and be supported in your continuous professional development. Being an RJC Professional
We build our team around five key attributes:

Creative Mindset – You bring fresh ideas, challenge assumptions, and turn obstacles into opportunities.
Proactive Approach – You take initiative, anticipate challenges, and seek ways to create a positive impact.
Supportive Teamwork – You foster a culture of inclusivity, respect, and collaboration, helping others succeed.
Trusted Advisor – You act with integrity, expertise, and honesty, earning the confidence of clients and colleagues.
Lead with Purpose – You empower, support, and guide others, driving meaningful results.

Location:
Vancouver, Toronto, Edmonton or Calgary Compensation:
$190,000 – $220,000 The Opportunity
The Vice President, Business Technology is a strategic senior leadership role responsible for enabling organizational capability through technology, information, enterprise systems, and digital services. Reporting to an Executive Principal, and working closely with operational and function leaders across the organization, this role ensures RJC has the systems, infrastructure, information, governance, and technology capabilities necessary to support operational excellence, informed decision-making, effective collaboration, and sustainable growth. The leader in this role will serve as both a strategic advisor and operational leader, helping ensure that technology investments deliver meaningful business outcomes while supporting RJC's long-term vision. A critical component of this role will be the ongoing stewardship, optimization, governance, and evolution of RJC's enterprise business systems, including the firm's ERP platform. The successful candidate will help ensure these investments continue to strengthen business processes, improve data quality, enable organizational effectiveness, and support future growth. Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership

Develop and execute a Business Technology strategy aligned with RJC’s purpose, vision, and long-term priorities, ensuring technology investments strengthen operations, employee experience, client value, and measurable business outcomes.
Provide strategic leadership that builds a high-performing, innovative, service-focused team and strengthens connection across the organization.
Collaborate with business and functional leaders to champion organizational change and the responsible adoption of emerging technologies, including analytics, automation, and AI, that deliver positive business outcomes.

Governance, Risk, and Resilience

Establish and maintain a business technology governance framework, including policies, standards, and data governance practices, to ensure the integrity, security, accessibility, and regulatory compliance of organizational information and business systems.
Set direction for cybersecurity and infrastructure risk management, ensuring gaps are identified, prioritized, and addressed.
Direct business continuity, disaster recovery, and technology resilience planning to ensure uninterrupted operations and effective risk mitigation.

Business Partnership & Enterprise Systems

Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leaders, partnering across the organization to understand needs and translate them into scalable technology solutions that enhance productivity and support business objectives.
Provide executive-level leadership for RJC’s ERP platform and enterprise business systems, including governance, optimization, integration, reporting, and future evolution, ensuring systems, data, and knowledge management support effective processes, decision-making, collaboration, and growth.

Operational Oversight, Team & Stewardship

Oversee the delivery and performance of technology infrastructure, applications, and services, ensuring reliability, scalability, and an exceptional user experience.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators and service metrics to measure operational effectiveness, project outcomes, and team performance.
Oversee workforce planning, budgeting, forecasting, vendor and contract management, and financial stewardship to optimize the value of technology investments across the organization.

Professional Qualifications & Experience

15+ years of progressive leadership experience in business technology, enterprise systems, business operations, or related fields, including 6+ years leading enterprise technology functions and organizational change.
Proven experience overseeing ERP platforms and enterprise business applications through implementation, stabilization, optimization, governance, adoption, and continuous improvement.
Strong ability to align technology investments with business strategy, operational effectiveness, employee experience, client value, and measurable outcomes.
Deep understanding of cybersecurity, privacy, risk management, data governance, enterprise architecture, information management, and emerging technology enablement.
Exceptional leadership, communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into practical business decisions.
Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Information Systems, Business, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline; equivalent experience will be considered.

Why Join RJC?
This is an opportunity to help shape the future of one of Canada's leading employee-owned engineering firms. As Vice President, Business Technology, you will:

Play a key role in advancing RJC's Purpose, Promise, Vision, and long-term strategic priorities.
Provide leadership for one of the firm's most significant business transformation initiatives through the continued evolution of our ERP platform and enterprise business systems.
Help strengthen the technology, information, and knowledge capabilities that enable our people to do their best work.
Partner with leaders across the organization to improve collaboration, decision-making, innovation, and organizational effectiveness.
Contribute to the long-term success of an employee-owned organization committed to technical excellence, continuous learning, and meaningful impact.

What We Offer

Competitive compensation and performance-based bonus program.
Opportunity to participate in RJC's share ownership program.
Comprehensive benefits package, including Health Care Spending Account.
Maternity and Parental Leave Top-Up Program.
RRSP matching program.
A collaborative and supportive employee-owned culture.
Meaningful opportunities for professional growth and leadership development.

Attention Staffing & Recruitment Agencies:
RJC Engineers, will not pay fees for recruitment activities related to the hiring of a candidate unless a written service agreement has been established between a duly authorized representative of our Corporate Human Resources department and the recruitment/placement firm. In addition, to qualify for recruitment fees, all candidate resumes must be submitted to RJC Engineers, through our Corporate Human Resources department. Resumes and profiles sent to our managers without the express agreement of our Corporate Human Resources department will not be eligible for a fee

The role is designed for a senior client-facing transformation leader who can convert ambiguous business priorities into structured roadmaps, governed execution plans, and executive-ready decision materials.

You will lead strategy-to-execution initiatives spanning platform modernization, Engineering and Enterprise applications transformation, integration, release planning, adoption, and value realization.

Required Qualifications

Candidate must be located within commuting distance of Mississauga, Ontario or be willing to relocate to the area. This position may require travel.

Bachelor’s degree or foreign equivalent required from an accredited institution. Will also consider three years of progressive experience in the specialty in lieu of every year of education.

At least 11 years of Information Technology experience.

Candidates authorized to work for any employer in the Canada without employer-based visa sponsorship are welcome to apply. Infosys is unable to provide immigration sponsorship for this role at this time.

15+ years of experience in management consulting, technology consulting, large-scale digital transformation, enterprise platform modernization, program management, or related advisory and delivery leadership roles.

Strong understanding of enterprise application modernization, integration dependencies, workflow design, release management, testing, adoption, and governance.
Experience developing transformation roadmaps, delivery plans, risk dashboards, budget or financial views, executive briefs, and steering committee materials.

Strong communication, facilitation, issue-resolution, and executive presence in high-visibility client environments.

Bridge business stakeholders, solution architects, technical leads, delivery teams, QA, vendors, and executive sponsors to align requirements, dependencies, and delivery outcomes.

Establish governance rhythms, RAID management, release planning, change control, executive reporting, and financial tracking disciplines for large-scale technology-enabled programs.
Guide Agile, hybrid, and waterfall delivery approaches, including sprint planning, backlog governance, release coordination, UAT readiness, training, and cutover support.

Partner with implementation and delivery leaders to ensure modernization strategies translate into executable plans and measurable business outcomes.

Support business development, RFP responses, proposal shaping, oral presentations, and client solution storytelling for SDC-led transformation opportunities.
Develop reusable consulting methods, governance templates, roadmap structures, executive reporting assets, and delivery accelerators.
Contribute thought leadership on enterprise digital transformation, connected lifecycle modernization, platform-led operating model change, and advisory-led execution.
Mentor consultants and program teams on executive communication, program discipline, stakeholder management, and structured problem-solving.

Exposure to enterprise ecosystems such as ERP, PLM, MES, ALM, QMS, analytics, service lifecycle, or connected product / customer-operating platforms.
Experience in regulated or process-intensive industries such as financial services, healthcare, high-tech, industrial manufacturing, medical devices, aerospace, or automotive.

Experience contributing to pre-sales, proposal development, client presentations, account growth, pipeline reporting, or cross-sell initiatives.

jobs.description:
Title: Director of Transformation

Reports to: CEO

Location: Open to Candidates based in the United States or Canada

Imagine working at the forefront of innovation in fluid-flow technology, with over 1,400 colleagues across the globe, and contributing to a legacy of excellence that spans eight manufacturing facilities on four continents. Armstrong Fluid Technology is more than just a leader in our industry; we are a community of the brightest and most creative minds, driven by a shared mission to engineer the future and safeguard our planet.

As part of our team, you'll be immersed in an environment that fosters growth, creativity, and collaboration. Here, you'll have the opportunity to push boundaries, tackle exciting challenges, and develop cutting-edge solutions that promote energy efficiency and reduce environmental impact. Every day offers the chance to make a meaningful contribution to a more sustainable future, driving innovations that help lower global carbon footprints. Together, we’re creating a legacy that goes beyond business—one that’s changing the world for the better.

The Role

Reporting directly to the CEO, this role carries four critical mandates: transforming the CEO's vision into a high-performance roadmap, leading a PMO that ensures top-tier program delivery, maintaining a Business Operating System (BOS) that guarantees every organizational process is documented and followed, and driving continuous optimization of the company's ERP and enterprise systems to improve operational effectiveness.

Core Responsibilities

Strategic Planning

Vision-to-Action: Lead annual and quarterly planning cycles to translate high-level vision into actionable, department-specific goals.
Strategic Alignment: Ensure that every initiative across the company is vertically aligned with the CEO's primary mission and long-term strategy.

PMO Leadership & Program Performance

Performance Accountability: Direct the PMO to ensure all enterprise-wide programs are delivered on time and achieve their intended business impact.
Delivery Excellence: Establish health metrics and early-warning systems to identify and course-correct underperforming initiatives before they impact the bottom line.
Benefit Realization: Track and report whether programs deliver the strategic ROI committed during the planning phase.
Budget Discipline: Develop and manage program budgets, ensuring delivery within approved scope and financial parameters.

Business Operating System (BOS) & Process Governance

Process Architecture: Act as the custodian of the Company Playbook, ensuring every critical operating process is documented, standardized, and centrally maintained.
Standardization: Partner with department heads to eliminate tribal knowledge by converting core workflows into repeatable, scalable operating procedures.
Operational Adherence: Implement rigorous auditing and compliance mechanisms to ensure documented processes are consistently followed across the organization. To ensure the BOS remains a living system rather than a static manual, you will manage a structured process auditing cycle:
Quarterly Process Audits: Conduct formal reviews of high-risk and core revenue-generating processes every 90 days to verify compliance and identify bottlenecks.
Risk-Based Prioritization: Adjust audit frequency based on process criticality, with high-impact processes reviewed monthly where appropriate.
Corrective Action Tracking: Own follow-up activities for audit findings, ensuring corrective actions are implemented promptly and sustained.

Enterprise Systems, ERP & Digital Operations

ERP Governance: Own the operational effectiveness of the company's ERP ecosystem, ensuring it supports standardized business processes and strategic objectives.
Process & ERP Diagnosis: Regularly assess existing ERP configurations, workflows, integrations, and user adoption to identify inefficiencies, process gaps, and improvement opportunities.
ERP Optimization & Upgrades: Lead ERP enhancement initiatives, upgrades, and continuous improvement projects in partnership with IT and functional leaders, ensuring minimal disruption and maximum business value.
Business Process Integration: Ensure business processes and system capabilities remain aligned, recommending process redesign or system enhancements where required.
Digital Transformation: Champion enterprise-wide automation and digitalization initiatives that improve operational efficiency, data quality, reporting, and decision-making.
Data & Process Integrity: Establish governance around master data, process ownership, and system controls to improve operational accuracy and consistency across the organization.

Stakeholder Engagement & Communication

Executive Liaison: Act as the de-bottleneck between senior leadership and execution teams, ensuring quicker alignment and decision-making.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Facilitate coordination across functions, geographies, and business units.
Structured Communication: Establish regular reporting cadences including executive dashboards, status reports, KPI reviews, and governance forums.

Technical Proficiency Requirements

Program & Project Management (PPM): Expert-level experience with platforms such as Jira, Asana, monday.com, or Microsoft Project.
Business Process Management: Expertise in process mapping using Lucidchart, Miro, Microsoft Visio, or similar tools.
Knowledge Management: Proficiency with Confluence, Notion, or equivalent documentation platforms.
ERP & Enterprise Systems: Strong experience diagnosing, optimizing, implementing, or upgrading enterprise ERP platforms (e.g., Infor LN, SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, IFS, Epicor) and integrating them with business processes.
Business Intelligence: Experience with Power BI, Tableau, or similar analytics tools for operational reporting and KPI visualization.

Experience & Qualifications

10+ years of experience in Strategy, Operations, Management Consulting, Business Transformation, or Operational Excellence.
Proven track record of leading enterprise PMOs, process governance, ERP transformation, or operational excellence initiatives.
Demonstrated success driving cross-functional business transformation through process improvement and digital enablement.
PMP (Project Management Professional), PgMP, Lean Six Sigma, or equivalent certification highly preferred.

Travel

International travel of up to 50% of the time

Why Armstrong Fluid Technology?

By joining us, you’ll become part of a global community dedicated to pushing the boundaries of fluid-flow technology while upholding Armstrong's commitment to sustainability. You’ll have endless opportunities to learn, grow, and make a significant impact on the world. Together, we'll build tomorrow’s solutions today.

jobs.description:
Nutrien is a leading provider of crop inputs and services, and our business results make a positive impact on the world. Our purpose, Feeding the Future , is the reason we come to work each day. We’re guided by our culture of care and our core values: We put safety first. We act with integrity. We are stronger together. We deliver with excellence.

Through the collective expertise of our nearly 26,000 employees, we operate a world-class network of production, distribution, and ag retail facilities. We efficiently serve growers' needs and strive to provide a more profitable, sustainable, and secure future for all stakeholders. Help us raise the expectation of what an agriculture company can be and grow your career with Nutrien.

Nutrien is looking for a Director, Data Governance to build and lead our enterprise data governance program—strengthening data ownership, quality, and controls across key data domains so Nutrien can confidently scale analytics, AI, and digital products. Reporting to the Sr Director, Data Office, you will partner across business, technology, and risk functions to set standards, enable adoption, and ensure regulatory, and policy requirements are met globally.

This role will ensure critical data at Nutrien is trusted, consistent, and compliant across all data domains and business areas. You will operate at the intersection of business, data, technology, and risk—enabling scalable analytics, AI, and digital products globally—while ensuring regulatory and policy requirements are met and maintained.

What You'll Do:

Support the design and implementation of Nutrien’s global data governance framework across core data domains (e.g., product, customer, supplier, location, and asset)
Define enterprise standards for master/reference data domains and critical data elements
Drive the implementation of governance ownership and accountability across all data domains and lines of business, partnering with domain leaders to clarify roles, responsibilities, and adoption of governance practices
Balance enterprise consistency with business needs, regulatory requirements, and regional/functional nuances
Facilitate and support enterprise and business unit data governance forums (e.g., councils and working groups) ensuring alignment, issue escalation, and effective decision making
Drive continuous improvement of governance practices as the data and AI landscape evolves
Partner with IT and to define the enterprise data quality strategy, including standards, issue management, root-cause analysis, observability and remediation
Operationalize data governance policies and standards to ensure alignment with global and regional regulatory requirements (e.g., data privacy, residency, and confidentiality), working closely with Legal, Risk, and IT partners
Lead a team delivering master data maintenance for multiple data domains at Nutrien
Partner with Legal, Risk, and Compliance to support audits, client due diligence, and regulatory inquiries related to data and analytics
Lead data governance initiatives and change adoption efforts, influencing stakeholders and enabling consistent governance practices across domains and functions

What You'll Bring:

Bachelors Degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field
15+ years of experience in data governance, data management, master data, or related enterprise data roles
5+ years of experience in a managerial role with demonstrated executive-level influence and stakeholder management, including leading governance councils and driving adoption across a matrixed organization
Proven experience building and launching a data governance program from the ground up
Experience operating in a global, matrixed organization with regional regulatory complexity
Deep knowledge of data governance concepts, frameworks, and best practices (e.g., DAMA-DMBOK)
Practical experience with ERP systems (specifically SAP), data hierarchies, and how master data is created and managed within large enterprises
Experience collaborating across multiple business areas and centralized functions within a large enterprise
Proven people leadership experience, with the ability to build, mentor, and scale a high-performing team and stewardship community

What You'll Get:

Purpose-Driven Work
– Make an impact as part of a global team feeding the future and support farmers locally and around the world
Excellent Benefits
– Comprehensive medical, dental and vision coverage, plus a retirement program with generous employer matching for your future
Grow Your Career
– Tuition assistance for future education and ongoing learning and training opportunities for career advancement pathways across the organization
Support When it Matters
– Employee Assistance Programs, inclusive leaves, and paid time for holidays, volunteering, vacation, and wellness
Thrive in a Strong Culture
– Guided by our core values we put safety first, act with integrity, are stronger together, and deliver with excellence in a collaborative, high-performing environment

Ready to make an impact with us? Apply today!

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
About Sv Law

SV Law is a leading full-service law firm proudly serving Guelph, Elora, Waterloo, and the surrounding communities since the mid-1960s. With a team of over 50 lawyers and dedicated professional staff, the Firm provides trusted, practical legal counsel across a comprehensive range of practice areas — including services to both business and personal clients.

The Firm is consistently recognized as a leader across Southwestern Ontario, is home to multiple lawyers named among The Best Lawyers in Canada and has been recognized as a Top Employer, in Guelph, and across Southwestern Ontario, and Canada. The Firm is deeply rooted in its communities — supporting local organisations through fundraising, sponsorship, and volunteerism.

The Firm has experienced continued year-on-year growth. To support the next phase of growth it is seeking an experienced financial leader to serve as its first Chief Financial Officer (‘CFO’).

THE OPPORTUNITY

This is an exciting opportunity for a senior finance professional to step into a newly created, high-impact leadership role. Reporting directly to the Managing Partner and working alongside the Executive Committee and the Chief Administrative Officer, the CFO will be an integral member of the Firm’s senior leadership team — supporting ongoing growth by maintaining and enhancing the Firm’s enviable financial foundation and overseeing the Firm’s approach to technology / artificial intelligence.

The CFO will bring the financial discipline, strategic rigour, and professional services expertise that a fast-growing firm of this scale demands. This is a superb role for a candidate who combines strategic vision with hands-on execution, and who thrives at the intersection of finance, technology, and people.

Key Responsibilities

The CFO will provide leadership across the following areas:

Planning & Strategy – Work with the senior leadership team to balance financial stability with the need to transform the Firm’s systems and policies. Provide oversight and ongoing enhancement of the Firm’s finance and technology teams and systems. Build and maintain a network across the legal profession to ensure the Firm is aware of competitive trends and best practices.
Budgeting & Forecasting – Direct the planning and execution of the Firm’s annual budget cycle, with responsibility to ensure the Firm achieves its annual Profit targets. Reporting regularly to the Executive Committee and Partnership. Provide ongoing education to all lawyers on fee strategy and profitability.
Client & Finances – Develop and execute a plan to streamline the client intake process. Drive the ongoing improvement of financial hygiene process.
Lawyer Support – Automate and simplify financial processes to ensure that lawyers can primarily focus on client work. Work with the Partnership on the partner compensation cycle to align with the Firm’s strategy.
People & Culture – Serve as a senior leader across the Firm, promoting the development of a positive and proactive culture.

Qualifications & Experience

The ideal candidate will be:

CPA designation required with a minimum of five years leadership experience within a professional services firm — preferably within the legal industry.
Demonstrated ability to work both hands-on, personally delivering service, and strategically advising and guiding the partnership
Understanding of technology and the fast-changing digital environment, including experience with practice management, document management, and billing systems.
Familiarity with the Ontario legal market, Law Society of Ontario regulations, and the economics of law firm management — including partnership structures and lawyer compensation models.
Excellent people skills with a proven ability to build trust, influence and persuade partners, lead teams, and foster collaboration while driving change and adaptation across the Firm.
A superb sense of humour and a genuine willingness to work as part of a successful, collaborative, high-performing team.

What We Offer

Competitive Executive Compensation:

A total rewards package commensurate with the seniority and scope of the role, including a performance-based incentive component.

Comprehensive Benefits - Health, dental, vision, life insurance, and employee wellness programs.
RRSP Matching - A meaningful employer-matched RRSP program to support your long-term financial security.
Professional Development - Ongoing investment in leadership growth through continuing education, professional development, and industry engagement.
Work-Life Integration - A flexible working arrangement balancing the requirements of this senior role. The Firm highly values work / life integration.
Exceptional Culture - A collegial, community-minded environment where your contributions will be valued, recognised, and rewarded.

How To Apply

SV Law has retained Triline Consulting Inc. to conduct this executive search. Qualified candidates are invited to submit a cover letter and résumé in strict confidence to:

Paul Wilson

paul@trilineconsulting.ca

Application Deadline: October 18, 2026

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

SV Law is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified individuals, including those from equity-deserving communities.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) will provide strategic and operational leadership for the technology function of CapitalSage Vantage, ensuring that technology, digital platforms, products, infrastructure, data and cybersecurity capabilities effectively support the Company's business strategy and growth objectives.

The CTO will lead the development and execution of the Company's technology strategy, oversee technology architecture and engineering, drive product innovation and digital transformation, and ensure the reliability, scalability, security and performance of all technology platforms.

The role will work closely with the GCEO/GMD, business and functional leaders to translate business requirements into scalable technology solutions, strengthen technology governance, optimise technology investments and build a high-performing technology organisation.

Key Responsibilities

1. Technology Strategy & Leadership

Develop and execute a technology strategy aligned with CapitalSage Vantage's business objectives, growth plans and product roadmap.
Provide strategic technology leadership and advise Executive Management and the Board on technology opportunities, risks and investments.
Establish technology priorities, architecture principles, standards and governance frameworks.
Assess emerging technologies and determine their relevance and potential business value.
Drive continuous technology innovation and digital transformation across the business.

2. Product Engineering & Digital Platforms

Provide leadership for the design, development, deployment and continuous improvement of digital products and technology platforms.
Ensure technology solutions are scalable, reliable, user-centric and commercially viable.
Oversee the product engineering lifecycle from requirements definition through development, testing, deployment and post-production support.
Establish effective software development methodologies, engineering standards, code quality practices and release management processes.
Ensure appropriate integration of internal systems, third-party platforms, APIs and technology partners.
Drive automation and technology-enabled improvements to customer and operational processes.

3. Technology Architecture & Infrastructure

Own the Company's technology architecture and ensure that systems are scalable, resilient, secure and fit for purpose.
Oversee cloud infrastructure, networks, databases, enterprise applications, systems integration and technology operations.
Ensure high availability, performance monitoring, disaster recovery and business continuity capabilities.
Review and optimise technology infrastructure to support business growth and increasing transaction/user volumes.
Develop and maintain appropriate technology standards and documentation.

4. Cybersecurity, Data Protection & Technology Risk

Provide executive oversight of cybersecurity and information security in collaboration with the appropriate risk, compliance and security functions.
Ensure technology platforms are designed and operated in accordance with applicable security, privacy and regulatory requirements.
Oversee vulnerability management, penetration testing, security monitoring and remediation of technology risks.
Establish and maintain effective access management, data security, backup and recovery controls.
Ensure appropriate data protection and privacy-by-design practices are incorporated into technology and product development.
Support regulatory examinations, audits and technology risk assessments as required.

5. Data, Analytics & Technology Intelligence

Establish a technology and data architecture that supports reliable business intelligence and data-driven decision-making.
Promote effective use of data across products, operations, customer experience, risk and commercial functions.
Ensure appropriate data governance, quality, availability and security.
Leverage analytics, artificial intelligence and automation where they can create measurable business value.

6. Technology Operations & Service Delivery

Ensure stable, reliable and efficient day-to-day technology operations.
Establish appropriate service management, incident management, problem management and change management processes.
Monitor technology performance against agreed service levels and business requirements.
Ensure timely resolution of critical technology incidents and minimise business disruption.
Develop appropriate technology disaster recovery and business continuity arrangements.

7. Technology Governance, Budget & Vendor Management

Develop and manage the technology budget, ensuring optimal allocation of technology resources and investments.
Establish governance processes for technology projects, architecture, procurement and implementation.
Evaluate and manage technology vendors, consultants and strategic technology partners.
Lead technology procurement and contract negotiations in collaboration with Procurement, Finance and other relevant functions.
Monitor technology costs and identify opportunities for efficiency and optimisation.
Ensure appropriate documentation, controls and accountability across the technology function.

8. Technology Projects & Transformation

Lead major technology transformation and implementation projects from conception through delivery.
Establish clear project objectives, milestones, budgets, risks and success measures.
Ensure technology projects deliver agreed business outcomes and value.
Work with business stakeholders to manage requirements, priorities, dependencies and change adoption.
Ensure appropriate testing, deployment and post-implementation reviews.

9. Team Leadership & Capability Development

Build, lead and develop a high-performing technology organisation comprising engineering, infrastructure, product technology, data and other relevant technology capabilities.
Establish appropriate organisational structures, roles, performance expectations and succession plans.
Develop technical leadership capabilities and promote continuous learning and innovation.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, security, engineering excellence and customer focus.
Attract and retain high-calibre technology professionals.

10. Business Partnership & Innovation

Partner with Commercial, Product, Operations, Finance, Risk, Compliance, Customer Experience and other functions to identify technology-enabled opportunities.
Translate business challenges into practical and scalable technology solutions.
Support the development of new products, services, channels and revenue opportunities.
Continuously evaluate the customer journey and identify opportunities to improve digital experience through technology.
Represent CapitalSage Vantage in relevant technology, fintech and digital ecosystems.

11. Performance & Reporting

Establish and monitor appropriate technology performance metrics and service standards.
Provide regular reports to Executive Management on technology performance, projects, risks, costs, incidents and strategic initiatives.
Track technology investments against expected business outcomes.
Ensure technology priorities remain aligned with evolving business requirements.

Qualifications & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Engineering or a related discipline.
Master's degree or MBA is an advantage.
12–15 years of progressive experience in technology, with significant experience leading technology teams and enterprise-scale technology environments.
Demonstrated experience in a CTO, VP Engineering, Head of Technology, Director of Technology or comparable senior technology leadership role.
Strong experience in software engineering, digital platforms, cloud infrastructure, systems architecture and technology operations.
Experience within fintech, financial services, payments, digital financial products or technology-driven businesses is highly desirable.
Demonstrable experience taking digital products/platforms from development through deployment and scale.
Experience managing technology budgets, strategic vendors and complex technology projects.
Strong understanding of cybersecurity, information security, data protection and technology risk.
Experience working with APIs, system integrations, cloud technologies, databases and modern software development environments.
Relevant professional certifications in technology, cybersecurity, cloud, architecture or project management will be an advantage.

Digital Transformation

jobs.description:
Change the future with us.

We are looking for dedicated and talented people who solve ever-changing challenges, customer needs, and questions from colleagues with clever concepts and creativity. We embrace change and work with curious minds re-inventing the future of work. Join us and let us focus together on what’s truly important: making lives better with new ideas and the latest technology around the world.

About the role:
R&D Team Leader
- Agentic AI

Are you an entrepreneurial technology leader with a passion for building high-performing R&D teams and turning advanced AI concepts into scalable industrial platforms?

We are seeking an outstanding R&D Team Leader
to join Siemens Digital Industries Operations Software
, to lead an Agentic AI
team, based in Kitchener, Ontario – shipping real agent capabilities fast, while staying tightly aligned with the shared platform architecture and standards set across the program.

In this leadership role, you will lead and build the Canada’s Agentic AI team, and drive the development of secure, scalable, customer-ready platforms and shape the future of industrial AI.

Siemens Digital Industries Operations Software
is a suite of integrated digital solutions to engineer, simulate and operate manufacturing operations across industries. Operations Software includes our product portfolio in manufacturing engineering (COMOS, Tecnomatix, NX CAM, ...) & production operations (Win CC, Scada, PCS 7 / neo, Opcenter, Insights Hub, ...). The portfolio helps organizations across many different industries to improve operational efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance decision-making by providing real-time visibility and control across manufacturing and business processes.

Formula 1 cars, ships, mobile phones, space exploration vehicles, food & beverages, pharmaceuticals and many of the other objects we see in our daily lives are being conceived and produced using our software.

We're redefining the industrial world using data and AI to make production: Agile, Adaptive, Autonomous. Eliminate productivity boundaries for today’s and tomorrow’s production operation. Join our mission to build the most comprehensive next generation AI-native Industrial Operations Software portfolio as the new operation system for industry in the age of AI. With us you have the chance to now apply AI to where it really matters: In the physical world of an industrial production and engineering of real things.

As part of Siemens Operations Software (OPS-SW), the Technology, Data Fabric & Agentic AI organization provides the technology foundation that enables the next generation of industrial software. Its portfolio includes AI Production & Engineering Systems, Data Fabric, Agentic AI frameworks, connectivity platforms, semantic data models, cloud-native architectures, and industrial AI services that power autonomous, scalable, and intelligent operations across the OPS-SW portfolio.

What will you do?

Lead and grow the team – recruit, manage, and develop a team of AI/ML engineers and developers; own delivery, team health, and performance
Ship agent capabilities – drive the design, build, and delivery of specific agent capabilities from prototype to production-ready features
Deliver against the system – build on the shared frameworks, APIs, and orchestration patterns defined by the R&D Leader; contribute back improvements rather than diverging
Stay aligned, move fast – translate the global platform roadmap into a local team backlog and remove blockers so the team ships without waiting on the wider program
Stay hands-on – participate in architecture discussions, review code and technical designs, and make sound day-to-day technical decisions with your team
Own quality and reliability – ensure your team's work meets shared standards for agent communication, data handling, error recovery, monitoring, and observability
Bridge research and production – help your team apply modern AI research (LLMs, agent frameworks, orchestration patterns) to reliable industrial systems
Collaborate across sites – work closely with the Global R&D Leader, Project Leads, and peer teams (Erlangen, Fürth, and beyond) to keep one coherent system, not disconnected experiments
Represent the team locally – act as the technical and people anchor for the Canadian team; connect with local talent, partners, and the wider Siemens network, with opportunities to extend leadership influence across other Canadian R&D teams.

What you will bring:

Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Robotics, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, Automation Engineering, or a related field.
8+ years of experience in Engineering Management, Technical Leadership, or Team Leadership roles in software, AI, robotics, industrial technology, or platform engineering.
Lead engineering teams – you've managed and grown software/ML teams that ship, and you know how to balance delivery pressure with sustainable team health
Have strong technical depth – you understand LLMs and what makes agentic AI different from traditional automation; you can engage credibly in architecture and code-level discussions
Deliver in fast environments – you're comfortable with ambiguity and rapid iteration, and you can create structure and predictability for your team where there is none
Build on shared foundations – you know how to align to a common platform and standards without letting your team become a bottleneck or a silo
Lead through technical credibility – engineers respect you because you understand the work and make trade-offs they trust
Balance innovation and pragmatism – you know when to try cutting-edge tools and when to pick boring, proven technology
Communicate across audiences – you can align your team, report up to leadership, and coordinate across distributed sites and time zones

What sets you apart:

Experience building agentic AI systems, multi-agent frameworks, or LLM-based orchestration platforms
Background in industrial automation, manufacturing systems, or industrial IoT
Track record delivering 0-to-1 products that scaled
Deep hands-on expertise in Python, distributed systems, cloud platforms, and modern AI/ML tooling
Experience with open-source AI frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, Nemo Platform, etc.) and a clear view of their strengths and limitations
Previous leadership roles in R&D, platform engineering, or technical team management

Why you’ll love working for Siemens!

Join our Digital World

At Siemens Digital Industries Operations Software, flexibility is how we work – hybrid, built on trust and autonomy. We build technology that shapes the real world. You'll grow through real projects, strong technical peers, and global mobility, backed by the scale and benefits of an industrial operations software leader. We're committed to equality and inclusion, and we hire based on merit, skills, and impact. Bring your curiosity and creativity and help us shape tomorrow!

—comprising Klick Health (including Klick Katalyst and btwelve), Klick Media Group, Klick Applied Sciences (including Klick Labs), Klick Consulting, and Klick Ventures—is an ecosystem dedicated to realizing the full potential of our people and clients in life sciences. Founded in 1997, we have offices in New York, Philadelphia, Saratoga Springs, Toronto, London, São Paulo, and Singapore. Consistently named a Best Managed Company, Most Admired Corporate Culture, and Great Place to Work, Klick is committed to fostering a high-performance, people-first culture with creativity, collaboration, innovation, and impact across everything we do.

About Our Technology Craft

Our Technology Craft powers Klick’s innovation through platforms, products, and emerging technologies. This craft enables scale, efficiency, and experimentation across the business. Technology teams transform ideas into functional, future-ready solutions. Their work supports both client delivery and internal growth.

Job Description

The Senior Director, Digital Experience Platforms is a senior technical leader responsible for the delivery, quality, and strategic direction of digital experience and platform solutions across a portfolio of client engagements. The role serves as a senior technology advisor to client stakeholders while leading architects, developers, and technical specialists across CMS, analytics, DAM, personalization, experimentation, and AI-enabled capabilities. The role partners with Client Services, Technical Engagement Leads, Project Management, Analytics, and other technical teams to connect technical execution with measurable client outcomes.

What You’ll Do

Lead technical direction and delivery across client engagements, overseeing architecture, quality, scope, timelines, budgets, and resolution of complex platform and delivery issues.
Design, review, and approve architectures across Contentful, AEM, WordPress, Drupal, DAM platforms, analytics solutions, personalization tools, and associated integrations.
Define and implement digital measurement, personalization, experimentation, and DAM frameworks using tools such as Google Tag Manager, Adobe Launch, Google Analytics 4, Adobe Analytics, Adobe Target, Optimizely, Bynder, and AEM Assets.
Drive adoption of AI tooling, automation, coding assistants, and AI-enabled digital experience capabilities to improve delivery efficiency, platform functionality, and client outcomes.
Lead technical discovery, requirements definition, solution scoping, client presentations, and strategic recommendations while partnering with director-level and executive client stakeholders.

Qualifications

Required:

8+ years of progressive experience in marketing technology, software development, or digital platform delivery, including 3+ years leading technical teams, with responsibility for delivery, architecture, or people management.
Hands-on experience with enterprise CMS platforms including Contentful and AEM, with demonstrated delivery of production digital experiences and platform integrations.
Experience leading and mentoring technical teams across onshore and offshore delivery models, including workload distribution, capacity planning, performance management, and career development.
Experience designing and implementing enterprise digital measurement solutions using tag management, event-based tracking, data layers, consent-compliant analytics, and platforms such as Google Analytics 4 or Adobe Analytics.
Experience with enterprise DAM, personalization, and experimentation platforms, including metadata governance, workflow configuration, audience targeting, A/B or multivariate testing, and integrations with CMS, CDP, CRM, or marketing technology platforms.
Experience delivering client-facing technology programs in an agency or consulting environment using Agile/Scrum or comparable SDLC methodologies, including requirements, scope, technical recommendations, and executive-level communication.

Desired:

Comfort and enthusiasm for using AI as a regular part of how work gets done.
Experience supporting technology programs within pharmaceutical, biotech, healthcare, or life sciences agency environments.
Experience integrating AI-powered capabilities such as semantic search, content recommendations, generative personalization, or AI-enabled content workflows into production digital experience platforms.
Experience with AI-assisted development tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or equivalent, with examples of improved engineering workflows or delivery efficiency.
Experience advising clients on platform-native AI capabilities across Contentful, AEM, Optimizely, or related MarTech platforms.
Experience contributing to business development through SOW development, technical proposal reviews, capability presentations, or client growth initiatives.

Additional Information

This posting is for an existing vacancy at Klick. The final amount offered will be determined based on several factors such as a candidate's work location, their unique skill set, education, and prior work experience.

Purpose. Performance. People.

Joining CPP Investments means joining one of the world’s most admired and respected institutional investors to drive a single mandate: to deliver strong, sustainable returns for generations of Canadians.

With a long-term horizon and global reach, we deploy capital at scale across public and private markets. Our size, stability, and disciplined investment philosophy allow us to pursue complex opportunities and build enduring partnerships worldwide.

For our people, this means meaningful work with tangible impact, real opportunity, and collaboration with exceptional colleagues who value partnership and performance. Here, you’ll contribute to outcomes that matter alongside team members committed to excellence and shared success.

The Role

The Director, Security Architecture & Engineering will provide strategic and technical leadership for CPP Investments' security architecture and engineering function. Reporting to the Managing Director, Security Architecture & Engineering, you will lead the development of enterprise security architecture, cloud security strategy, and security engineering capabilities while partnering across the organization to embed security into technology delivery and operations. You will build and mentor a high-performing team, drive innovation, and help strengthen CPP Investments' overall cybersecurity posture

The Team

Technology & Operations enables CPP Investments to deliver on its global investment mandate through secure, resilient, and innovative technology capabilities. The department partners across the organization to provide scalable platforms, modern infrastructure, and cybersecurity capabilities that protect the organization while supporting business growth.

The Security Architecture & Engineering team is responsible for establishing enterprise security architecture standards, advancing security engineering capabilities, and embedding security by design across technology platforms. The team works closely with technology and business partners to deliver secure, resilient solutions that effectively manage cyber risk.

Accountabilities

Provide strategic leadership, direction, and mentorship to the Security Architecture & Engineering team while helping shape and execute the organization's long-term cybersecurity strategy.
Lead the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of enterprise security architecture, ensuring alignment with business objectives, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.
Develop and execute the organization's cloud security strategy, strengthening the security, scalability, and resilience of cloud environments.
Evaluate emerging cybersecurity technologies, trends, and standards, driving the adoption of innovative solutions that align with the organization's risk appetite.
Lead security architecture reviews and risk assessments, providing expert guidance and actionable recommendations to stakeholders.
Partner with technology, operations, and business teams to embed security-by-design principles throughout the technology lifecycle and effectively communicate security strategies and risks to diverse audiences.
Oversee the design and implementation of security platforms, automation capabilities, and engineering solutions that enhance operational effectiveness and strengthen the organization's security posture.

What You Bring

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Security, or a related discipline.
CISSP, CISM, CCSP, or an equivalent industry certification.
Minimum of 15 years of experience in security architecture, security engineering, or a related cybersecurity discipline.
Minimum of 4 years of people leadership experience leading security architecture or security engineering teams.
Demonstrated expertise in enterprise security architecture, cloud security, security engineering, risk assessment, and security technologies within complex organizations; experience in Canadian financial services is considered an asset.
Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence technical and business audiences.
Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and collaboration skills, with a commitment to continuous learning and staying current with evolving cybersecurity trends.

You are motivated to contribute to something larger than yourself, approach complex challenges with rigor, and hold yourself to high standards in a collaborative, performance-driven environment.

We provide colleagues with cutting-edge AI tools, dedicated learning time, and practical support to help them deliver with greater impact.

Simon Fraser University is a leading research university, advancing an inclusive and sustainable future. Our purpose – the essence of SFU – is to create and connect knowledge, learning and community for deeper understanding and meaningful impact. We are committed to fostering excellence, innovation, belonging and community in all that we do.

The Office of Institutional Research and Planning (IRP) supports university planning and decision-making through the collection, analysis and interpretation of institutional data. The team provides reporting, projections and analysis related to enrolment planning, academic planning and performance measurement. IRP also supports university-wide data governance, survey and research initiatives, and institutional reporting to senior administration, Senate, the Board of Governors and government. The office works closely with Faculties, academic departments and administrative units, senior leaders and external partners to provide reliable information that supports planning and informed decision-making across SFU.

About The Role

The Executive Director, Institutional Research and Planning is responsible for directing the University’s Office of Institutional Research and Planning, providing data analyses and modeling for the University’s strategic planning, and contributing to the evaluation and development of institutional policy by identifying issues, analyzing trends and projecting outcomes to support and inform policy decisions by the University’s senior administration. The Executive Director designs and oversees the collection, analysis and interpretation of data and the dissemination of reports, proposals and recommendations necessary to support institutional enrollment management and planning, academic planning, academic budget allocations and space planning. The role represents the Vice-President, Academic both within the University community and to external constituencies.

Qualifications

Master's degree and a minimum of ten years of experience in institutional research or a cognate area within a university environment, or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.

Excellent knowledge of research methodologies and survey techniques; statistical methods; data collection, reduction and analysis techniques.
Superior quantitative, qualitative, analytical and problem-solving skills; computer systems and programming skills.
Excellent leadership, operational management, supervisory, team building and mentoring skills.
Excellent strategic planning and project management skills.
Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with a broad range of people including clerical, professional, management, and executive personnel both within and outside the University.

Prorated for part-time employees

jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Director, AI Center of Excellence (CoE) is the technical and strategic leader of Future Electronics’ enterprise AI capability. This role sets AI strategy, builds and leads a team of AI specialists, and establishes the standards, tools, and governance that let AI and automation be adopted safely and effectively across the business.
This is fundamentally a hands-on AI leadership role. The ideal candidate has deep, current expertise in applied AI and automation and has personally built or led the delivery of real AI-powered solutions — not just directed others to. The Director works closely with AI Business Partners embedded in operational functions (Customer Service, Purchasing, Accounting, Finance, Marketing, and others) to turn business opportunities into working solutions, owning the technical direction, delivery standards, and team that make that possible.

Key Responsibilities

AI Strategy & Roadmap

Define and evolve the enterprise AI strategy and multi-year roadmap.
Evaluate emerging AI and automation technologies and assess their fit for the business.
Prioritize AI initiatives based on business value, feasibility, and risk.

Center of Excellence Leadership

Build, lead, and grow a team of AI specialists / automation engineers.
Set technical standards, delivery methodology, and reusable frameworks so solutions scale across functions instead of being rebuilt each time.
Coach and mentor the team, staying close enough to the technology to make real technical calls, not just review them.

Enabling the Embedded AI Business Partners

Act as the technical backbone for AI Business Partners embedded in operational teams — providing tools, playbooks, training, and hands-on support.
Translate business opportunities surfaced by embedded partners into scoped, deliverable AI/automation solutions.
Drive reuse and consistency across functions rather than each team building in isolation.

Governance & Responsible AI

Establish governance frameworks for AI development, deployment, and monitoring.
Ensure compliance with data privacy, cybersecurity, and regulatory requirements, in partnership with IT and Legal.
Promote responsible AI practices and manage associated risk.

Value Realization

Define KPIs and success metrics for CoE-led initiatives.
Track and report productivity gains, cost reductions, and business impact to executive leadership.
Build the business case for continued and future AI investment.

Qualifications

Required

Deep, demonstrated expertise in applied AI — generative AI, machine learning, or intelligent automation —
with a track record of building or leading the delivery of real AI/automation solutions. This is the single most important qualification for this role.
5+ years of hands-on experience in AI, automation, or applied data science, including recent, current experience with generative AI / LLM-based tools.
Experience leading or mentoring a technical team — as a people manager or as a senior technical lead.
Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical business stakeholders and executives.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred

Experience with enterprise AI/automation platforms (e.g., Azure AI Services, OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot Studio, Power Platform, Power Automate, Microsoft Fabric, Logic Apps) or equivalents.
Experience in distribution, manufacturing, supply chain, or another global operations environment.
Experience establishing an AI or automation function from the ground up.

Leadership Competencies

AI & Technical Fluency

Stays current with the fast-moving AI landscape and can personally evaluate new tools and techniques.
Translates emerging AI capability into practical, scoped business solutions.

Strategic Thinking

Builds a roadmap that balances near-term wins with long-term capability building.
Connects AI investment to measurable business outcomes.

Team Building

Attracts, develops, and retains strong technical talent.
Creates a culture where engineers can move fast without losing rigor.

Communication & Influence

Builds credibility with both engineers and executives.
Makes the business case for AI investment clearly and convincingly.

Pragmatic Delivery

Biases toward shipping working solutions over long theoretical exercises.
Balances innovation with a relentless focus on business value.

Why join us

At Future Electronics, we mean it when we say we care about our employees. Our approach to employee wellness is holistic, which is why alongside competitive salaries, and premium health and dental benefits, corporate employees have access to:

● Onsite gym and fitness studio with scheduled group classes - think yoga, aerobics

● Onsite medical clinic

Future Electronics is taking a hybrid approach to work. We value collaboration and working together, which our offices facilitate, combined with working remotely.

The role ensures advisor platforms effectively support business objectives, advisor productivity, operational efficiency, regulatory requirements, and client experience expectations.

Acting as the primary liaison between advisors, operations, compliance, technology teams, and external vendors, the VP establishes business priorities, governs platform enhancements, manages vendor relationships, oversees platform performance, and drives platform evolution. Key responsibilities include:

Advisor Platform Strategy & Governance
Own the overall business strategy, roadmap, and success metrics for existing advisor and client technology platforms.
Works closely with Technology’s Product Owner and Business leaders (Operations, Compliance, Finance, IT, Regional teams) to identify future needs and pain points to drive improvements/enhancements with the vendors.
Define business requirements for enhancements, integrations, and upgrades that support firm and advisor growth.
Ensure consistency in processes and digital experiences across the advisor ecosystem.
Balance advisor experience, operational efficiency, risk management, and business growth objectives.
Track ROI and adoption metrics to demonstrate business impact.

Vendor Relationship & Service Governance
Own strategic relationships with advisor and client platform vendors.
Lead vendor governance forums, service reviews, and escalation management.
Monitor vendor service performance and operational commitments.
Influence vendor roadmaps and advocate for firm priorities.
Coordinate issue resolution and ongoing vendor accountability.

Platform Lifecycle Management
Govern the ongoing evolution of advisor platforms.
Establish intake and prioritization processes for platform enhancements.
Assess and prioritize business improvements, operational changes, and advisor requests.
Evaluate platform capabilities and identify opportunities to improve advisor experience and business outcomes.
Oversee implementation readiness for new platform capabilities and functionality.
Ensure platform priorities align with strategic business objectives.

Platform Configuration & Access Governance
Establish governance for platform configurations, workflows, and business rules.
Oversee entitlements, user access frameworks, and permission structures.
Maintain platform documentation and standards.
Partner with Compliance, Operations and Technology teams to ensure appropriate controls are maintained.
Establish intake and prioritization processes for platform enhancements.

Production Issue & Enhancement Governance
Act as the business escalation point for platform-related issues.
Oversee governance and prioritization of production issues and platform enhancements.
Coordinate business impact assessments for platform incidents or operational issues.
Ensure issues are communicated effectively to stakeholders and advisors.
Track recurring issues, trends, advisor impacts, and improvement opportunities.
Maintain visibility of platform risks and remediation activities

Integration Oversight
Define and maintain clear business requirements and priorities for integrations across advisor and client technology systems.
Represent the business perspective in integration planning, ensuring solutions enable efficient advisor workflows and client experiences.
Partner with IT and Data teams to ensure that execution aligns with business intent and that integration outcomes support firm goals.

User Experience, Adoption & Communication
Partner with the Training and Advisor Enablement teams to drive adoption and effective use of advisor platforms.
Provide business direction, messaging, and prioritization for training and communications related to platform updates.
Collaborate on the development of user guides, FAQs, and onboarding materials to simplify platform engagement.
Capture advisor feedback and partner with Training to translate insights into business-driven platform enhancements.

Compliance & Risk Alignment
Ensure all platforms and workflows comply with internal policies, data privacy, and regulatory requirements.
Support the firm’s risk management objectives by embedding controls within platform processes.
Partner with Compliance and Risk teams to conduct periodic audits and strengthen governance.

Performing other duties and projects, as assigned.

The ideal candidate will possess:

A minimum of 5 years’ experience managing advisor or client technology ecosystems in financial services.
A degree in Business, Information Systems, or related field required.
PM designation is an asset.
CSC and/or CIRE exam completion preferred.
Proven experience in vendor management, governance, and strategic platform ownership.
Demonstrated success in driving adoption, process improvement, and business enablement through technology.
Familiarity with service management tools such as Jira, ServiceNow, or Zendesk
Proficiency with the MSOffice suite, including Word, Excel, Powerpoint, Teams, and Outlook.
Exceptional stakeholder and vendor management skills.
Strong problem-solving and analytical capabilities.
Skilled in communicating complex concepts to non-technical audiences.
Collaborative and highly organized, with a bias toward action and accountability.
Business-level understanding of APIs, integrations, and SSO concepts.
Experience managing platform configuration and release testing.
Demonstrate a high level of accountability, reliability, adaptability, and innovation in accomplishing day to day work and long-term goals.
An excellent attention to detail.
Exemplary interpersonal and influencing skills; an ability to communicate effectively and work collaboratively, across multiple mediums (in-person, over the phone, and virtually).
Strong organizational skills.
A high tolerance for ambiguity; highly adaptive and able to manage a large volume of competing priorities.
Strong critical thinking and written and verbal communication skills.

jobs.description:
Position Title

Director, People and Culture Strategy

Employment Type

Permanent

Existing Vacancy

Yes

Division/Branch

People and Culture Division / People and Culture Strategy

Application Deadline

September 25, 2026

Pay Level

13

Pay Range

$149,307 to $186,631

Work Location:

Head Office, Toronto, ON; (In-Office)

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO)
is an agency where innovation thrives, ideas flourish, and passion drives us to new heights of excellence. Reporting to the Ministry of the Attorney General, the AGCO is responsible for regulating Ontario’s vibrant alcohol, gaming, horse racing, and private retail cannabis sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is seeking a strategic, collaborative and forward-thinking leader to serve as Director, People and Culture Strategy. Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer (CHRO), the Director People and Culture Strategy provides enterprise leadership for People and Culture strategy, transformation and modernization, with responsibility for advancing the People Strategic Plan, divisional priorities, enterprise metrics and executive reporting, HR digital enablement, responsible AI adoption, diversity, inclusion and accessibility (DI&A), inclusive leadership and high-performing team leadership.

This role translates enterprise and divisional priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, implementation plans, performance measures and governance mechanisms that strengthen organizational readiness, workforce planning, evidence-based decision-making and measurable impact across AGCO.

The ideal candidate is a trusted strategic advisor who brings strong judgment, systems thinking and a collaborative leadership style. They are comfortable operating in a complex public-sector environment, balancing long-term transformation with immediate operational priorities, and translating data, risk, workforce trends and stakeholder needs into practical, inclusive and measurable people strategies.

If you are motivated by the opportunity to lead strategic HR transformation, advance responsible digital and AI adoption, strengthen diversity, inclusion and accessibility, and support a strong employee experience, this role offers a meaningful platform to make a lasting enterprise-wide contribution at AGCO.

What You Will Do

Lead the development, implementation and ongoing refresh of AGCO’s People Strategic Plan, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities, government mandates, workforce risks and evolving organizational needs.
Translate organizational priorities into actionable people strategies, roadmaps, initiatives, performance measures and implementation plans.
Oversee the planning, prioritization and delivery of People and Culture initiatives, projects and divisional priorities that advance organizational goals.
Establish planning, governance, reporting and accountability mechanisms to monitor progress against strategic commitments and demonstrate measurable impact.
Provide strategic advice to the CHRO, C-Suite, senior leaders and governance committees on HR priorities, workforce implications, transformation risks and organizational readiness.
Design and oversee enterprise People and Culture performance indicators, dashboards, workforce analytics and executive reporting to support transparency, accountability and evidence-informed decision-making.
Lead HR digital enablement and responsible AI adoption by developing practical capability, governance practices and high-value use cases that improve service quality, efficiency and decision-making.
Provide enterprise leadership for DI&A strategy, accessibility and inclusive leadership, embedding inclusion principles into AGCO culture, operations and people practices.
Lead the refresh, implementation and evaluation of enterprise DI&A strategy, including the development and reporting of meaningful performance measures.
Act as a senior subject matter expert on DI&A and accessibility, advising executives and senior leaders on inclusive talent practices, cultural transformation and emerging obligations.
Provide leadership and direction to a team by setting clear expectations, prioritizing deliverables, supporting development and fostering a culture of inclusion, accountability, learning and high

You Have

Post-secondary education in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Organizational Psychology, Adult Education, Strategic Planning, Leadership, Human Rights, Public Policy or a related field, or equivalent work experience; a master’s degree is considered an asset.
Minimum of 8 years progressive leadership experience in strategic planning, organizational transformation, HR strategy, performance measurement, workforce analytics, DI&A, accessibility, digital enablement and/or related areas.
Demonstrated ability to translate enterprise priorities into practical strategies, roadmaps, governance structures, implementation plans and measurable outcomes.
Strong understanding of HR digital adoption, HRIS-enabled process improvement, workflow automation, workforce analytics, digital service delivery, change management and responsible AI use.
Knowledge of HR data governance, privacy, accessibility, security, records management and ethical use of workforce information.
Experience developing executive-level reports, dashboards, briefings and presentations that translate complex information into clear insights and recommendations.
Strong consultation, facilitation, public speaking and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence and build alignment across senior leaders, governance bodies and cross-functional partners.
Demonstrated experience leading DI&A strategy, accessibility initiatives, inclusive leadership development, employee engagement forums, committees or enterprise-wide measurement frameworks.
Strong knowledge of Ontario legal and regulatory frameworks related to human rights, accessibility, employment standards and inclusive workplace practices.
Experience leading, coaching and developing teams in a complex, unionized and public-sector environment is an asset.
Eligibility to work in Canada and the ability to successfully complete a criminal background check.

To apply to this vacancy, please submit your application online at our Careers webpage located at Careers | Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario by September 25, 2026.
Please note that only applications submitted through the Applicant Tracking System will be accepted.

About The AGCO

The Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario (AGCO) is an Ontario provincial regulatory agency that reports to the Ministry of the Attorney General. We are responsible for regulating the alcohol, gaming, horse racing and cannabis retail sectors in accordance with the principles of honesty and integrity, and in the public interest.

The AGCO is proud to be recognized as one of Greater Toronto’s Top Employers for the second year in a row. This annual distinction reflects our commitment to cultivating a workplace environment that prioritizes employee well-being, emphasizing work-life balance, mental health resources, and opportunities for professional growth. We remain committed to fostering a supportive and rewarding work environment for our employees.

What We Offer

The AGCO provides a comprehensive range of benefits and programs (subject to eligibility), including:

Generous time-off policy, including 2 volunteer days to contribute to causes that matter to you.
Defined benefit pension plans to secure your financial future.
Comprehensive health, dental, and vision plans, with 100% employer-paid premiums.
Well-being credits to support gym memberships, therapy, financial planning, and more.
Employer-paid parental leave top-up.
Professional development opportunities with access to training programs, leadership resources, and reimbursement for professional memberships.
24/7 confidential support through our Employee Assistance Program.
Convenient, central location near the subway line for easy access when working in the office. Paid onsite parking is also available.

Please note that only applications submitted through the Applicant Tracking System will be accepted.

The AGCO is an inclusive and equal opportunity employer.

The AGCO has the responsibility to lead by example in advancing racial equity and to build a diverse, inclusive, accessible and respectful workplace where every employee has a voice and the opportunity to fully contribute. To this effect, you are encouraged to reflect upon the diversity you would bring to the role within your application including, but not limited to, individuals identifying with one or more of the under-represented groups identified within Ontario’s Human Rights Code. 

Disability related accommodation during the recruitment process is available upon request. Persons with disabilities who require accommodation during the application process, or who need job postings in an alternative format, may email their request to askhr@agco.ca. The subject line should read “Accommodation in Application – [Position Title].

We do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to screen, assess, or select applicants at any stage of the hiring process. All applications will be reviewed and evaluated by our Human Resources team and hiring managers.
